News.title: Horrifying moment elephant tramples rickshaw driver to death after knocking him to ground as he fed beast in street
News.content:
SHOCKING footage shows the moment a rickshaw driver was brutally trampled to death by an elephant on a crowded street.

Vijay Holkar, 49, was feeding the animal a lump of jaggery – a traditional Indian sweet treat – when he was suddenly knocked to the ground on July 25.



Footage shows the elephant turn on the driver in a busy street in Chandan Nagar, India, after its handler reportedly struck it on the head with a stick.

It is then seen wrapping its trunk around Vijay, thrusting him to the ground and stomping aggressively on his legs, back and abdomen.



The recording shows Vijay struggling to get back up as the elephant crushes him on the tarmac before eventually abandoning him.

The horror attack unfolded in front of a crowd of stunned onlookers near the Raj Nagar police station.



The elephant was reportedly being led through the city by a group of holy men who were collecting donations.

Vijay is understood to have approached the animal to feed it before disaster struck.



He was rushed to a state hospital with severe injuries and was later transferred to a private hospital, where he tragically died.

Witnesses in the area said the animal had appeared docile prior to the attack, which happened in a matter of seconds.

Tilak Karole, in charge of the Chandan Nagar police, said a post mortem examination revealed Vijay had died from serious internal bleeding.

Police say an investigation is now underway to establish whether permission had been acquired from forest officials to parade the elephant through a bustling, urban area.

The handler, known locally as Umesh Goswami, was subsequently arrested and accused of failing to keep the elephant under control.



Goswami has been booked under sections 106 and 291 of India’s Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita – the country’s criminal code covering death by negligence and unlawful conduct of an animal.

Elephants are regarded as sacred animals in many parts of India and are occasionally used by religious groups to collect donations.

The practice continues despite rising concerns from welfare campaigners over treatment of the animals.

The shocking attack follows another tragic incident in eastern India, whereby a herd of elephants trampled six people to death – including a three-month old baby.

News.title: My gran’s body was left to rot by rogue funeral boss & I was given stranger’s ashes – what he did to the dead is wicked
News.content:
WALKING his Maltipoo dogs at a National Trust park, undertaker Robert Bush appears without a care in the world – but this week faces jail after stashing dead bodies in fridges and mixing up ashes.

In exclusive pictures obtained by The Sun, he was seen on a long walk at Brimham Rocks in North Yorkshire ahead of a week-long sentencing hearing in which more than 200 victims are expected to give devastating impact statements.



Bush, 47, sympathised as grieving families said goodbye to their loved ones at his makeshift chapel at Legacy Independent Funeral Directors in Hull.

They believed their relatives would then be taken for cremation but in most cases the coffin was empty and the dead still stored inside fridges and cold rooms. Worse still, some families were given ashes that belonged to others.

In Britain’s most horrendous funeral home scandal, the callous conman even stole money donated by mourners for charities and sold funeral packages and burial plots that didn’t exist.



Tristan Essex, 27, told The Sun how his beloved grandmother Jessie Stockdale was placed in several different coffins, including one spattered with blood, after her death in November 2023.

Tristan said: “We thought my nana had been cremated, and instead she was being left to rot for four months.

“She brought me up and we were so close so I went to view her every day and she was being placed in different coffins.

“One had frills around the edge, but no plastic lining in it and she was basically lying on bare wood.

“Another had blood splashed on the frills and when I asked Robert about it he said he was very sorry but didn’t explain why.”



Tristan said he was given Jessie’s ashes in a ‘sweetie jar’ while waiting for an urn they ordered to arrive.

He said: “It was full to the brim and in retrospect, there must have been more than one person’s ashes in it.

“I bought scatter tubes so other members of the family could have some of her ashes. We obviously had no idea it wasn’t Jessie because her body was still at Legacy.

“I kept the ashes on my mantlepiece and was talking away to nana with no idea it was someone else. It’s sickening.”

Tristan, along with other families, is unhappy that Bush was the only person charged, but Humberside Police said he was the only one for whom the legal test for prosecution was met.



In April, Bush admitted 67 charges including the prevention of a lawful and decent burial, fraud, fraudulent trading and theft.

He was told by Judge Mr Justice Hilliard that he faces jail.

He was arrested in March 2024 on an incoming flight to Heathrow after enjoying a holiday in America.



Bush had debts of more than £50,000 but enjoyed a lavish lifestyle, living in a house in one of East Yorkshire’s most exclusive villages, Kirk Ella. He owned several motorbikes, a Land Rover and enjoyed days out racing around the country.

Karen Dry, whose parents’ funerals were handled by Bush and has become a spokesperson for families, said: “The idea that Bush did this because he got into financial trouble is rubbish.

“He was a man motivated by greed and didn’t care about those he was meant to give a dignified end. He is a wicked, wicked man.

“There were half a tonne of human ashes in that funeral home and some families will never find out if they were given the right remains.

“He hasn’t shown an ounce of remorse for what he’s done and didn’t even look at families during court cases. He’s an absolute pig.”



Michaela Baldwin said she was stunned by the size of her stepfather Danny Middleton’s coffin when the family held a service at the Hessle Road funeral home.

She said a relative even joked that Danny, who Michaela describes as a “large” man, couldn’t have squeezed into the coffin containing his body after his death in November 2023 when he was in his 70s.

Mum-of-two Michaela, 36, now knows that in reality, it was most likely an empty casket.



She said: “We were given ashes but they weren’t Danny’s and it’s likely we will never know whose remains we had because the heat of cremation means DNA isn’t available to test.

“Bush did this through pure greed. I heard he even had a home gym at the end of his garden.

“I don’t think he will ever apologise to the families involved. He’s so self-centred and I really believe this would still be going on now had he not got caught.”

Michaela has been left mystified as to why Bush was not remanded in custody after pleading guilty to his sick offences.



She said: “Apparently he wasn’t considered a flight risk and was being a good boy, checking in with police and doing everything he was told.

“But look at all the pain he’s caused the families. He’s out walking his dogs like nothing has happened while everyone has to live with what he’s done.”

Families are now calling for new regulations around funeral parlours.

Funeral directors do not need to register with any organisations, although there are two trade bodies. Apprentices need just five GCSEs to enter the profession.



Michaela said: “The truth is it’s easier to open a sandwich shop than it is to operate a funeral business. “

News.title: Fears Bordeaux will be reduced to ashes with ‘apocalyptic’ wildfire just 7 miles away as 250k evacuate & tourists banned
News.content:
RAGING wildfires are closing in on Bordeaux with mass evacuations continuing across France as officials battle the “apocalyptic” flames.

The rampant fires are now less than seven miles away from the ancient city with over 850,000 residents being warned Bordeaux is at risk of being reduced to ashes in the coming days.



Thick plumes of smoke are already looming over the city as concerns rapidly grow over the “erratic” fire whirlwinds sending the flames east across France.

Local official Sophie Brocas has urged holidaymakers to stay away and urged tourists already in the city to pack their bags and make plans to leave.





She said: “We urge tourists not to come to this region, at least until the situation is under control. I encourage tourists who are already here to consider another destination.”

Bordeaux sits in the direct path of the Gironde wildfire which has been scorching huge swathes of land as it continues to grow.



Sebastien Berge, head of the Gironde firefighters’ union, has now warned of major concerns for those still in Bordeaux.

He said: “When there’s a fire of this magnitude, it creates its own weather pattern… it’s difficult to monitor.

“When you see how far it’s spreading, I think we can now be concerned about the city of Bordeaux.”



Bordeaux, famed for its wine-making, is the sixth largest city in France based on its entire metropolitan area where over 850,000 people live.

Mayor Thomas Cazenave has urged that there are currently no plans to evacuate the city’s population as they hope to control the flames in the coming days.

Le Barp, a municipality less than 20 miles from Bordeaux, has already been ordered to evacuate immediately via the south.

Over 284,000 acres have been burned due to wildfires since the start of the year, according to French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez.

He told France 2 television that the country is now battling 30 to 40 wildfires every day.



President Emmanuel Macron is now due to convene a crisis meeting today with cabinet ministers to discuss the raging wildfires.

It comes after Gironde firefighting Chief Eric Brocardi compared the battle to contain the inferno as a “David-versus-Goliath scenario”.

Currently, 2,500 firefighters, 1,500 military personnel and around 1,200 police officers have been deployed to the Gironde region.



Officials say fire crews have been “overwhelmed” by the ferocity of the flames and remain “far from” bringing them under control.

Two people have died due to the wildfires so far with at least 75 injured.

Dozens of homes have been burnt to the ground with an estimated 220,000 people displaced and forced to live in shelters while the flames remain high.

Gironde authorities have now banned vacationers from entering the region by closing off several main roads and cancelling holiday camps for children and people with disabilities.

Some of the blazes in the Gironde wildfire are said to be so powerful they have now created a terrifying giant fire cloud which can create its own lightning.



The unprecedented “pyrocumulonimbus” is a dangerous weather system that whips flames around its own winds and can strike and ignite even more fires.

Wildfires have also engulfed huge parts of Spain in recent days.

A national emergency has been declared as firefighters fight against merging fires outside Madrid.



Spanish PM Pedro Sánchez conceded there were “complex times ahead”.

Three huge fires have all merged to the west of the Spanish capital, where around 77,000 people have been evacuated and another 28,000 locked down in their homes.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A man, believed to be in his 70s, was found dead in his car by firefighters as they extinguished a blaze in Valencia.



The major fire near Madrid was described over the weekend as being “at its peak” and “beyond the capacity” of firefighters to control.

News.title: How slaves are hidden in plain sight across the UK & the signs your local business is employing them as we join cop raid
News.content:
FRANTICALLY trying to get away from cops, a man launches himself over a spiked fence, which cuts open his inner thigh.

Police believe that he and several other men are working at a car wash illegally and might be victims of exploitation.



Officers are hot on his trail, and sirens can be heard as cars speed around the backroads to cut him off.

The man has fled a car wash seconds after spotting a group of police making their way en masse as he jet washes a grey Cupra Formentor.





He’s eventually found hiding in a shed in the hopes he won’t be questioned by immigration officials about his documents.

The man is one of eight staff believed to be illegally working at Central Auto Carwash in South Manchester. Police are now investigating if the men are being exploited or are victims of modern slavery.

All of them had to be chased down by cops as they fled in different directions.

The Sun joined the cops on two days of action across the city into organised immigration crime, and watched as the investigation got underway.



During questioning by Greater Manchester Police, the men claimed that they weren’t asked to show right-to-work documents and were required to wash cars eight hours a day, six days a week.

And chances are they’re in a pretty miserable situation outside of work, too. Most of the men are from Pakistan, and as they are working illegally, it is unlikely they are being paid minimum wage.

Detective Chief Inspector Abigail Cronin, head of GMP’s Modern Slavery and Organised Immigration Crime Unit, tells the Sun: “We find people sleeping in absolutely horrendous conditions. They don’t have a bed. There’s just a mat on the floor.

“There can be overcrowding in the houses, and they might not know where they are.

“Often they have one poor source of income, which isn’t what they were promised, and that can be in any capacity from car washes to nail salons.



“They don’t know a way out of their situation; they might be worried about contacting the police for help, or they have a family back home that they still need to support.

“Victims of organised immigration crime are stuck in their situation.

“These people come from all walks of life and will often end up in a situation they weren’t expecting to be in. Initially, they may not realise they are being exploited.

“Victims we’ve supported through long-scale complex investigations are traumatised, and you might not even realise that they are the person serving you in a shop or elsewhere.”

Many illegal workers are trafficked to the UK and given the promise of a better life, before being forced into modern slavery or, in the case of women, sex work.



Often gangs promise workers a better life in the UK with a good job and accommodation, but when they arrive it’s hard work for little pay, and they are made to live in overcrowded houses.

Then, once here, they can have their passports taken off them or threats of violence against their families back home used to control them.

Car washes are a well-known job where illegal workers are exploited, and this one is directly opposite a Manchester police station.

The cops have been tipped off that multiple men are working there illegally, leading them to make investigations for a few weeks before conducting a visit with trading standards.

Initially, they believe there are four men, one of whom is working despite having applied for asylum, but as they walk over the road, eight men in total run away.



Within seconds, screaming and sirens are heard as cars race to help catch the men, as officers on foot start running after the suspects.

Police are still considering if they will bring charges in relation to immigration offences.

Prices for a wash at the business start from £12, and a mini-valet from £25.

Charities warn that a wash costing any less than £5 means it’s likely being done by modern slaves.

Other signs of modern slavery according to charity Unseen include avoiding eye contact, rarely travelling alone and seem unfamiliar with the neighbourhood.



For establishments like nail bars, workers could be potential modern slavery victims if they seem to work long hours with no breaks, and appear to have a language barrier.

Detective Chief Superintendent John Griffith, of the Organised Immigration Crime Domestic Task Force, tells The Sun: “Immigration is a good thing as long as it’s controlled and safe.

“Organised crime can benefit from illegal immigration on our high streets, and individuals are being brought into this country so that they can be exploited.

“There is no doubt about that. People who are brought into the grey economy can end up working in service sector industries for low wages with no protection under employment law.

“By stopping organised immigration crime, we can prevent these criminal businesses from undercutting legitimate businesses employing people the correct way.



“Employing people for lower than minimum wage, or selling illegal commodities, are ways organised immigration crime is damaging our high street.



“This is not punitive, this is about improving our communities and educating those individuals at their running businesses, and ensuring they’re being regulated properly within the laws of the UK.”

The raids are part of a nationwide week of cracking down on organised immigration crime across 39 police forces under Operation Lockstream.

They are done in partnership with police, Immigration Enforcement, Trading Standards and HMRC, and others to ensure all risk areas are tackled.

Nationally, 911 businesses were visited by police and immigration officers, resulting in 362 arrests, £1million in cash seized and more than £700,000 worth of illicit tobacco, cigarettes and vapes confiscated.

Last year, The Sun on Sunday revealed car washes have been fined up to £3milion for hiring illegal workers by the government. Central Auto Car Wash was not one of them.



In November last year, a car wash owner in Mitcham, south London, was jailed for eight years and six months for exploiting and trafficking illegal workers from Romania.

Hewa Margai, 45, of Carshalton Road, Mitcham, was found guilty of eight counts of holding a person in slavery or servitude.

One of the men he’d brought over and forced to work was a 15-year-old boy. Cops discovered Margai’s victims were deprived of their basic human rights and routinely subjected to physical, mental and psychological abuse.

Management at Margai’s Mictcham car took documents from the eight men, leaving them trapped.

What Is Human Trafficking? Human trafficking involves the use of force, fraud, or coercion to obtain some type of labour or commercial sex act. Every year, millions of men, women, and children are trafficked worldwide – including right here in the UK. It can happen in any community and victims can be any age, race, gender, or nationality. Traffickers might use the following methods to lure victims into trafficking situations: Violence

Manipulation

False promises of well-paying jobs

Romantic relationships Language barriers, fear of their traffickers, and/or fear of law enforcement frequently keep victims from seeking help, making human trafficking a hidden crime. Traffickers look for people who are easy targets for a variety of reasons, including: Psychological or emotional vulnerability

Economic hardship

Lack of a social safety net

Natural disasters

Political instability. Source: Blue Campaign



It’s a common picture across the UK. In Carlisle, Cumbria, Defrim Paci, 42 and Sitar Ali, 33, were jailed in 2021 for a modern slavery ring related to their car wash.

Romanian workers were forced to work 11 hours a day, up to seven days a week and then paid just £20.

One man told the court how hot water had “eaten away at his feet” after working nine days in a row without correct equipment.



Another said: “I was treated like a piece of garbage by those running the place.”

It took police a four-year investigation to get the case to court and secure the conviction of the men.

It is not known if the men at the car wash in Manchester are modern slavery victims, but police believe they are, at the very least, being exploited.

Also on GMP’s list of targets are a variety of businesses, including takeaways, nail shops, barbers and more.

Nail salons often exploit Vietnamese nail technicians, as they arrive in the UK already trained from their home country. Car washes vary from having Pakistani to Eastern European men working for very little pay.



A rising hotspot for illegal workers being exploited and the sale of dangerous or illegal products is mini-markets.

Less than two miles away from the car wash is the cops’ next target – a mini market.

They’ve been told by locals that a shop on the Curry Mile – Wilmslow Road in Rusholme – has been forcing illegal migrants to work for him.

The bright purple shop is stacked to the brim with electronics, kids’ toys and sweets, making it difficult for the team of eight cops to squeeze in and search it.

During their inspection with trading standards, The Sun understands that several unlawful children’s squishy toys were seized alongside illicit tobacco and illegal vapes.



It’s believed that the sale of illicit tobacco costs the Treasury more than £1.7bn in lost tax revenue.

It was one of several mini-markets being targeted by the boys in blue over the intensification period on organised crime.

But for cops, the most important part of the day is helping protect people who are being exploited because they cannot legally work.

Organised Immigration Crime in stats Involvement from 39 police forces and 177 deployments across the UK

Visits to 911 businesses/premises by police and Immigration Enforcement.

Over 4,000 encounters with individuals at premises visited.

Over 1,000 vehicles stopped. 362 arrests made, of which 269 were immigration arrests.

57 immigration arrests of the 269 – 21%- entered the UK by small boat.

Over £1m in cash seized.

Over £700,000 (street value) of illegal tobacco, cigarettes and vapes seized.

73 civil penalty referral notices were issued to businesses, with a maximum possible penalty of £60,000 per illegal worker.

£131,000 (street value) of drugs seized.

92 cars and 31 e-bikes and scooters seized.



Detective Chief Inspector Chris Woodburn manages organised crime on a district level. He tells The Sun: “Often people are sold a false dream where they’re told they will be given employment in the UK, but when they arrive they are given work in cash businesses, such as car washes, and sometimes sexual exploitation in brothels.

“What we’re hoping is that we can go into these establishments and safeguard people, but also generate further intelligence, which means we’ll be able to continue to target these premises outside of the days of action.”

And Forced Labour Charity Unseen tells The Sun how vital it is for police to try and get the perpetrators of the exploitation.

Hilary Agg, head of policy and research at Unseen, says: “The survivors are the most important thing in modern slavery.

“To be able to pursue traffickers, a lot of the time, law enforcement need to be able to engage survivors to be able to build that trust so that they can start to begin to explain what’s happened to them and provide the evidence that’s needed to go after the traffickers.



“We are really advocating for greater resources for law enforcement to be able to build financial investigations.



“Modern slavery is an economic crime. We need to be able to go after the money, hit them where it hurts, and build that evidence base so that wherever possible, survivors aren’t being re-traumatised by having to tell their story over and over again.”

All of the visits taken across the week by GMP were led by intelligence from members of the public, before being verified by police and other partners.

DCI Cronin adds: “We’re not just going to put a plaster on the problem. Organised Immigration Crime is tied up in many things from modern slavery to money laundering and drugs.

“GMP’s intelligence and understanding of this area continues to grow. We are passionate about rooting out the people who are exploiting very vulnerable people, and our officers are trained to spot it.

“We can’t do this on our own, we need all of our partners and that includes the public helping us find who needs our help.”



Minister for Border Security and Asylum, Alex Norris says: “These results are yet another example of targeted collaboration between the police, Immigration Enforcement, and other partners, to crack down on organised immigration crime.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We are using every lever we have to loosen the grip of criminal gangs on our high streets.

“This specific action comes alongside illegal working visits and arrests being at their highest level in British history, and our action to return nearly 70,000 people with no right to be here since coming into power.”

News.title: Viral vid of teens’ disgusting behaviour on school trip sparks diplomatic incident as embassy officials beg forgiveness
News.content:
A VIRAL video of teens’ disgusting behaviour on a school trip sparked a diplomatic incident as embassy officials had to beg for forgiveness.

The Italian school group were caught on camera insulting a Thai woman who asked them to keep the noise down on a train in Bangkok.



Footage shared social media showed the woman confronting the rowdy group on the BTS SkyTrain, telling them: “In Thailand, we don’t scream.”

When asked where they were from, the teens mockingly replied: Thailand before calling her a “B****”.



One teenager was seen raising a middle finger at the woman as the rest laughed and continued making noise.

The shocking exchange escalated further when a teacher sarcastically told her: “Sorry for bringing money to your country.”



The teacher then told the woman to “shut the f*** up” and insisted the group were “just children”.

The explosive clip racked up 16million views online, triggering a furious backlash.

One social media user blasted: “Bringing money, no one complains, but please bring some manners too.”

Another fumed: “Bringing money to Thailand doesn’t make you a god.”



The online fury quickly snowballed, with users identifying the teenagers and flooding their schools’ social media pages with criticism.

Others went even further by waiting outside the hotel where the group were staying and demanding an apology.

As the international storm intensified, the Italian embassy in Bangkok released a cringeworthy video showing three adults and one teenager bowing as they begged for forgiveness.

After bowing, a male adult said: “We are the leaders of the Italian group that went viral.

“We are making this video to apologise to the Thai people and Thai culture.



“We wanted to shoot this video yesterday, but we were worried and scared so we postponed. That was probably the wrong decision.

“We wanted to ask for forgiveness for our behaviour to the Thai people and the country.”

A woman said: “I’m personally extremely sorry for what has happened.

“I know that money can’t buy respect and I’m really sorry for all the people offended and for having offended Thai culture and Thai people.”

A teenage boy added: “I’m very sorry for everyone in Thailand because of what I did on the BTS train. It was wrong. I’m very sorry for my behaviour.”



A second adult woman said: “We do not accept this behaviour.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The students are returning to Italy as soon as possible, and we will also try to teach our group again to strictly respect that culture.

“Thank you for welcoming us and we humbly ask for your forgiveness.”

News.title: Boy, 2, suffers COCAINE overdose as cops find white powder at Airbnb and arrest mum’s friend who was watching him
News.content:
OVERDOSE HORROR Boy, 2, suffers COCAINE overdose as cops find white powder at Airbnb and arrest mum’s friend who was watching him

A TWO-YEAR-OLD boy who overdosed on cocaine while staying at a holiday Airbnb has miraculously survived.

Alexander T. Moles, a friend of the tot’s mum, has been arrested after cops found white powder and straws at the rental home in New Jersey.



Moles, 39, was supposed to be watching over the young boy while his mum showered.

He is now facing charges of child endangerment and cocaine possession, among others, after allegedly failing to keep the child out of harm’s way.



When the mum stepped out the shower, she panicked after seeing that her young son was having trouble breathing and acting sleepy, according to court documents.

Moles then allegedly rushed the tot to hospital and called the mum en route to ask if it was OK for her son to fall asleep.

She replied that it was not OK and called first responders to the scene of their holiday rental home on the Jersey Shore.

Moles allegedly told police that he believed the child had taken “pain killers”.

Once in hospital, the boy was saved thanks to two doses of Naloxone nasal spray that reversed the overdose, according to NJ.com.

The tot tested positive for cocaine after he was taken to Cooper University Hospital Cape Regional for blood tests.



A clear bag containing white powder, tinfoil packets labelled “tapentadol hydrochloride” and a pill were found when cops searched the Airbnb.

Tapentadol hydrochloride is a strong opioid used to treat chronic pain.

Drug users can abuse prescription medication by mixing it with substances like cocaine to strengthen the effects.



Moles had been staying with the woman and her multiple children, including the victim, at the rental property.

Police did not disclose the nature of his relationship with the mother.

The 39-year-old, who works as an emergency medical technician for the Paterson Fire Department, was arrested on Tuesday.

He was booked in the Cape May County Correctional Facility and released with conditions following a detention hearing on Friday.

In full, Moles has been charged with endangering the welfare of a child, possession of cocaine, possession of drug paraphernalia and possession of prescription legend drugs.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

He now faces up to 10 years in prison if convicted.

The Sun has reached out to Moles’ lawyer, John Zarych, for comment.

News.title: Man and woman die after being pulled from sea at popular UK surfing beach
News.content:
BEACH TRAGEDY Man and woman die after being pulled from sea at popular UK surfing beach

A MAN and a woman have died at sea near Britain’s most famous surfing beach.

Emergency services raced to Fistral Beach in Newquay, Cornwall, at 9.45pm after two people were pulled from the water.



Cops said in a statement: “Police were called by the South Western Ambulance Service at around 9.45pm on Sunday 26 July following reports that two people had been recovered from the water at Fistral Beach, Newquay.

“Emergency services attended and a cordon was put in place, which has since been removed.



“Sadly, a man and a woman were pronounced deceased at the scene. Their families have been informed, and our thoughts are with them at this extremely difficult time.

“A file will be prepared for HM Coroner.”

Locals reported at least nine emergency vehicles and a helicopter at the scene, alongside two lifeboats on the water.

The 750 metre-long beach is known as the “home of British surfing” and is known for massive winter wave swells.

It hosts several surf competitions throughout the year including Boardmasters, and is the birthplace of champion longboarder Ben Skinner.

One eyewitness told The Sun she saw the horror unfold, saying: “A man came running up the cliff saying there were people drowning in the water.



“I went halfway down the cliff and saw people at the edge of the water trying to help people out.

“A woman was desperately trying to ring someone but couldn’t get through.

“I told her we didn’t know who it was in the water but she was in tears.

“There was a helicopter overhead and there was a lifeboat in the water.

“They recovered one body on the beach, while the other one was brought up the cliff.



“Another man came up soaking wet and in a foil blanket. He knew them and had been trying to help. I’m just in shock, it was awful to watch.”

Sand Phoenix, who was sleeping on Fistral Beach when the tragedy unfolded around 9.30pm on Sunday night, said he “sprinted” up to help.

The 33-year-old told The Sun: “He had been pulled out of the water but had been in there about seven minutes.

“I had an adrenaline pen which I jabbed him with and tried to give him oxygen but his lungs were full of water and there was no response.

“The paramedics arrived and carried on trying to give CPR. He was still wearing his trousers so I don’t think he had been swimming.



“It looks like they had been walking near the rocks and had fallen in.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A coastguard statement read: “HM Coastguard has been responding to an incident in the South Fistral area, Newquay, overnight.

“First informed at around 9.30pm (26 July), Coastguard Rescue Teams from Newquay, Padstow and St Agnes, lifeboats from Newquay RNLI and an HM Coastguard helicopter were sent to the scene, alongside other emergency services.”



﻿

News.title: TikTok star Rebecca Luna dies aged 49 after battle with early-onset Alzheimer’s and final tragic message to followers
News.content:
TIKTOK star Rebecca Luna has died at the age of 49 after spending years documenting her battle with Alzheimer’s online.

The inspirational influencer turned to Medical Aid in Dying (MAID) to end her life over the weekend as her death was announced in a final heartbreaking video posted to her account.



The short video from her oldest daughter Maya said: “Rebecca passed away July 25th at approximately 1.15 pm surrounded by her loved ones.

“Thank you for your support and privacy.”



Rebecca, a mum-of-two based in Victoria, British Columbia, had over 47,000 followers on TikTok at the time of her tragic death.

She managed to build up a loyal fan base after announcing her Alzheimer’s diagnosis in April 2025.



Rebecca openly admitted to symptoms first appearing in her late 40s as she suffered blacking out mid-conversation and constantly forgetting things such as where she left her keys.

Earlier this month, Rebecca announced her decision to go through with MAID.

MAID is a process that allows someone who is found eligible to be able to receive assistance from a medical practitioner to end their life on their terms.

Rebecca had been given a five to seven year life expectancy by doctors when she was first diagnosed at the age of 46.



She candidly told her followers just a few days ago that she will undergo MAID due to her “decline coming faster than I had hoped”.

The brave mum explained in her final TikTok video: “It’s a hard decision to make, because I’m living in a body that doesn’t feel comfortable, safe, good, nothing.

“It feels terrible. This is when I get to prioritise myself, and I haven’t done that my whole life.”



She added: “I’ve suffered enough in this world. But at the same time, the suffering has brought me to this place of ‘I really know who I am and I really know that I have a good f**king heart’.”

News.title: France wildfires live: Inferno threatens Bordeaux as Macron holds crisis meeting
News.content:
More than 250,000 people have been evacuated in south-west France due to raging wildfires heading towards Bordeaux and its airport

Violent wildfires are less then seven miiles the French city of Bordeaux and its airport, with more than 250,000 people evacuated from the area.

Firefighters are struggling to contain the flames, which have burned 42,000 hectares - an area four times the size of Paris - leaving two firefighters dead and 84 injured. Volunteers, including local farmers, are helping by towing huge water tankers to the scene.

President Emmanuel Macron is holding a crisis meeting as shifting winds and arid conditions have made the blaze impossible to control. The main fire has caused an unprecedented "pyrocumulonimbus" - a huge fire thunderstorm fuelled by its own winds and lightning, the National Firefighters Federation of France said.

And flames have now prompted the closure of the hotel zone at Bordeaux Airport, and travellers have been advised to look outside the evacuation areas for accommodation.

Meanwhile in Spain, wildfires have burned out of control around Madrid, with evacuations carried out yesterday in the Valencia region.

News.title: TV Licence rule that could see UK households get a refund
News.content:
TV Licence rule that could see UK households get a refund

Lots of people don’t realise they might not need a TV Licence in the first place - which could save them a fair bit of money over the year.

View 3 Images Not everyone needs a TV Licence (Image: MMassel via Getty Images)

If you only need a TV Licence for part of the year - or your circumstances change and you no longer need one - you could be entitled to a refund. Even if you’ve already paid, it may still be possible to claim some of the cost back.

‌



A standard colour TV Licence costs £180 a year, while a black-and-white licence costs £60.50. The updated prices reflect the most recent increase, which came into force on April 1, 2026.

‌



TV Licensing's website confirms that getting one "covers you to watch all TV channels, live TV on pay TV and streaming services, plus everything on BBC iPlayer. On any device". But what about if you no longer need one or decide you don't want to watch these channels anymore?

‌



I don't watch live on any channel, TV service or streaming service or use BBC iPlayer. Can I get a refund?

View 3 Images The fee increased in April 2026 (Image: Getty)

Yes. You can cancel your licence and may be eligible for a refund if, before your licence expires, you won't be:

watching TV on any channel, like BBC, ITV, Channel 4, U&Dave and international channels

watching TV on pay TV services, like Sky, Virgin Media and EE TV

watching live TV on streaming services, like YouTube, Netflix, and Amazon Prime Video.

using BBC iPlayer - a licence is not needed to watch S4C programmes on demand.

‌



Do not cancel your direct debit

TV Licensing cautions: "Please don’t cancel your Direct Debit" if you'd like to:

request a refund

apply for a different type of licence

change payment scheme

It adds: "We will cancel your Direct Debit for you. Cancelling your Direct Debit does not cancel your licence, so unless we hear from you, you will still receive the reminder letters we send to unlicensed addresses."

‌



How can I apply for a TV Licence refund?

You can apply for a refund if you won’t need your licence again before it expires and you have at least one full unused month left. If you qualify for the blind concession, you can apply for a refund at any point, for whatever time remains on your licence.

Refund applications can be made up to 14 days before the date you no longer need a TV Licence.

When will I get my TV Licence refund?

View 3 Images You may get a warning letter if you are not registered (Image: Stephen Barnes via Getty Images)

‌



TV Licensing officials state: "We aim to process and issue refunds within 21 days of receiving your application. Any refund due to you will be paid to you by either a cheque or by BACS transfer directly into your bank account. Your refund may be delayed if we have to contact you for more information."

It adds: "Working out precise refund amounts can be complicated. But we will do it for you. We’ll look carefully at the information you give us and let you know if we can offer you a refund, and how much it will be."

I am watching TV without a Licence, could I get a fine?

Yes. Watching, recording or downloading TV programmes without a valid TV Licence may result in prosecution. If you’re convicted, you could be fined up to £1,000.

Article continues below

You may also have to pay any legal costs and compensation. In Guernsey, the maximum fine is higher, at up to £2,000.

News.title: Gianni Infantino’s rambling World Cup rant shows FIFA boss has gone ‘full Donald Trump’
News.content:
Gianni Infantino’s rambling World Cup rant shows FIFA boss has gone ‘full Donald Trump’

The FIFA president has responded to his critics and has claimed that the 2026 World Cup was 'outstanding' but his assessment of the tournament is badly flawed

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino sounded like his good friend Donald Trump during a lengthy rant directed at World Cup critics (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

Considering the amount of personal criticism he gets, Gianni Infantino is allowed the right to respond. Of course he is.

‌



And the FIFA president can respond in whatever manner he sees fit. Had he responded via a press conference at the end of the World Cup, it might have been better. But if he wants to do it in a 15-slide post on social media, that is fine.

‌



However, his declarations about the tournament are the ramblings of someone who has been made truly delusional by power. Having spent so much of the last couple of years on the shoulder of Donald Trump, why wouldn’t Infantino feel powerful?

‌



There are suggestions Trump wants Infantino as the next secretary-general of the United Nations, for goodness sake. But Infantino’s lengthy outburst against critics of some aspects of the 2026 World Cup reads like wilfully deceptive propaganda.

Gianni Infantino slams FIFA critics in bizarre letter that glosses over World Cup issues READ MORE :

World Cup final referee Slavko Vincic quits football days later as statement released READ MORE :

“We experienced no violence, no incidents, 100 percent safety and security, only joy and happiness!” That is one of his declarations in his Instagram essay.

There was, indeed, a lot of joy and happiness, but four people died during World Cup celebrations in Mexico City following Mexico’s victory over Ecuador in the round-of-32. Fans from four competing countries - Iran, Haiti, Somalia and Ivory Coast - could not share the ‘joy and happiness’ because they were banned from entering the United States.

‌



In his post, Infantino says that “Iran entered the United States without incident or conflict.” Yet it was widely reported that only four of the 15 Iranian team staff members who were originally denied visas were later granted the right to travel into the country.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

And don’t forget, Omar Artan - regarded as African football’s best referee - was denied entrance to America on the eve of the tournament.

‌



“You mentioned the few people denied visas and overlooked the millions who were approved, from all parts of the world,” wrote Infantino. “Because football unites the world and it was demonstrated impressively this summer.”

So, is everyone supposed to just brush aside cases such as the Artan one? Yes, according to Infantino, it seems.

He says critics of the tournament should ‘meditate, pray or watch a football match’ in order ‘to find peace’. He says critics have been ‘spreading hate’.

‌



View 3 Images Top referee Omar Artan was sent back to Somalia after being refused entry into the United States for the 2026 World Cup (Image: SAID YUSUF WARSAME/EPA/Shutterstock)

But no-one is ‘spreading hate’ by denouncing FIFA for allowing football on the grandest stage to become a game of four quarters. Was there a pundit out there who likes the idea of compulsory hydration breaks?

And no-one was ‘spreading hate’ when denouncing FIFA for the suspension of Folarin Balogun’s automatic one-game ban after the United States’ 2-0 victory over Bosnia and Herzegovina in the first round of knockout games. Trump had phoned Infantino to ask him to review the Balogun ban. It was subsequently suspended, allowing the player to line up against Belgium in a round-of-16 tie.

‌



“Indeed, ‘arguable’ referees’ decisions or ‘strange’ disciplinary rulings such as for instance potentially mistaken red or yellow cards or subsequent decisions not to ban players in certain situations are routine and widely accepted in some of the biggest leagues in the world,” Infantino wrote. “It’s curious that the same countries employing these practices are the ones criticising.”

View 3 Images Folarin Balogun's one-game ban at the 2026 World Cup was controversially suspended by FIFA (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

There are rights of appeal in disciplinary processes in club leagues but the Balogun decision was a totally arbitrary one that has yet to be explained by anyone at FIFA. Clearly, it should, though, in the eyes of Infantino, be brushed under the carpet. We should all just chill out and admit the World Cup was great.

‌



“To the pens and papers, to all the screens, may you find love and peace where the people behind you couldn’t,” he went on. “May you find peace; we at FIFA have found ours and we deliver it, by delivering the most outstanding FIFA World Cup.”

As the final ended in scenes of post-match violent chaos, he really is delusional if he thought that was ‘the most outstanding FIFA World Cup.’ He has been hanging around with him so much, he has gone full Trump.

News.title: RAF plane 'declares emergency' over Liverpool as pilot issues squawk alert
News.content:
RAF plane 'declares emergency' over Liverpool as pilot issues squawk alert

The T-6 aircraft took off from Anglesey Airport in Wales and indicated a general emergency on board while flying over Liverpool

View Image The emergency was declared over Liverpool (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

An RAF aircraft has reportedly declared a general emergency on board over Liverpool.

‌



The T-6 aircraft, which took off from Anglesey Airport in Wales, transmitted the 7700 code. The 7700 squawk code is declared by pilots when an aircraft experiences an in-flight emergency that requires immediate priority handling and assistance from air traffic controllers.

‌



Such emergencies include "mechanical failures, onboard safety threats, medical emergencies or unclear or escalating situations". The code acts as a silent "Mayday" which prompts air traffic control to clear airspace and alert emergency services on the ground.

‌



The aircraft is then guided to the nearest suitable runway. Flight RRR59 / VYT59 departed from Anglesey Airport in north Wales, where RAF Valley is located. The flight, operated by a T-6 aircraft identified as TEX2 (ZM343), returned to base around half an hour later.

It landed just before 9.20am.

News.title: Newquay emergency live: Man and woman dead at Fistral Beach as 999 crews swarm
News.content:
Devon and Cornwall Police, coastguard and the ambulance service have all rushed to Fistral Beach in Newquay, with a helicopter circling the area

A man and a woman have been pronounced dead at the scene after being pulled from the water at a popular beach in Cornwall.

Police, coastguard and the ambulance service have all been deployed at Fistral Beach in Newquay since last night. The Royal National Lifeboat Institution (RNLI) confirmed two lifeboats were launched yesterday at around 9.30pm.

Witnesses described seeing up to nine emergency vehicles at the beach, with a rescue helicopter also circling overhead, CornwallLive reports.

Cornwall Police said the families of the two dead have been informed.

The Mirror has launched the Save Lives For Sam water safety campaign to tackle the UK's growing drowning crisis. Backed by MPs, Olympic champions, national water safety organisations and bereaved families, the campaign is calling for urgent action to make our waters safer.

News.title: Andy Burnham's council tax plans - what an overhaul could mean for you and your money
News.content:
Andy Burnham has said there are 'big decisions' to be made on council tax as he criticised the unfairness of the way the system operates.

The current council tax system is seen as deeply flawed and can mean someone living in a £150,000 terraced house in Middlesbrough pays the same as the wealthy owner of a £250million in London’s Westminster.

The Prime Minister told the BBC: "There are people here in Greater Manchester who pay a much higher council tax than people living in much larger homes in London.

"So the Chancellor before, Rachel Reeves, was right to start to reform council tax to create some fairness there in relation to people in homes that are of much greater value, who haven't seen their council tax go up over the years because of the failure to revalue the banding. So that's an example of something that I think was right and fair."

‌



He added: He added: "We need to honour the manifesto upon which Labour was elected, and if I was to bring forward any changes, obviously people would rightly say, well, is this consistent with that manifesto? So there are big decisions ahead, you are right about that."

Mr Burnham has previously said he has been 'persuaded' of the argument for reforming the system. But Number 10 has denied reports that the Government is considering replacing council tax and stamp duty with a tax based on property or land values.

Backers of a property tax overhaul claim that replacing the current council tax system with a proportional property tax could save 18 million households an average of more than £550 a year.

Dozens of MPs, leading think tanks and others have swung behind the idea - and the new Prime Minister said last month he was “personally keen to see reform of council tax.”

‌



But although many households would pay less under the proposed change, owners of more expensive homes, especially in the south east, would see their annual property tax jump.

View 5 Images Homes on 'billionaires row' in north London can have council tax bills that are not hugely more than a three bed semi in County Durham (Image: Alex Segre/UCG/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

What Andy Burnham as PM could mean for your money - from taxes to state pension READ MORE :

What is council tax?

It replaced the hated poll tax - officially the Community Charge - introduced by the Tories in 1990 in England (a year earlier in Scotland) which itself replaced the old domestic rates system. After a massive backlash - which contributed to Tory leader Margaret Thatcher’s resignation - council tax was brought in instead.

It saw all properties split into eight bands (A to H) based on how much they were worth in 1991. It’s remained the same since. Council Tax is an annual fee you pay to your local council, which set the amount for each band, and goes towards funding local services, such as rubbish collection and libraries. It brings in £35billion a year but not nearly enough to meet local authorities’ funding needs.

‌



View 5 Images Council tax arrears have soared under the current system (Image: Getty)

What is stamp duty?

A tax usually paid when buying a property or a piece of land. It applies to residential properties in England and Northern Ireland costing more than £125,000, unless you are a first-time buyer, where it’s £300,000. For all other buyers, it’s then 2% on purchases from £125,000 to £250,000, and increases in price blocks above that. Scotland and Wales operate similar systems.

Stamp duty is a big money spinner for the Treasury, raking in more than £18billion a year. However, critics say it is a big drag on the housing market, adding thousands of pounds to the cost of buying a home.

View 5 Images A terraced house in Darlington has the same council tax as a £14m apartment in Westminster (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Why is council tax seen as unfair by some?

Critics say the system is long overdue for reform given dramatic regional differences in property prices. Official estimates suggest the average home in London is now worth more than six times what it was in 1995, compared with barely three times in the North East.

Due to limited number of bands, it’s led to a ludicrous situation where people living in vastly more valuable homes paying the same - or even less - than others in properties worth a fraction. For example, an ultra-luxury apartment in Westminster on the market for a staggering £14million is liable for Band H council tax of £2,096.

Yet that’s less than a three-bed semi-detached house for sale in Darlington for £245,000 in Band C and paying £2,250 a year. Put another way, the tax on the Darlington property is 0.92% of how much it’s worth, compared with just 0.015% for the Westminster flat.

Bishops Avenue in North London has been famously dubbed “Billionaires’ Row” given it is home to the super-rich. It is one of the wealthiest residential streets in the world. Currently for sale is a £35million seven-bed mansion, complete with indoor swimming pool, sauna, steam room, lift and staff quarters.

‌



The combined Barnet Council Greater London Authority bill for the property is £4,265. In Bishops Auckland, County Durham, meanwhile a three-bed terrace on the market for just £45,000 is still liable for council tax of £1,766. The tax on the terraced home is 4% compared with a minuscule 0.012% on the Bishops Avenue mega-home.

View 5 Images Scrapping stamp duty could take away one of the barriers for older people in larger homes thinking on down sizing (Image: Getty)

Andrew Dixon, founder of Fairer Share, which is calling for the abolition of council tax and stamp duty, said: “Families in ordinary homes in towns across the country are often paying 10, twenty or even sixty times more as a share of their property value than owners of multi-million-pound homes in London. This is not a glitch. It is the inevitable result of a tax still based on 1991 property values, crude bands and a top band that stops at values completely detached from today’s housing market.”

What is the alternative being suggested?

Fairer Share is among those arguing for council tax and stamp to be scrapped and replaced with what is known as a proportional property tax set at 0.48% of a property’s value, or 0.96% for second homes, empty properties and those owned by foreign buyers. Supporters say technology allows for a real-time assessment of property values, similar to those used by websites such as Zoopla and Rightmove.

‌



They are, however, based on asking prices, which may be different from what the property is actually worth if sold. As the tax would be paid by owners, that would mean landlords rather than tenants. That said, there is a risk landlords will just pass it in on through higher rents.

The i Paper reports that another option being considered, is introducing a land value tax, which would be an annual charge based on the value of the land a property sits on, rather than the building.

Would I pay more or less?

While supporters claim three quarters of homes would pay less, that means one in four will be stung with a tax hike. Given how much prices differ, the hit would be mostly concentrated on millions of home owners in London and the South East.

Aware of the backlash, supporters propose capping any annual increase at £1,200, still a big shock for many. The cap would, however, be removed when the home is next sold, meaning a potentially whopping tax bill going forward for the new owner.

‌



In another nod to concerns among those who are “asset rich, cash poor”, there would be the option to defer the increase until the property is sold, when it would all need to be paid.

The Fairer Share website has an online tool to work out how you might be impacted.

What is the impact on council coffers?

The current system has banding charges that are not vastly different by council. However, basing it on a percentage of property values risk meaning windfalls for already rich areas, and poorer areas suffering a slump. To tackle this, supporters say central government would redistribute tax revenues so councils in lower-value areas are not left worse off, while still giving local authorities a stable funding base.

The shake-up, claim supporters, would be revenue-neutral, meaning it wouldn't mean any loss of taxes. But setting the PPT higher could rake in more tax though mean more losers in term of paying more.

News.title: Jet2, Ryanair and TUI passengers warned 'never to pack' 5  items into checked luggage
News.content:
Jet2, Ryanair and TUI passengers warned 'never to pack' 5 items into checked luggage

There are some items that are best kept in your hand luggage for safe keeping, so make sure these items don't end up in your big suitcase when you go away for your summer holidays this year

View 2 Images Some items are better packed in your hand luggage (Image: Getty Images)

No matter how many times you go on holiday, packing is always an awkward task, as you need to balance the lack of space with the essentials.

‌



And if you have checked luggage in addition to a cabin bag, you may be tempted to throw most of the things you own into your hold baggage. This means you have less stuff to carry around the airport and onto the plane with you.

‌



But there are some things you should never put in checked luggage, and it’s not just the obvious stuff like weapons and flammable items. Here are five items to never send to the hold.

‌



London Gatwick alert to everyone taking checked baggage READ MORE :

View 2 Images Keep prescription medication in your hand luggage for safe keeping (Image: Julien Behal/PA Wire)

1. Prescription medication

Overall, less than 1% of hold luggage goes missing, and usually it’s simply misdirected, so it will eventually make its way to you. But while you try to retrieve your bag, it’s a good idea to have supplies of essential items.

Prescription medication is better taken as hand luggage, as it’s much less likely to go missing. If there’s a delay with your hold bag getting back to you, you won’t need to worry about missing vital doses of your meds.

‌



If you do lose your medication when travelling, visit a local pharmacy for advice, as they may be able to arrange an emergency supply.

2. Batteries and electronics

Because of the risk of items such as power banks catching fire, items with lithium batteries, such as power banks and vapes, can’t be placed in hold luggage and must be taken onboard with you.

Some airlines have limits on how many Personal Electronic Devices (PEDs) can be taken onboard, with Jet2 and Ryanair restricting the number to 15 per passenger. Ryanair also has a limit of 20 lithium batteries or power banks, each up to 100Wh, in hand baggage.

‌



3. Valuable items

If you have jewellery, cash or other expensive items, you may be nervous about carrying them around in your backpack at the airport. However, it’s not a good idea to leave valuables in your checked-in bags.

There’s a risk of damage to items in transit, and while it’s rare, theft from bags does happen by airport staff. While travel insurance does cover lost baggage, it usually has a limit and policies have an excess to pay, meaning you may not be able to claim enough to cover valuable items.

4. Swimwear

When you’re on the way to a sunny beach holiday, you may want to pack swimwear in your hand luggage rather than your big suitcase. This means that if there is a delay in getting your bag to you, you can at least spend some time on the beach or by the pool while you wait for your bag to arrive.

‌



It also means that if you can’t check into your room straight away when you arrive, you can just change into your swimwear and enjoy some sunshine while you wait for your room to be ready.

UK holiday parks with new lidos and cabanas have family holidays under £400 this summer READ MORE :

Ryanair to axe two million seats to European country by early 2027 READ MORE :

5. Phone charger and adapter

Once you arrive at your destination, your phone battery is going to be as low as your energy levels, and you won’t want to be scrambling through your suitcase to find your charger.

Ensure you’ve got your phone charger and adapter for the country you’re visiting in your hand luggage so you can get plugged in as soon as you arrive.
