Sports.title: Micky van de Ven takes dig at Thomas Frank as he tells Tottenham fans what to expect under Roberto de Zerbi next season
Sports.content:
MICKY VAN DE VEN also aimed a dig at former Spurs boss Thomas Frank by praising Roberto De Zerbi’s preference to play attractive and attacking football.

A number of Spurs stars grew disillusioned under Frank, who was sacked after just eight months in charge in February with the north Londoners having won just two of 17 Premier League games.



A disastrous spell with Igor Tudor followed that left the white-half of north London on the brink of relegation.

But much of the damage was done with the squad Frank assembled and the style he imposed, which Van de Ven believes is night and day with De Zerbi.



He said: “It’s going to be different compared to the former manager we had last season. It’s going to be more with the ball, more playing football, it’s going to be more enjoyable also for people to watch, when playing offensive football.

“The last couple of weeks of last season, you saw he brought a lot of passion into our group, a lot mentality- wise, passio-n wise, on the pitch.

“It is something we needed because everybody was a little bit down. We started to play a lot with the ball, because he loves us to be on the ball, he loves to play the football he wants to play, and that’s also something I really enjoy.

“I like being on the ball, instead of running behind the ball the whole time. He brings a lot of good energy and from preseason, we have really got the time now to bring his football into the team. That’s really enjoyable.”

The 25-year-old also hailed Tottenham for their ambitious £230million recruitment drive following a relegation scare.

The Dutchman, who Spurs are hoping to tie down to a new deal, says it is an important change of direction for players who have been part of back-to-back 17th-placed finishes.

Spurs’ dismal season saw them in a relegation battle until the final day of the campaign.

Sports.title: Female futsal star banned for five years after sickening kick to head leaving opponent in hospital
Sports.content:
THIS is the horror moment a female futsal player kicks an opponent in the head after slide-tackling her before punching another in the face when she tries to intervene.

Lara do Nascimento Costa turned violent with her feet and fists in an astonishing five-second flurry of violence during her team’s futsal championship match.



Kick assault victim Ana Julia Alencar, who was lying on the ground when she was booted twice in the head, ended up being taken to hospital after the ugly incident.

The shocking turn of events happened at a sports centre on the outskirts of the Ceara state capital Fortaleza in northeast Brazil.



The female aggressor’s side As Resenhas was losing 1-0 against opponents Projeto RDJ Esport Feminino in an amateur match played as part of the Eusebio Municipal Women’s Futsal Championship.

The incident occurred at the beginning of the second half of the tie and led to the game being abandoned.



Overnight it emerged the female player who lashed out had been banned from playing in any event organised by the Eusebio Sports League for FIVE YEARS following a disciplinary hearing on Friday.

Action has also been taken against her team over Wednesday’s incidents.

Eusebio Town Hall said in a statement: “The Municipality of Eusebio wishes to publicly state that it strongly condemns violence and any form of unsportsmanlike conduct.

“A team from our Sports and Youth Department is accompanying the athlete who was kicked in the head and was treated at an emergency medical care unit in Eusebio. She is doing okay.”

Radio Nascimento, President of Projeto RDJ Esport Feminino, confirmed Ana Julia Alencar and her unnamed teammate who was punched in the face were both recovering at home.

She said: “It is an extremely regrettable situation and one we would never want to witness on a sports court.



“We will continue to take all appropriate measures to ensure that incidents like this do not happen again and that our athletes have the safety and respect they deserve.”

Futsal is an association football-based game played on a hard court which is a variation of mini football. It is played between two teams of five players each, one of whom is the goalie.

Antonio Edson dos Santos Sousa was filmed on a live online feed falling to the ground as he went to high five an overjoyed teammate.

Sports.title: Fifa president Gianni Infantino issues bizarre 880-word statement on ‘strange’ decisions as he slams World Cup critics
Sports.content:
GIANNI INFANTINO has congratulated himself on an “incident-free” World Cup and accused his critics of “spreading hate”.

The Fifa president, 56, reflected on this summer‘s tournament in the USA, Canada and Mexico in a lengthy 15-slide Instagram post.



In it, he called out the hypocrisy of those who kicked up a fuss after Folarin Balogun‘s one-match ban was suspended following a phone call from Donald Trump, celebrated the way the Iranian national team was treated, and defended the visa drama that left an African referee out in the cold.

A defiant Infantino wrote: “To those behind their pens and papers, behind their screens spreading hate and false rumours, I want to say that while you are sitting behind, we at Fifa are on the front lines organising, working hard, and delivering the best show in the world.”



He added: “We experienced no violence, no incidents, 100 per cent safety and security, only joy and happiness!

“While they celebrated, you were busy planting seeds of hate.”



Most would consider it a World Cup packed with controversy.

Balogun’s suspended ban was front and centre of the drama, sparking strong criticism from European governing body Uefa, the threat of legal action from the Belgian FA, and a formal complaint from Norwegian football chiefs.

But Infantino said: “Maybe it’s time to show some love.

“Indeed, ‘arguable’ referees’ decisions or ‘strange’ disciplinary rulings such as for instance potentially mistaken red or yellow cards or subsequent decisions not to ban players in certain situations are routine and widely accepted in some of the biggest leagues worldwide.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“It’s curious that the same counties employing these practices are the ones criticising.”

The Fifa boss also celebrated the safe passage of the Iranian team into American territory amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.



That is despite the fact Iran were only allowed to fly into the States the day before their first two group games, and four of their staff members were initially denied visas.

He continued: “While you spread hatred, we worked tirelessly to unite two countries at war.

“Iran entered the United States without incident or conflict.

“It’s not about politics. Football is about unity, not division. Football is bigger than hate and discrimination.”

Infantino also brushed off the visa issues that affected some fans and barred Somali referee Omar Artan from travelling to the tournament.



He said: “You mentioned the few people denied visas and overlooked the millions who were approved, from all parts of the world.”

Sports.title: ‘It kills everything’ – Levi Colwill out to prove he can be a Premier League great after Chelsea star’s injury hell
Sports.content:
LEVI COLWILL is out to prove he can be a Premier League great after feeling “helpless” last season.

The Chelsea defender suffered a horror ACL injury on day one of pre-season last summer and was only fit for the final four games of a season in which the Blues had three managers and slumped to a 10th place finish.



Colwill‘s ACL rupture robbed Chelsea of a key figure in their Club World Cup triumph, as well as preventing him from making his Champions League debut and having a shot at making England‘s World Cup squad.

Now, aiming for a full pre-season, the academy graduate wants to take his game to the next level.



Colwill, 23, said: “When you can’t do anything to affect the game on the pitch, you feel helpless and that’s how I felt at times.

“You tell yourself everything happens for a reason but you start doubting yourself.

“You come off winning the Club World Cup feeling on top of the world and then an injury like that happens.

“It kills everything, kills the momentum and you’re out for a long time.

“But you’ve got to stay positive, you’ve got to believe in yourself and trust the process, which I’ve done.

“I felt like that helped me a lot when I came back for the last few games of the season, to be strong and hungry to be the best player I can be and help the team as much as possible.

“I know my targets in my head. I want to take my game to the next level this year. I want to be regarded as one of the best centre-backs in the league this year, 100 per cent.

“Hopefully I can help my team and lead them on to good things this year.”

Colwill’s return, along with the appointment of Xabi Alonso has the potential to transform the Blues.



With no European football, Alonso has plenty of time to work with his new squad across the season and the players are not putting a limit on their ambitions.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso says Chelsea’s busy transfer window is only just getting going despite splashing out £226m on new signings
Sports.content:
XABI ALONSO says Chelsea’s busy transfer window is only just getting going.

The new Blues boss is prepared to be doing deals up until the final day of the window, having already spent £226million on new signings this summer.

Sports.title: Chelsea outline Pedro Neto stance as Man City and Liverpool consider offers
Sports.content:
Chelsea outline Pedro Neto stance as Man City and Liverpool consider offers

Chelsea winger Pedro Neto is being eyed up by some of the Blues' Premier League rivals - but they are determined not to sell the former Wolves star on the cheap

View 2 Images Pedro Neto is wanted by other Premier League clubs (Image: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC)

Chelsea would look to ensure any transfer fee received for Pedro Neto would be proportionate to some of the mammoth figures being quoted for other wide attackers this summer amid growing interest in the former Wolves man.

‌



Liverpool and Manchester City have both been credited with an interest in Neto, who joined the Blues back in the summer of 2024. Chelsea shelled out £54million to bring the 26-year-old to Stamford Bridge, but the market has exploded in the last couple of years.

‌



And that means Chelsea will only sell Neto this summer if his suitors are willing to pay a premium price.

‌



The Mail report that Chelsea have noted some of the figures being placed upon in-demand wingers this summer, such as Bradley Barcola and Yan Diomande. Both players are valued in excess of £100m.

Jadon Sancho finally receives shock contract offer months after Man Utd exit READ MORE :

While it's noted that Neto would be unlikely to command such a transfer fee, Chelsea could still ask for a figure which is some way north of the amount they signed him for two years ago.

Interest from Premier League rivals is not thought to be a surprise to Chelsea; Enzo Maresca favoured Neto as his first-choice right winger while in charge at Stamford Bridge and is keen on working with him again at Manchester City.

‌



Liverpool are in the market for wide attackers as they revamp their squad following the departure of Mohamed Salah, while there is also interest in Neto from clubs in Saudi Arabia.

Neto is currently on holiday after featuring at the World Cup for Portugal.

View 2 Images Enzo Maresca would like to reunite with Neto at Manchester City (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Speaking back in October, just weeks before his explosive exit from Chelsea, Maresca lauded the winger for the improvements he had been showing.

"He’s top, he's very humble and working hard,’ Maresca said of Neto.

"He's a very important player for us, and we are very happy with Pedro. He's exactly the same as other players – he needs to be always 100 per cent, because in the moment that you drop a little bit, mentally or physically, in this league, it's complicated."

Sports.title: Spain star Dani Olmo accuses Argentina coach of lying after World Cup final brawl
Sports.content:
Spain star Dani Olmo accuses Argentina coach of lying after World Cup final brawl

The fallout from the unsavoury scenes after the full-time whistle in the World Cup final continues, with Spain midfielder Dani Olmo accusing Argentina coach Roberto Ayala of lying

View 2 Images Roberto Ayala clashed with Dani Olmo after the World Cup final

Spain star Dani Olmo has refused to accept an apology from Argentina coach Roberto Ayala and accused him of lying about what happened following the World Cup final.

‌



There were violent clashes on the pitch after the full-time whistle crowned Spain as champions in New Jersey. Ferran Torres' goal in extra-time was enough to seal a 1-0 win for Spain, but their winning moment was tarnished by what followed.

‌



Argentina's Leandro Paredes kicked and punched as he shoved Eric Garcia to the ground and grappled with Gavi, while Nahuel Molina appeared to have instigated the altercation by throwing a punch at Rodri.

‌



There was also a flashpoint involving Ayala and Olmo, with the Argentina assistant coach caught on camera putting his hand around the Barcelona midfielder's neck.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Gianni Infantino slams FIFA critics in bizarre letter that glosses over World Cup issues READ MORE :

FIFA are investigating the ugly scenes, which could prompt suspensions and fines. And the backlash against Argentina is continuing, with Olmo speaking out after Ayala said he reacted to something he had heard.

‌



Olmo told newspaper Diari de Terrassa: "Someone who says they're sorry, but justifies a punch by saying it was a response to a comment, is surely not sorry, because he is lying.

"I didn't say anything to him, so he doesn't need to apologise. What truly defines us is not the mistake, but the courage to acknowledge it with humility, honesty and dignity."

He added: "When my children, my family and all those fans watch the game, I want them to be proud of how we competed, how we won and, above all, of our behaviour, because the importance of football means that us players are an example for children and the new generations, and that brings with it a huge responsibility."

‌



View 2 Images Dani Olmo was able to celebrate the win after the incident (Image: Rob Newell/Getty Images)

Ayala had previously said: "Of course I'm sorry. Given my position, I cannot allow a feeling, or whatever I might receive from the other party, to affect my mood or my actions.

"For me, we need to draw a line and leave it at that. It was more of a shove than anything else, it wasn't a punch as they're making it out to be."

‌



He added: "It was a reaction to something he said, but that's it. If I see him, I'll obviously apologise to him in person."

FIFA have appointed a disciplinary and ethics prosecutor to assess the ugly scenes after the full-time whistle. It is likely to result in fines for Argentina failing to control their players and staff.

"There is no place or space for that," Alan Shearer said on the BBC at the time. "We know how much it means to them and we know how much it hurts to lose, but there is a way to lose. Too many times we have seen that from Argentina. The reaction after the final whistle is terrible."

Article continues below

Argentina's lack of discipline was obvious in the game, with Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez sent off after catching Pau Cubarsi with a high foot to receive his second yellow card, having been shown a first one for dissent.

Sports.title: World Cup final referee Slavko Vincic quits football days later as statement released
Sports.content:
World Cup final referee Slavko Vincic quits football days later as statement released

Slavko Vincic has chosen to end his refereeing career after arguably reaching the peak of his field by taking charge of a World Cup final

View 2 Images Slavko Vincic has chosen to retire after refereeing the World Cup final (Image: (Photo by Michael Regan - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images))

The Slovenian FA have confirmed that World Cup final referee Slavko Vincic has officially retired. The 46-year-old was selected by FIFA to officiate Spain's prestigious win over Argentina and has now chosen to end his career, as confirmed by the football association of his home country.

‌



The opening to their official statement read: "One week after the World Cup final in the USA, Slavko Vinčić officially concluded his historic refereeing career at the very top of the world.

‌



"The Maribor native became the first Slovenian head referee to officiate the grand final of the 2026 FIFA World Cup between Spain and Argentina in East Rutherford, confirming his status as one of the greatest officials in history.

‌



Gianni Infantino slams FIFA critics in bizarre letter that glosses over World Cup issues READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino letter to Argentina 'leaked’ with astonishing claim on violent World Cup scenes READ MORE :

"As the crowning achievement of his farewell season, the International Federation of Football History & Statistics (IFFHS) named him the best referee of the World Cup, and he received the prestigious Giulio Campanati award in Italy."

Their statement went on to mention his best achievements which includes being involved in three Europa League finals and refereeing the 2022 showpiece between Frankfurt and Rangers.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Two years later he took charge of the Champions League final between Real Madrid and Borussia Dortmund with his vast experience in crucially important games seemingly playing a role in his World Cup final selection.

Upon learning of the honour being bestowed upon him, Vincic broke down in tears. He had overseen three games earlier in the tournament including the knockout clash between Ecuador and Mexico.

He was forced to send off Piero Hincapie in that match after the Arsenal star covered his mouth to speak to a Mexico player during a heated exchange.

‌



View 2 Images Slavko Vincic showed a red card to Enzo Fernandez during the World Cup final

The red card was also displayed by Vincic at MetLife Stadium after Argentina's Enzo Fernandez committed two yellow card offences.

The 2022 champions were perhaps fortunate to only have one player dismissed with Leandro Parades' conduct disgraceful after he came on as a substitute. The midfielder was one of many involved in a post-match brawl with Vicnic struggling to keep the players apart.

Article continues below

A FIFA investigation was launched in the aftermath but there is yet to be a definitive outcome with the only official update being that Parades was not actually shown a red card by Vicnic after the final whistle.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino slams FIFA critics in bizarre letter that glosses over World Cup issues
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino slams FIFA critics in bizarre letter that glosses over World Cup issues

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has attempted to rewrite history by writing a bizarre 886-word letter which glosses over the controversies of the World Cup and fires back at his haters

View 3 Images FIFA president Gianni Infantino has penned a lengthy open letter (Image: Chris Brunskill/Getty Images)

Gianni Infantino has told FIFA's critics to "take a moment to reflect, meditate or pray" in a rambling and bizarre open letter that attempts to gloss over the problems surrounding the World Cup.

‌



FIFA's president was highly visible during the tournament, attending 44 matches in 39 days in a private jet in order to rub shoulders with world leaders, celebrities and those whose votes he needs to secure another term. Yet his presence at the tournament doesn't seem to have given him any insight into its issues.

‌



The World Cup saw headlines generated over Somali referee Omar Artan's denied visa, Iran's difficulties in entering the United States, Donald Trump's interference in the disciplinary proceedings involving US striker Folarin Balogun after a red card and Argentina celebrating with a banner about the Falkland Islands.

‌



A scandal over massively inflated ticket prices and the controversial introduction of hydration breaks in every half were also major talking points during the tournament, which was staged across the US, Canada and Mexico from June 11 to July 19.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Gianni Infantino accused of contempt as scale of World Cup private jet travel emerges READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino letter to Argentina 'leaked’ with astonishing claim on violent World Cup scenes READ MORE :

Even the final of the World Cup was marred by the behaviour of some of Argentina's players and coaching staff following Spain's victory. Infantino was in attendance alongside Trump at the final in New Jersey a week ago, but has wiped the unsavoury scenes from his memory.

‌



In an 886-word open letter published on his personal Instagram account and FIFA's website, Infantino addresses those who were "so consumed by hate and criticism" that they "missed watching kids, babies, grandparents, and parents come together for the beautiful game" at "the best show in the world".

In words that echo his ally Trump, he notes there was "zero incidents, zero hostility, zero violence, just joy, emotions, happiness, unity, and togetherness" and that "virtually all global celebrities from music, movies, entertainment, and sports attended".

View 3 Images Donald Trump admitted interfering in the process around Folarin Balogun's red card (Image: Alex Pantling/FIFA via Getty Images)

‌



The head of football's governing body, who Trump has put forward as the next head of the United Nations, then attempts to whitewash various controversies. He claims "Iran entered the United States without incident or conflict" and that "countries facing serious health issues or other challenges were granted visas".

He adds: "You mentioned the few people denied visas and overlooked the millions who were approved, from all parts of the world. Because football unites the world, and it was demonstrated impressively this summer."

Infantino then appears justify the overturning of Balogun's red card as the sort of thing that happens routinely in other leagues.

‌



View 3 Images Iran had to base themselves in Mexico, despite playing all three group games in the US (Image: Jamie Squire, Getty Images)

He writes: "Your dissatisfaction with a few decisions made by the competent authorities is understandable, but please refer to public records: such decisions are common in some of the most important leagues.

"Indeed, 'arguable' referees' decisions or 'strange' disciplinary rulings such as for instance potentially mistaken red or yellow cards or subsequent decisions not to ban players in certain situations are routine and widely accepted in some of the biggest leagues worldwide. It's curious that the same countries employing these practices are the ones criticising."

‌



He then concludes with a message to his haters: "To the pens and papers, to all the screens, may you find love and peace where the people behind you couldn't.

"May you find peace; we at FIFA have found ours and we deliver it, by delivering the most outstanding FIFA World Cup. May football rise above all hate."

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Barcola makes call on forcing transfer as new signing ruled out for the season
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Barcola makes call on forcing transfer as new signing ruled out for the season

Liverpool have received a major update in their transfer chase to sign's PSG and France star Bradley Barcola

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola reportedly will not force an exit from PSG as Liverpool hope to snap up his signing (Image: Getty Images)

Andoni Iraola's first summer transfer window at Liverpool has been a mixed bag thus far but looks like it's set to heat up significantly. And the saga surrounding Paris Saint-Germain forward Bradley Barcola in particular has taken on a new form of late.

‌



The Reds are still heavily invested in sourcing a successor to Mohamed Salah following his exit ahead of schedule this summer. Victor Munoz's £34million arrival from Osasuna has helped replenish the ranks, though more business is widely expected at Anfield.

‌



There's less welcome news on the transfer front after one of this summer's fresh signings has been told he can't play this season. Mirror Football addresses all that in more detail as the Reds continue their pre-season tour of the United States.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Barcola 'won't force PSG exit'

Despite the promise of a Premier League move on the other side, France winger Barcola seemingly won't push his luck at PSG. It emerged on Sunday the 23-year-old has told his current employers he has no intention of signing a new contract at the Parc des Princes.

Liverpool sent strong Michael Olise transfer warning by Bayern Munich chief READ MORE :

Liverpool and Arsenal alerted after Bradley Barcola transfer call as PSG seek record fee READ MORE :

That seemingly applies beyond this summer after he rejected PSG's latest offering of fresh contract talks. And the current state of play certainly ramps up the pressure on his club to consider a sale if they're to maximise his sale.

‌



Le Parisien has reported Barcola "will not force a move" from his home of the past three years. Further to that, it's not even clear if he has his heart set on leaving this summer, just that he's not interested in extending his current terms.

It's also alleged Barcola has already turned down an approach from Chelsea earlier this summer. And that too could bode well for the Reds, possibly hinting Barcola has a specific destination in mind.

In a way, Liverpool can only commend the player's resolve if Le Parisien's claims are true. Too often is it considered a straightforward get-out-of-jail card for a player to simply down their tools in a bid to land their desired transfer.

It may complicate things on Liverpool's end as one of their preferred choices to replace Mohamed Salah may prove even more difficult to recruit as a result. However, it suggests the former Lyon youngster is a man of principles as he seemingly won't pull any old trick to get a move.

Ndukwe can't play for Liverpool

After being rocked by Joe Gomez's latest injury setback in pre-season, Liverpool's defence has suffered another hit. That's after reports confirmed summer arrival Ifeanyi Ndukwe won't be able to play for Iraola this term.

The 18-year-old's £2.6m move from Austria Wien was confirmed in January but didn't officially go through until July. However, it may not be long before Ndukwe is heading back out of the exit if he's not allowed represent the Reds.

It's been confirmed Ndukwe hasn't met the threshold to obtain a work permit in the UK. In turn, a loan elsewhere looks all but inevitable for the teenager so that he can attain the necessary experience and become a viable option in the near future.

The development is a particularly damaging one in light of Gomez's injury, with fellow new signing Jeremy jacquet yet to make his debut and youngster Giovanni Leoni on his way back from a serious knee injury. The news also comes in the wake of Ibrahima Konate's free transfer to Real Madrid as Iraola looks to reshape Liverpool's backline this summer.

Manchester United continue to push for more transfers this summer ahead of the upcoming Premier League season

View 3 Images Manu Kone could be on his way to Old Trafford this summer (Image: Johnny Fidelin/Icon Sport via Getty Images)

Manchester United are pushing for more reinforcements as they continue their pre-season tour of Europe. Michael Carrick has welcomed Youri Tielemans, Karl Darlow and Andrey Santos to Old Trafford.

The United boss needs to build a squad capable of competing domestically and in the Champions League. Paris Saint-Germain are next up for the Red Devils before Leeds and then a reunion with Ruben Amorim against AC Milan.

Carrick could have another transfer through the door before the next fixture as Manu Kone has reportedly agreed personal terms to head to Old Trafford. And another target in Carlos Baleba is desperate to join him as the Brighton star explores the possibility of a United move.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Big Vinicius Jr transfer update as target tries to force move
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Big Vinicius Jr transfer update as target tries to force move

Arsenal transfer latest as Mikel Arteta chases Vinicius Jr

View 3 Images Vinicius Jr is set for key talks over his future (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal's summer business has been completely overshadowed after it emerged they are exploring an audacious bid to sign Vinicius Jr from Real Madrid. The Gunners' interest in the Brazil international, who has one year remaining on his contract, is genuine.

‌



It is believed that a move for Vinicius – who scored 22 times for Real last season and netted four goals at the World Cup – is in its very formative stages as Mikel Arteta looks to land a marquee signing to build on the club's first Premier League title in more than two decades.

‌



The 26-year-old fits that bill, with Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez, RB Leipzig's Yan Diomande and Bradley Barcola of Paris Saint-Germain also on their radar.

‌



Arsenal have already bolstered their attacking options with the £34million signing of Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge but landing Vinicius would blow their other dealings out of the water. Here's a round-up of the latest Gunners transfer news…

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Vinicius' stance

Amid the excitement among Arsenal fans, it has emerged that Vinicius is still leaning towards staying with Real Madrid, despite his contract impasse with the club.

‌



Spanish media share Vinicius Jr to Arsenal transfer truth and if deal will happen READ MORE :

Vinicius has just a year remaining on his current deal and Los Blancos are desperate to avoid losing him for nothing next summer. According to Spanish media, he is asking for an increase that would take his wages to around £17m net per year.

According to AS, talks between player and club will resume in days once he returns from his post-World Cup break. Vinicius and his team want clarity on two key issues: where he fits into returning boss Jose Mourinho's plans and whether he can secure a salary that reflects his global status in the game.

View 3 Images Vinicius Jr is being linked with a sensational move to Arsenal (Image: Lars Baron/Getty Images)

‌



Mourinho, who has signed a three-year deal at the Bernabeu, was criticised for comments he made after Vinicius accused Benfica's Gianluca Prestianni of racially abusing him during a Champions League tie in February.

But Mourinho, who was Benfica's manager at the time, reportedly wants Vinicius and the club's other top stars to stay. AS says the intention of both sides is to agree a new deal, despite the Gunners' interest.

View 3 Images Bradley Barcola is pushing to leave PSG (Image: Getty)

‌



Barcola wants out

Barcola has told PSG he will not be signing a new contract amid Arsenal's interest in the France World Cup star.

Barcola has been key to PSG's success in recent seasons but could fall down the pecking order as Luis Enrique looks to revamp his forward line, which could see them sign the in-demand Diomande.

Whether PSG win the race to sign Diomande or not, it appears Barcola wants out, having told the club he has no intention of extending his contract. The 23-year-old's deal with the European champions has two years left to run.

Analysis: Vinicius Jr would be jaw-dropping signing for Arsenal

Image: Brazil's Vinicius Junior celebrates after opening the scoring in Miami (AP Photo/Lynne Sladky)

Sky Sports' Peter Smith:

"It's well known Arsenal are aiming to strengthen their left-wing options this summer - but a deal for Brazil ace Vinicius Jr would be a jaw-dropping addition.

Image: Vinicius Jr's stats from last season at Real Madrid

"However, it is understood the player and head coach have been in touch since an incident last season which saw Vinicius Jr abused by Mourinho's Benfica midfielder Gianluca Prestianni and that the pair were ready to start this new campaign together with a clean slate.

"But with Arsenal's interest being reported, there is now the possibility Vinicius Jnr will be kicking off the 206/27 season in the Premier League.

"It's a thrilling thought for Arsenal fans and neutrals on these shores - but a worrying one for the Gunners' title rivals."

Are Vinicius Jr's wage demands too much for Arsenal?

Spanish football expert Terry Gibson on Sky Sports News:

"Vinicius Jr is currently on 15m Euros a year net.

"Real Madrid have offered him 20m Euros. He wants 30m Euros - just over 550,000 Euros a week net.

"There's no budging on the contract from Real Madrid or Vinicius. Real Madrid are looking at a potential replacement in Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig. This [contract situation] has been ongoing for 18 months.

"But when you put those figures in the melting pot, it's hard to imagine Arsenal or anybody in the Premier League matching those sums of money."

Sports.title: Nelson: Fury vs AJ excites me more than ever and Fury has the edge
Sports.content:
This fight excites me more than it ever has, and I think Tyson Fury has the edge.

Listen, I'm an AJ fan, but it comes down to what we saw this weekend.

The shots that caught Joshua on Saturday, that sneaky little uppercut on the inside, the one that caught him again, those are natural shots for Tyson Fury.

Heart, determination, desire and want, I put all of that in Joshua's corner. But on Saturday's performance, and on Friday's, it's Fury for me.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Anthony Joshua’s comeback bout with Kristian Prenga as the former world heavyweight champion returns to winning ways to set up a blockbuster all-British showdown with Tyson Fury (Courtesy of DAZN)

And believe me, it takes something for me to say that, because if I'm honest with you, I never thought we'd see Anthony Joshua in the ring again.

I thought it would take him so long to get over what happened emotionally, mentally, spiritually. I think being in the ring, being in the gym training, is probably what has kept him on the path of trying to get himself right again.

Watching him on Saturday, you could still see it bubbling over the top, still see a guy struggling to come to terms with something most people will never experience. It put a lump in my throat.

Just to get in the ring alone was an amazing feat and hats off to him for that.

Then the first round happened, and I thought what most people thought, "he's gone, his punch resistance has gone".

But then it was a case of "Oh my goodness, this fight is going to be so exciting".

He was hit, he was hurt, he looked vulnerable. Nigel Benn looked vulnerable too and he was a dangerous fighter every time he got in a ring.

Joshua is not the fighter he was, but that vulnerability is exactly what will make the Fury fight such compelling viewing.

Are both fighters ready to face each other?

Image: Johnny Nelson believes Tyson Fury will have too much for Anthony Joshua

The risk is clear if they don't fight each other soon; look at Saturday night. So it has to be their next fight.

Prenga has a knockout record - he can hit and he can hurt – but he shouldn't have been in Anthony Joshua's league, point blank.

There's a word for AJ, though... mercurial.

He has so much talent but it's a case of which version of Anthony Joshua turns up.

The talented fighter we know wasn't there in Jeddah. The guts and the heart were, because after 20 seconds he was down and had to get back up again.

But he was still making rookie mistakes, and you just shouldn't be making those mistakes at this stage of your career.

You've got to give him a pass, though, because remember what he's coming from.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player An emotional Anthony Joshua dedicates his win over Kristian Prenga to his late friends who died in December's car crash (Courtesy of DAZN)

Boxing for him isn't about the money. I think it's about creating some kind of stability inside himself.

They were boys when this started and they're men now. They've had the losses and they've had the highs, and they need each other to bring the best out of each other.

That's why, even with both men past their best, it's even more exciting now.

The fight won't begin when the first bell goes. It begins in the build-up, in the gamesmanship, in how one fighter gets into the head of the other.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Spencer Brown says Tyson Fury's presence at ringside for Joshua v Prenga was never discussed and he's not convinced AJ will be in favour of fighting The Gypsy King in New York

Where should the fight take place?

Of course it has to take place in the UK, I just don't think it will.

They can make as much noise as they want, and we want it here. I think this is going stateside because that's where the audience is and that's where the paymaster realistically wants it as well.

Imagine being a fan in November at Wembley, up in the tier seats, freezing cold, waiting for a 2am first bell. I understand historically it should be here but I personally think it'll end up in America.

Either way, this fight is five years behind. We've always wanted to see it, so whatever we get from both fighters, we're going to make the most of it.

Sports.title: Amazonian Dream looks to go back-to-back at Windsor
Sports.content:
We have a busy day’s racing on Monday with flat action from Ripon, Southwell and Windsor, live on Sky Sports Racing...

7.28 Windsor - Course specialist Amazonian Dream headlines

Amazonian Dream headlines a field of 14 in a competitive Fitzdares Sprint Series Handicap.

The in-form Rod Milman stable turn out course specialist Amazonian Dream just one week after his first win since 2024.

He is up five pounds for that success and moves up in grade, however, the manner in which he won suggests he can remain competitive.

The very lightly-raced Regional Rock heads the opposition as he looks to go one better when narrowly going down by a neck at Doncaster last time out.

Sudden Flight has resumed his progress with newly fitted cheekpiece. He can challenge, aiming to get off the mark for the season.

3.00 Southwell - Impressive Frankel colt Sharp Move and Gregory's half-brother, Humphrey clash

Exciting, lightly raced four-year-old Sharp Move makes his highly anticipated return as he clashes with Humphrey in the First Aid Training Novice Stakes.

This Frankel colt put his debut well behind him when scoring by seven lengths at Newcastle last November, making him just about the one to beat with the potential to prove highly progressive at four.

However, Sharp Move faces stiff opposition from race-fit, well-bred, and unexposed types. Humphrey was beaten at odds-on when looking much too green during his Sandown run last time.

He is a half-brother to Royal Ascot winner Gregory and likely has much more to offer with a run under his belt.

Kingman colt Turrent knuckled down well to win at Carlisle last month with the second coming out and winning well, as Wootton Bassett-colt Kokbastau was notably eye-catching on reappearance at Yarmouth. He can put that experience to good use here.

8.10 Ripon - Masked Warrior faces five in a trappy affair

The lightly raced Masked Warrior opposes five in a trappy renewal of the City of Ripon Handicap.

The William Haggas-trained three-year-old sets the standard having won impressively at Kempton, before finishing a creditable third in a competitive class two handicap at Chester.

He looks to capitalise now dropped in grade, but faces opposition in the form of the revitalised Beyond The Bar who bounced back when winning nicely at Catterick last time out.

Wathnan-owned Enchant could make marked improvement up in trip on handicap debut, as the unexposed Noelan Star should put his Royal Ascot blip behind him to prove relatively well treated off a mark of 90.

Sports.title: Rising star Koivun holds off Scheffler to win on third PGA Tour start as a pro
Sports.content:
Jackson Koivun held off a charge from world No 1 Scottie Scheffler to win his first PGA Tour title in just his third start as a professional as he triumphed by three strokes at the 3M Open in Minnesota.

The 21-year-old's final-round, five-under 66 came after Scheffler - looking for his first title since the American Express back in January - applied the pressure with an eight-under 63 to post the clubhouse score at 22 under par.

Koivun had carved out a three-shot lead over Emiliano Grillo and Ben Kohles after round three following a stunning, bogeyless 10-under 61 that included two eagles and four birdies on an eight-under back nine.

Image: Scottie Scheffler's eight-under 63 came in vain on Sunday as he finished three shots adrift of Koivun

The youngster's Sunday was not as dramatic but he kept his cool to complete victory, securing the 3M Open scoring record of 25 under par in the process as he finished a blemish-free weekend with a par.

Koivun, who had made 10 starts as an amateur on the tour, turned professional after the US Open in June and missed the cut in his first event - the John Deere Classic - before finishing tied-10th at the Isco Championship.

He made 24 birdies, those two Saturday eagles and just three bogeys all week at TPC Twin Cities during a performance that hinted at an extremely bright future and also pushed him up 124 spots in the FedExCup standings to 70th, the final play-off berth with two regular events remaining.

Image: Jackson Koivun's remarkable start eclipses the game's greats

Koivun: Golf was love at first sight

He said afterwards: "I played a great round of golf. I definitely had some nerves coming down 18.

"I heard the crowd saying, 'Scottie's coming, Scottie's coming' but I just tried to blank that out and play the golf I knew I could. I was able to find some good putts down the stretch.

Image: Koivun won his first PGA Tour title at the age of just 21

"I love this game, it's everything I do. It was love at first sight and I just want to say thanks to my parents for getting me into this and supporting me on my entire journey."

'Houdini chipper Koivun will make it to the top'

Sky Sports' Simon Holmes on Jackson Koivun:

Image: Koivun made just three bogeys throughout the week, all in his second round

"He is turbocharged and ready to perform immediately. He has presence in front of the camera and media. This guy is going to create a lot of fans.

"If you look at some of the talent th.at has come through that college system - Jordan Spieth, Collin Morikawa and Viktor Hovland - you'd say he is at least on a par with all of those players. But there is something in him that sets him apart from that group.

"Spieth had amazing putting but not a great driver. Morikawa, similar, amazing irons.

"With Koivun, you say driver, fantastic - he can play golf from the middle of the fairway. Iron control, amazing. Can he chip? Absolutely, he is a [Harry] Houdini.

"The best parts of his game are his putting and his mindset. He sees himself reaching the top of the pyramid - that is the outcome he expects.

"Let's see him make that journey. It's going to happen."

Sports.title: Craig Overton wins battle with brother Jamie in entertaining Hundred finish
Sports.content:
Craig Overton won his one-on-one battle with twin brother Jamie as Trent Rockets beat London Spirit by four wickets with two balls to spare in The Hundred.

Rockets needed 10 runs from the final five deliveries at Trent Bridge on Sunday night with Craig batting for the hosts and Jamie bowling for the visitors.

Craig (20no off six) earned bragging rights, and four points for his team, by top-edging Jamie for six over deep fine leg and then picking up successive twos to take Rockets to their target of 160, after Ben Duckett had spanked an excellent 75 off 47 balls up top.

Image: The Overton twins shake hands after Sunday evening's match at Trent Bridge

Craig Overton's six-two-two off his sibling had mirrored his efforts off Andrew Tye across the previous three deliveries with a maximum over long-on followed by a brace of two-run hauls, exploits that helped Rockets to a first win of 2026 and condemned Spirit to successive defeats.

Earlier in the game, Overton had caught and bowled Spirit opener Jonny Bairstow for a duck and also dismissed South African biffer Lhuan-dré Pretorius for 24.

Pretorius' compatriot Dewald Brevis top-scored with 39 from 24 balls in Spirit's 159-9, while captain Liam Livingstone contributed 33 off 24 deliveries.

Buttler blasts Super Giants to back-to-back wins

Elsewhere, Jos Buttler cracked 90 from 50 balls as Manchester Super Giants hammered Birmingham Phoenix by 87 runs to join Welsh Fire in winning their first two matches.

Buttler's knock at Emirates Old Trafford, which featured seven fours and five sixes and helped Super Giants post 187-5, was only 10 runs fewer than Phoenix managed as an entire team, with the visitors bundled out for 100 as Liam Dawson claimed 3-15.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch all of Jos Butler's sixes in Manchester Super Giants' win over Birmingham Phoenix

The hosts backed up their narrow seven-run win over Spirit at Lord's on Thursday, while Phoenix slipped to a first loss having edged Rockets by 10 runs in a high-scoring clash at Edgbaston on Friday.

Buttler was supported by Tom Moores' 39 not out off 17, which included five maximums, but Phoenix's batting did not fire at all in the chase, with skipper Donovan Ferreria (23) top-scoring.

Image: Super Giants seamer Josh Tongue celebrates the wicket of Phoenix's Rehan Ahmed

England pacer Josh Tongue struck twice in two balls to rock Phoenix early on, inflicting a golden duck on Rehan Ahmed, and the Midlanders never really recovered.

England quick Sonny Baker and Afghanistan spinner Noor Ahmad also bagged two wickets for Super Giants, who look to have a potent all-round attack.

What is happening in The Hundred on Monday?

After the four-games-a-day set-up at the weekend, Monday sees a return to a single double-header with Southern Brave's women's side hosting MI London from 3pm before the men's sides square off from 6.30pm. Catch both fixtures live on Sky Sports.

Sports.title: Are the Big Six raiding the rest of the Premier League?
Sports.content:
What do Elliot Anderson, Morgan Rogers and Sandro Tonali have in common?

All three made moves for £100m or more this summer - but they also follow a growing trend where 'Big Six' clubs - defined as Arsenal, Manchester City, Liverpool, Manchester United, Chelsea and Spurs - sign players from their non-Big Six Premier League rivals.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on the Transfer Talk Podcast, Henry Winter and Keith Downie discuss the importance of Bruno Guimaraes to Newcastle and how much he's worth to the club

So, how much are the league's powerhouse clubs spending on players from other teams in the top flight?

Since summer 2016, Big Six clubs have spent £2.8bn on players from non-Big Six Premier League rivals. The trend has accelerated sharply: £647m last season was the highest in history, and the total already stands at £420m this summer.

Sports.title: In-form Herbert breaks LIV Golf record with win in UK
Sports.content:
Australia's Lucas Herbert followed an impressive showing at last week's Open at Royal Birkdale with a record-setting victory at the LIV Golf UK event in Staffordshire.

Herbert, who finished tied for sixth in the final men's major of the year, four shots adrift of champion Ryan Fox, romped to the LIV trophy in Rocester with a score of 30 under par.

That was the lowest winning score since the circuit was established in 2022 and left the 30-year-old six strokes clear of Tyrrell Hatton and nine in front of Bryson DeChambeau.

Image: Herbert's win was his second on LIV in 2026, after May's event in Virginia

Herbert also set the LIV record for most birdies in a tournament (30) and most combined birdies and eagles (32) after a 10-under, blemish-free 62 on Sunday.

He had begun the event with an 11-under 61 that contained 10 birdies and an eagle and his worst round all week was a three-under 69 on Saturday.

Herbert shot an eight-under 62 in the second round of the Open earlier this month and said after his victory at Rocester, his second of the LIV season after triumphing in Virginia in May: "I just wanted to carry that into this week the best I could.

"It was good to play like that today when I was being pushed by two of the best players in the world."

Hatton carded a nine under 63 on Sunday and said: "I wanted to get off to a fast start, which I did, but unfortunately Lucas did as well.

"It would have been amazing to win in front of home fans, but I tried my best. Lucas was incredible this week."

Sports.title: Real Madrid ready to seal deal for Yan Diomande after PSG pull out of move
Sports.content:
Real Madrid look to have won the race for RB Leipzig’s coveted winger, Yan Diomande, after Paris Saint-Germain withdrew from the bidding war.

The Ivory Coast international has been the subject of an intense transfer saga this summer, following a breakout season in the Bundesliga and an impressive World Cup campaign.

The 19-year-old was linked with a move with Liverpool early in the window, before the player’s camp revealed he would instead prioritise a switch to Paris. However, with Real now moving ahead of PSG, Diomande looks set for the Bernabéu with the reported fee “well in excess” of €100m (£85m).

The breakthrough comes just days after Leipzig rejected Madrid’s opening proposal of €90m plus €10m in add-ons. Diomande, who has reportedly already agreed personal terms with Real, is now expected to fly to the Spanish capital for a medical.

The deal will come as a blow for PSG, who looked to be the frontrunners, with many reports suggesting they were his first choice if he did leave Germany. However, the European champions were unable to agree a fee and issued a statement on Sunday insisting they will not break their “principles”.

The statement read: “Paris Saint-Germain has this evening formally withdrawn its interest in and bids for Yan Diomande. PSG will not break its principles of rational financial management and squad balance.”

Meanwhile, Liverpool have turned their attention to PSG’s Bradley Barcola as they continue to search for wingers.

Sports.title: Teamwork, tactics and data: behind the scenes at Wigan’s pre-season training
Sports.content:
“This is the only rule I’m going to have for yous all season: ‘team first’,” says Gary Caldwell. The Wigan head coach’s Scottish accent booms over the gentle hum of a projector in a darkened classroom at the club’s Christopher Park training ground. “That is the one thing that we cannot ever go against,” he says, pointing to a slide on screen. “The team is the most important aspect of everything we do.”

Three rows of professional athletes listen intently, keen to learn not only what the day holds, but about the 10 months ahead.

Some shall see it through to next May, others may leave before the 2026-27 League One campaign begins on 14 August, and new faces will be added.

It is pre-season and before the interminable football carousel begins spinning, there is much work ahead.

View image in fullscreen Gary Caldwell talks tactics with his squad. Photograph: Dom Maltby/The Guardian

The meeting is short, just long enough for Caldwell to zip through a handful of tactical points. As he speaks, the head of performance analysis, Lauren Jones, plays clips from their “best practice bank”.

Because she, Caldwell, and the first-team coach, David Perkins, joined from Exeter only in February (the physio, Michael McBride, and goalkeeping coach, Kevin Miller, followed this summer), the bank is small, but growing.

There are myriad general football clips that Caldwell could use, but he values “the lads seeing players in Wigan shirts doing what we’re asking of them”.

Perkins relays the day’s plan – a 1.5km time trial, several drills, some out-of-possession shape work and an afternoon weights session – before the class is dismissed and told to reassemble on the grass 45 minutes later.

There is no idling, though, the entire squad soon beginning self‑led pre-activation (in old money, warming up).

Bodies are strewn across the in-house gym with bands, benches and foam rollers used as aids to contort muscles and limbs.

Wigan’s facility is, by modern standards, modest but functional. A printed sign sets out the simple rules: £50 fines for anyone with a phone, wearing sliders or sulking.

When the centre-back James Carragher discovers the Guardian will be joining the morning’s run, a sanction of double that amount is declared should anyone not beat the guest journalist. At 10.55am, the strength and conditioning lead, Matthew Barrow, explains that the run consists of 15 pitch lengths with 14 turns. “Your choice lads – boots or trainers, but I recommend boots so you don’t lose time on the turn.”

“I’m glad I’m not doing it,” Caldwell says, laughing. “It’s a maximal test and anything like that involves people pushing themselves.”

Could you survive a professional football pre-season fitness test? – video

It is not the squad’s first testing of pre-season. Their first day back involved a series of body and strength tests “designed to provide us with a benchmark”, Caldwell says. “If they get injured, we know where we need to get them back to.”

But the days of players reporting back overweight are long gone, with only a small number a smidge above their optimum numbers during body composition testing. “That will all have been gone with the first week or so,” Caldwell says.

Running for running’s sake is also past practice. Instead, Barrow and the sports scientist Jack Craigie will use the run data to get each individual’s maximum aerobic speed. “From that, we individualise all the running they’ll do,” Craigie says. “For example, if we have a volume session planned, rather than giving a generic number of lengths, we set individual distances based on their results. That way they all get the same stimulus.”

By 11am, the players are jogging through a warm-up lap. According to the sign-in sheet outside the staff offices, some arrived on site three hours ago. The physio hub just off the gym has had a steady stream of visitors, a mix of prevention and cure. Breakfast was enjoyed in a canteen acting as a social space for staff and players.

It marks a leisurely start when measured against some mornings. With no tour plans, Caldwell is finding alternative ways to avoid monotony. Several 6am meets precede 3.5km runs to a partner gym for intense, Hyrox-style workouts. With players working in trios, staff are as interested in attitude and demeanour as fitness.

View image in fullscreen The players take part in various training drills. Photograph: Dom Maltby/The Guardian

“We’re taking the group out of their comfort zone to see how they react under a bit of pressure,” Caldwell says. “We can look at the energy someone brings at 6am when others are tired. That will help us know who is going to pick the group up when we’re a little fatigued.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Those sessions also promote Caldwell’s “team first” ethos. “When you’re ‘off’ you still have a role to play,” he says. “Are you helping your pal get in and out of the straps on the rower more quickly? We want to see how they react in that situation. Come November, when it is cold and we’re struggling in a game, we can remind them of these sessions.”

A late-morning run feels tame by comparison, albeit after several pitch lengths that naive notion is dispelled. No one loses £100 to the club kitty.

Soon the footballs are out and the group is split into two groups for a series of drills. The energy is impressive, with Max Power, who recently rejoined Wigan for a third spell, among the tone setters.

In one exercise he encourages a junior teammate to make a pass, only for a defender to block the space. Rather than get frustrated or dish out abuse, Power immediately finds another opportunity to tee up a similar ball and praises a successful outcome. “The better the player, the less stick they give people, I find,” says one staff member. “They want everyone to improve.”

The staff’s challenge is to manage the intensity, building towards a peak. Caldwell avoids directly asking players to hold back, but with a drone monitoring everything and GPS data available in real time, sessions can be adjusted accordingly. Sometimes it is as simple as moving cones in a few yards.

For one drill, tape on the grass creates a dozen boxes, within which three banks of four must work to create and find gaps. “Football is sometimes about the chaos,” Caldwell says, grinning. “If we give them more space, they will use it.”

View image in fullscreen Wigan use the in-house gym during a break from the action on the pitch. Photograph: Dom Maltby/The Guardian

Building towards a peak is also Wigan’s aim. Supporters want a return to the relatively recent success, which is natural after eight seasons as an established Premier League side. That ended in 2013 – the year they lifted the FA Cup at Wembley with Caldwell in the squad.

Four Championship relegations and three League One promotions have followed, including in Caldwell’s first full season in management. That was 2015-16 and the third-tier title was claimed.

Caldwell’s immediate challenge last season was avoiding relegation from League One, and patience is required for the next step.

After lunch, the day concludes in the gym with a short, sharp, upper body strength session. In one corner, pull-ups, in another perfectly formed jackknives.

“Once the season begins, training loads are consistent around games,” Barrow says. “But with the time in here now we can really chase that hypertrophy.”

Pre-season was once, in effect, punishment for a summer well enjoyed, but in 2026 is a meticulous, data-driven, foundation-building exercise.

The payoff will become known only next May.
