Sports.title: How the death of Jayden Adams shook a community: ‘Being on the pitch was his happy place’
Sports.content:
For Jayden Adams, the South Africa midfielder who died this month at the age of 25, football was a “safe space”. Those words, used by Adams’s junior coach Steve Barker at his memorial service 10 days ago, tell you everything you need to know about his life beyond the pitch.

Adams’s battles were bestowed on him almost from birth. Though he was born into newly democratic South Africa, by the early 2000s the revolution was well on its way to being betrayed. The vote was extended to all, but few could make full use of the freedoms available to them because socioeconomic circumstances in the country had barely changed. Stellenbosch, where the Adams family were based, is a perfect example.

Its facade is a tourist dream: a university town nestled among vineyards, Cape Dutch architecture and indie boutiques. Most visitors never venture beyond the town centre or into its suburbs, which are home to the far less privileged and are havens of neglect. Those areas are classic apartheid hangovers, where the wealth has been preserved for a historically advantaged elite and those on the margins, working-class communities of people of colour, are all but invisible.

Ironically, that is how Adams is most often described. He moved in the shadows, both of society and the sport in which he excelled. “Jayden was a guy of very few words. He was quiet, very shy and the smallest among his teammates,” Brendine Johnson, an Adams family spokesperson, says. “Initially, a lot of people missed his football qualities because of his size, but he had a very good fighting spirit. It just wasn’t always on display.”

Adams loved the game dearly and his aunt Monica Thaoge recalled how, as a child, he would kick anything round – “even onions” she said at his memorial. His parents, Juanito and Candice, previously mentioned potatoes as their son’s football of choice. Nobody in the family talks about lacking in financial means because theirs was a community striving to make life better. But there were absences, especially early on.

View image in fullscreen Members of the Mamelodi Sundowns football club carry Jayden Adams’ coffin at the funeral service for the player on Saturday. Photograph: Esa Alexander/Reuters

“Everybody in areas like that is just trying to make ends meet,” says Roger Telemachus, the former South Africa cricketer who grew up on the same street as Adams’s father in Cloetesville. “For the kids, they may not have noticed so much because they were occupied, mostly with playing sport. Some fathers, like Juanito, really encouraged their kids and everyone used to play everything on the street: tennis, football, rugby, cricket. It was also the best way of staying out of trouble.”

Problems were there for everyone to see and, according to Telemachus, have got worse “in the last 20 years”. They include gangsterism, substance abuse and crimes that range from petty to serious. Adams was able to escape from that life when he moved to the slightly more affluent area of Ida’s Valley, but still he did not have a life of luxury. For a period, the family of six, which included four children, lived in a two-bedroom place. At other times, they were with his maternal grandmother, Marianna. “He basically grew up in her yard,” says Johnson.

Things started to change for Adams when he was picked for the Stellenbosch Academy Under-18 side at the age of 15. “The environment was tough, especially if you are not big or tall enough, but when physicality was no longer the most important thing, people saw that Jayden was technically very good,” says Johnson.

His coaches agree. Barker, the nephew of South Africa’s Afcon winning coach, Clive, and the current coach of Simba in Tanzania, gave an emotional assessment of Adams’s skills shortly after his death. “You get many good footballers but you get few great footballers. Jayden was great,” he told Newzroom Afrika.

“Jayden had three attributes that set him apart: an incredible first touch, his weight of pass – I’ve never seen anything like it – and he loved the game so much. Being on the pitch was his happy place. He didn’t pass the ball, he used to caress the ball. He was special and his football intelligence was just outstanding.”

View image in fullscreen Jayden Adams played in South Africa’s World Cup group game against Czechia despite the death of his grandmother the day before. Photograph: Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire/Getty Images

It was under Barker that Adams blossomed. He became the first player from the Stellenbosch Academy to play in South Africa’s top flight, the Premier Soccer League. Five years and an international call up later, the country’s richest club, Mamelodi Sundowns, came calling. This year, at the start of his second season with them, Adams shaved his head, in what he joked was a sign of maturity and called himself a “grootman” (big man). The nickname stuck.

Adams never said it, but he may also have realised how much he had grown up. By then, he had been picked, played for and dropped from the national side after arriving late at a training camp and irking the head coach, Hugo Broos. He had also lost two of his academy teammates, including a close friend.

In February 2023, Oshwin Andries, who was 19, died from stabbing injuries he sustained in Paarl, which is 16km north of Stellenbosch. Three years later, Jeandre Gaffoor, 20, drowned in the Krom River.

When Sundowns won the CAF Champions League in May, Adams dedicated his medal to Andries. To lose so much has weighed on the town, but through Adams they have had reason to celebrate.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Fortnightly Sign up to The Hotspot A new fortnightly newsletter covering the intersection of sport and the climate crisis Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Members of Adams’s family, including his father, Juanito (centre left), and mother, Candice (centre right), at his memorial service last week. Photograph: Rodger Bosch/AFP/Getty Images

His role in Sundowns’ continental victory and a call-up to the World Cup squad suggested Adams’s career trajectory was rising. After a first season at Sundowns when he was often playing off the bench and his place in the side was questioned, he had become integral to the team. At Adams’s memorial, the Sundowns senior coach, Steve Komphela, called him “the heart of our team and the heartbeat of our playing style” who “understood the game like a coach and played it as a player”.

In the past year, Adams was playing to the potential people who knew him well had seen years ago and surprising others with his courage and drive to succeed. South Africa’s captain, Ronwen Williams, recalled an incident at this year’s Africa Cup of Nations when the tiny Adams took on a tall Mali opponent with some choice local words. Williams asked Adams if he knew the size of the player he was sledging, but Adams shrugged it off and replied that the Malian wouldn’t understand anyway.

“That was the character he had,” Williams said at the memorial, smiling through his tears as he bade farewell to the teammate he called “my ma se kind” (my mother’s child, a term of endearment used in South Africa).

As his star rose, Adams was careful not to advertise his achievements. “Jayden knew what he had, but he never wanted to voice it. He was very competitive, but he would never brag,” says Johnson. “You get people who are very good verbally on social media. Jayden was not like that. And he wanted to give back. After every game, he would be giving away shirts and boots to kids who asked.”

He also concentrated on providing for his family because he “always promised them he would change their financial situation”.

View image in fullscreen Jayden Adams signs a South Africa shirt for a young Mexican fan who arrived at the team’s World Cup hotel. ‘He wanted to give back.’ Photograph: SAFA

At the World Cup, Adams played for them, even through immense pain. His grandmother Marianna died the day before South Africa’s match against Czechia and Adams opted to remain with the squad. He played that match and appeared in good spirits afterwards and called the 1-1 draw positive, even if he was feeling the opposite way.

He also played the next game against South Korea, which South Africa won to reach the knockouts for the first time. Post-game footage showed him sitting on his own while the rest of the squad celebrated with a signature song and dance.

At the memorial, Komphela offered the Adams family a Bible verse as a comfort, but it may as well be a summary. Psalm 23:4: “Though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me.”

They will know Adams took that walk many times over his short life and he did not fear. He leaves behind his parents, three siblings, a partner, two children and a community who have gone through what no neighbourhood should. In all that, he has gone from not wanting to be known, to entering the footballing world’s spotlight. A minute’s silence was observed at several World Cup games in Adams’s memory. That is not the way his family would have pictured him coming to global attention, but it has shown them that, in football, he was always far more valued than anyone thought.

“I don’t think the community knew how big he was and how people enjoyed his football,” says Johnson. “It’s a huge shock.”

Sports.title: Chiesa wants ‘new chapter’ with Iraola after frustrating time under Slot at Liverpool
Sports.content:
Federico Chiesa has said he wants “a new chapter” at Liverpool with Andoni Iraola following a frustrating time under Arne Slot and claimed the club were lucky to qualify for the Champions League last season.

The Liverpool forward has been linked with a return to Italy this summer having struggled for minutes during his two years at Anfield. Chiesa made 36 appearances for Slot last season, a healthy return on paper, but only five were starts.

He started one Premier League game last season despite the problems Liverpool had in attack because of injuries to Alexander Isak and Hugo Ekitiké, and his last start came in the FA Cup fourth-round win against Brighton on 14 February. A change of head coach, Chiesa hopes, will herald a change in fortune as a Liverpool player.

“It is always a fresh start at the beginning of the year,” said the 28-year-old, who produced a fine finish in Liverpool’s 4-2 friendly defeat of Sunderland in Nashville on Saturday. “Maybe there have been too many fresh starts [for him]. But I don’t care, I am trying to do my best for this new manager.

“Last season under Arne Slot, I was trying to do my best. Last year I felt ready for a bigger role, then it depended on the coach whether he wanted me to play or not. Of course I wanted to play more but it is what it is. The gaffer had his gameplans, he took his decisions, I have nothing to say about that. It is football. This year, let us say it is a new chapter. There is a new manager and I have to focus on that.”

Chiesa admits he has not discussed his future with Iraola since the Basque coach succeeded Slot in June. “The only conversations I had were about pressing and tactics,” he said. “He put me striker against Sunderland and he wants me there.”

But the Italy international, who has two years remaining on his Liverpool contract, claimed his priority is to prove himself to the head coach rather than seek a return to Serie A. Como and former club Juventus have been linked with a move for the forward.

“Right now, at the moment, I am happy here at Liverpool,” said Chiesa. “I love the club, I love the fans, I love everything. I am doing the best I can to have a chance here. And then we will see. At the minute, the only thing I am thinking about is Liverpool.”

View image in fullscreen Federico Chiesa scored for Liverpool against Sunderland in Nashville on Saturday. Photograph: George Walker IV/AP

Liverpool secured Champions League qualification on the final day of a troubled season in May in what proved to be Slot’s final game in charge. Chiesa insists that was no cause for celebration at a club of Liverpool’s stature and there must be improvement next term.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The forward said: “Liverpool deserves more. Two years ago, we were Premier League champions. Last year, we almost went out of the Champions League spots. We were battling for fifth, which was enough at the time but as we know usually only four go in. We were lucky.

“It was a tough season last year and this season we need to do better, in the Champions League as well. We went out to PSG. We want to go further in that competition and then we want to do even better in the Premier League as well.”

Chiesa also hopes to reclaim his place in the national team next season, having missed out on several squads recently. Italy are now searching for a new head coach, having failed to qualify for the World Cup under Gennaro Gattuso.

Chiesa said: “The situation is that I spoke to the manager a few times, Gattuso, and I was not ready physically at the time. When I got back in March, unfortunately I got injured. But I am looking forward to playing for the national team. I have won with the national team [the European Championship]. It is always nice to play and win for your national team.”

Sports.title: Régis Le Bris says Chelsea’s pursuit of Sunderland captain Xhaka is ‘closed’
Sports.content:
Régis Le Bris has declared Chelsea’s pursuit of Granit Xhaka “closed” and insisted there is no prospect of Sunderland selling their influential captain this summer.

Xhaka played a major role in Sunderland qualifying for the Europa League on their return to the Premier League last season, prompting Chelsea to make an £8m bid for the 33-year-old this month. Xabi Alonso, the new Chelsea manager, is keen to be reunited with his former midfielder at Bayer Leverkusen.

Sunderland, however, immediately rejected Chelsea’s bid and their head coach has emphatically denied that a deal could be revisited before the end of the transfer window.

“No, this topic is closed,” said Le Bris after Sunderland’s 4-2 pre-season friendly defeat by Liverpool in Nashville on Saturday. “He has been really clear about his future. He loves Sunderland, he wants to stay in Sunderland. He wants to make the future of Sunderland. He is a good captain. Great leader.”

Despite the added demands of European football next season Sunderland have been quiet in the transfer market, signing only the experienced Belgium defender Thomas Meunier on a free from Lille so far. Le Bris anticipates further additions but admits this summer will be nothing like the rebuilding work before Sunderland’s return to the top flight 12 months ago.

The Sunderland head coach added: “It’s going to be quiet. Under the radar, right? I won’t give you information. Because I think we are working hard behind the scenes, and it’s really important to be quiet because otherwise it’s a mess. And we are looking at probably a different transfer window if you compare with last season. We had to sign 14 new players. It won’t be the case this year. We’ll see what will happen.”

Sports.title: ‘We want to win the league’: Arsenal’s new recruits ink in WSL success
Sports.content:
Georgia Stanway looks at her arms and then down at her legs on day one of Arsenal’s pre-season. “As you can see, I’m covered in tattoos,” she says. “I only see the bare skin, the space, so I need to keep collecting more.”

Tattooing and being tattooed is her creative outlet, her way of expressing herself off the pitch. But seeing space is key to the 27‑year‑old England midfielder being exceptional on the pitch.

Stanway’s unveiling video, after her move from Bayern Munich, showed a delicate, cursive script reading “whatever the weather” tattooed on her arm. It was a bold statement to get the lyric from North London Forever, Arsenal’s anthem, etched into her skin before she has stepped on to the Emirates Stadium pitch in red and white. “It shows I’m going to give absolutely everything for this club. I want to hit the ground running, play my game, connect with my teammates, connect with the fans and look forward to an exciting future at the club.”

Stanway is emblematic of Arsenal’s summer of change, one of seven signings so far. Meanwhile, Lotte Wubben-Moy, a lifelong fan who joined Arsenal’s academy at 13, represents the core and culture that is a point of focus at the club. It is a culture players want to be a part of, so much so it leads to getting a tattoo on day one of being there. “She has set a very high bar,” says Wubben-Moy, with a grin. “That’s Georgia. She goes all in and I like that.”

Wubben-Moy is ready to stake a claim in Arsenal’s starting XI after struggling to nail down a position in defence despite having performed exceptionally well when covering for injured players. “I’ve always felt ready,” says the 27-year-old. “When I get my moment, I deliver. Historically, as a club, we’re built on defensive solidity. If we have a solid defence, it allows us to create and score. That should be the stepping stone towards victories. So I will continue to contribute to the defensive solidity in whatever way, shape or form that is. But I want my spot.”

View image in fullscreen Lotte Wubben-Moy lifts the Champions Cup trophy during the Arsenal trophy parade in May. Photograph: Alex Burstow/Arsenal FC/Getty Images

There was widespread recognition that Arsenal’s squad needed a revamp, that the age needed to be lowered and changes made if they were going to take the next step. That meant big names leaving, most notably Beth Mead and Katie McCabe. “They’re both absolute legends of the game and we have so much respect for them,” says Jodie Taylor, the former Arsenal striker who became the club’s technical director in January. “But we always knew this window was going to come with some changes.”

“Change is inevitable in women’s football,” says Wubben-Moy. “If you speak to a player and they don’t say they’re nimble, you’ve got someone that’s not built for the game. We’ve become a nimble team, a team that can move with the ebb and flow of women’s football.

View image in fullscreen Beth Mead left in a busy summer for Arsenal. Photograph: Rhianna Chadwick/PA

“That’s not just within the playing group, it’s something replicated within the staff, the boardroom, the commercial team, the comms team. Everyone is so willing to move and to dictate what we want.

“If you’d asked me about change four or five years ago, I’d have been a bit intimidated, but now I know what to do and I’m part of the driver of it. The opportunity we have and that I see for us as a team, as a collective, is something that really excites me.”

Arsenal’s approach to Stanway’s recruitment was a contributing factor to her wanting to join the club. “Arsenal came in early doors,” she says. “I really enjoyed they were super loyal from the beginning and wanted me even when I wasn’t available. It’s a nice feeling being wanted.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“The last four years in Munich were unbelievable, but I knew I wanted to take the next step and I felt at Arsenal there was an opportunity for me to be able to progress, to make my game better and to play with world-class players.”

Arsenal have done most of their business early, with Stanway joined by experienced internationals Selina Cerci, Géraldine Reuteler, Ona Batlle and Misa Rodríguez, as well as young talents Lisa Baum and Isabella Damm. No major international tournament and seven signings in for day one of pre-season is a big boost for Renée Slegers and her coaching staff, particularly after two seasons of slow starts to domestic campaigns.

“The market is not easy, though, it’s constantly changing and the pool of elite talent is small and several clubs are fishing from it,” says Taylor. “You try and plan as much as you can, but you also have to be reactive in the market. We’re always trying to keep an eye on the future, but we have to be quite agile.

“We can talk about positional needs, qualities, ages and succession planning, but if a player’s not available or they just don’t exist, it can be like trying to fit square pegs and round holes. As well as looking at current needs and positional profiles, we talk a lot about our core style of play, but we also want to play with variety, be unpredictable and have different qualities in players too.”

View image in fullscreen Former Arsenal striker Jodie Taylor, now technical director, is leading the strong recruitment this summer. Photograph: Zuma Press/Alamy

The players who have come in have brought energy, says Wubben-Moy, who was on an emotional rollercoaster during Arsenal men’s Premier League and women’s Champions Cup-winning parade, with the bus looping past Highbury Corner, where she filmed her contract renewal video, and past Islington town hall, where she got married to cyclist Tao Geoghegan Hart a few weeks later.

“I like to focus on what they’re entering,” says Wubben-Moy, “which is a culture that has been created by history, by players and staff that are the core of this team and who have all lived through the changes to different degrees: Kelly [Smith], Renée, myself, Leah [Williamson], Kim [Little], Jodie too. We’ve been privy to lots of different things but all of us are holding on to and releasing, in a healthy way, the things we know we need to. It’s efficient, we’re focused, we know what we do next.

“It’s like you’re cooking the most beautiful recipe and then you add the final small ingredients that make the marginal difference, that elevate, and you create something that’s beautiful and that you can relish and enjoy. That’s what we’re in the process of now with a beautiful long pre-season. I’m desperate to get it out of the way so we can then serve what we’re cooking to the fans and be like: ‘Let’s eat and we’ll all eat together for the whole year.’”

The average attendance of more than 34,000 fans for WSL games at the Emirates last season and the club’s pioneering history in women’s football, as well as the Champions League win in 2025, are huge selling points, and all concerned at Arsenal want more, including a first Women’s Super League title since 2019.

“We’re in a great place,” says Taylor. “But we would have liked to have won more trophies last season and that is our huge ambition coming into this year. I’ll flat out say it: we want to win the league. We are an ambitious club and with the signings we’ve made we feel like we’re in a great place to do that.”

Sports.title: Inter enter talks with Tottenham over signing captain Cristian Romero
Sports.content:
Inter have entered talks with Tottenham over the potential signing of Cristian Romero. The Spurs captain helped Argentina reach a second straight World Cup final this month, but could leave this summer for a significant fee after an eventful five-year spell.

The centre-back has made 156 appearances since he joined Tottenham in 2021 and guided the club to Europa League success last year, but served four separate suspensions during a difficult 2025-26 campaign.

With Jan Paul van Hecke signed for £52m from Brighton and Marcos Senesi joining as a free agent in June to boost the defensive options of Roberto De Zerbi’s side, Spurs will let Romero depart and his representatives have been in Milan for talks with Inter this weekend.

Inter’s sporting director, Piero Ausilio, told Sky Italy: “It’s definitely a deal we are trying to sign with the player and the club. These things take some time but there’s definitely interest. Let’s see.”

Sports.title: Arsenal willing to hand Vinicius Jr record contract to seal shock transfer
Sports.content:
Arsenal willing to hand Vinicius Jr record contract to seal shock transfer

Arsenal have the finances in place to make Vinicius Junior their highest-paid player, talkSPORT understands.

Gunners winger Bukayo Saka is the club's top earner with a weekly wage of over £300,000.

2 Saka penned a new five-year deal with Arsenal in February Credit: Getty

However, Vini Jr's mooted wage would gazump Saka's pay packet.

The Brazil star takes home a wage of approximately £246,000-a-week at Real Madrid.

How much is Vini Jr hoping to earn?

But with his contract at Real expiring at the end of the season, Vini Jr is hoping for a bumper increase.

Reports claim the 26-year-old is seeking as much as €550,000 (£470,000).

Despite the eye-watering figure, it would not make him the Premier League's highest-paid player.

Instead, that tag belongs to Manchester City striker Erling Haaland, who signed a new contract in January 2025 that made him the first player to earn £500,000-a-week.

Arsenal are pondering whether to make a move for Vini Jr, whose future at the Bernabeu is uncertain following the Spanish giant's pursuit of Yan Diomande.

It is understood Real have a verbal agreement in principle with RB Leipzig for Diomande, beating Paris Saint-Germain and Liverpool to his signature.

As for Vini Jr, Arsenal are yet to initiate direct contact with Real over a move and view the 26-year-old as an option rather than their number one target.

Troy Deeney's verdict on Arsenal's Vini Jr pursuit

Although the Brazilian would undoubtedly bring plenty of quality to Arsenal and the Premier League as a whole, former Watford striker Troy Deeney questioned whether the striker's character would be the right fit for their dressing room.

2 The 26-year-old has been with Real Madrid since 2018 Credit: Getty

"If it did happen, it would be amazing for the Premier League to have a superstar on that level in terms of global appeal," Deeney said on talkSPORT Breakfast.

"I don't like it. I don't think it suits the way Arsenal play. I don't think his personality suits [Mikel] Arteta.

"I think he's a massive diva in terms of what he wants and what he needs.

"I don't think he would buy into the collective, and that would be something new for Arteta to have to deal with, because he's all about the group.

"You'd have Saka on one side, who's done everything right, then you bring in this guy and go, 'Everyone, give him the ball.' And you have to keep giving him the ball.

"I don't like it. I don't think it helps Arsenal, I really don't."

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino slams FIFA critics for ‘spreading hate’ during World Cup in scathing social media rant
Sports.content:
Infantino posted a 15-slide message across the official FIFA Instagram account, urging critics to 'reflect, meditate, pray, or watch a football match'

Gianni Infantino has launched a scathing attack on his critics, and accused them of 'spreading hate' about FIFA and his leadership in the wake of the 2026 World Cup.

The message was shared across 15 slides on his personal Instagram account, and also cross-posted on FIFA's platform, which is followed by more than eight million people.

4 Infantino has launched an astonishing attack on critics following the World Cup Credit: Getty

In his bizarre statement, Infantino defended the handling of the World Cup, which took place across the United States, Canada and Mexico, and claimed critics had 'missed all that joy and togetherness' of the tournament.

He also accused people of 'spreading hate and false rumours' after the final that was won by Spain, and urged them to 'reflect, meditate, pray, or watch a football match' instead.

"To all of you who missed watching kids, babies, grandparents, and parents come together for the beautiful game, I say sorry that the matches are now over and sorry that you missed all that joy and togetherness," Infantino wrote.

"Sorry that you were so consumed by hate and criticism that you missed it all.

"To those behind their pens and papers, behind their screens spreading hate and false rumours, I want to say that while you are sitting behind, we at FIFA are on the front lines organising, working hard, and delivering the best show in the world.

"While you hide, we are exploring the streets of Canada, Mexico, and the United States, talking with fans, engaging with people and ensuring everyone's safety.

"While you divide, we unite."

Infantino suggested the World Cup experienced 'no violence, no incidents, 100% safety and security, only joy and happiness' -- and claimed seven million people from more than 200 countries attended matches this summer.

FIFA, though, has faced criticism for its handling of the event.

Gianni Infantino responds to backlash over 2026 World Cup

US travel restrictions affected supporters and officials from a number of competing nations, and Iran's national team was vocal about the 'mistreatment' it faced from the government.

4 Infantino's relationship with Trump was called into question during the tournament Credit: Getty

Somali referee Omar Artan was also unable to enter the United States after being denied a visa, and therefore could not officiate at the tournament.

Meanwhile, a saga surrounding USMNT striker Folarin Balogun and his suspended one-game ban put political interference in sport at the heart of the conversation, and called into question Donald Trump's friendship with Infantino.

The FIFA president, though, defended the restrictions, adding in his statement: "You mentioned the few people denied visas and overlooked the millions who were approved, from all parts of the world.

"Because football unites the world, and it was demonstrated impressively this summer."

He also alluded to the Balogun situation, which saw the US star play against Belgium in the last-16 after his automatic one-match ban for a red card against Bosnia and Herzegovina was scrapped.

Infantino didn't reference that moment directly, but wrote: "Indeed, 'arguable' referees' decisions or 'strange' disciplinary rulings such as for instance potentially mistaken red or yellow cards or subsequent decisions not to ban players in certain situations are routine and widely accepted in some of the biggest leagues worldwide.

4 Balogun was at the center of a saga after his red card suspension was overturned Credit: Getty

4 Infantino has urged his critics to 'reflect, meditate, pray, or watch a football match' Credit: Getty

"It's curious that the same countries employing these practices are the ones criticising. This FIFA World Cup celebrated humanity at its best."

Infantino, who is facing two formal ethics complaints as pressure mounts over his personal relationship with the US president, concluded his message by urging critics to 'find peace,' and insisted he was proud how the tournament unfolded.

"Because only our beautiful game can deliver such an extraordinary show, a show where everyone becomes one and reconnects as humans," he said.

"To the pens and papers, to all the screens, may you find love and peace where the people behind you couldn't.

"May you find peace; we at FIFA have found ours and we deliver it, by delivering the most outstanding FIFA World Cup. May football rise above all hate.

"Finally I am incredibly proud, as FIFA President, to have contributed, even a little, to this show. It's a great feeling! Much love to all."

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo lined up for surprise new job away from football to spark ‘bidding war’
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo lined up for surprise new job away from football to spark ‘bidding war’

Cristiano Ronaldo has been tipped for an acting career ahead of starring in a new football TV show.

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner is set to appear in a series about a fictional football agent.



3 Ronaldo has been tipped for an acting career ahead of starring in a TV show he is producing Credit: Getty

Band of Brothers star Damian Lewis will play the lead role in the show, which Ronaldo is serving as an executive producer on.

With filming already underway, including at League Two club Barnet, the Portugal captain is expected to cameo in the show, called Day 1s.

According to The Sun, Thierry Henry will also play a role in the series having been pictured at Barnet's The Hive Stadium.



The show is based on a concept devised by the Arsenal legend's real-life agent Darren Dein.

In demand

Dein is also one of the show's executive producers with the series expected to be in high demand amongst streaming platforms.



A source told The Sun: "It’s likely to spark a bidding war between the streamers.

"The sheer calibre of figures behind it, not to mention the cast, means it’s a prestige project, albeit a surprising one for Ronaldo as he crosses into making dramas."



The insider added: "After the World Cup, there’s a renewed international interest, particularly in the States, in British football.

"It’s one that’s been growing for some time with shows like Ted Lasso.

"But this isn’t a sitcom. It’s definitely a drama, with some comedic elements, and has some serious names backing it."

3 Henry will also appear in Day 1s, a new show about a fictional football agent Credit: Getty



Ronaldo's acting future

Alongside Golden Globe winner Lewis, British rapper Dave will also star in Day 1s alongside newcomer Carlotta Banat.

Meanwhile, the newly-formed UR Marv Studios will make the show.

The firm is a collaboration between Ronaldo and director Matthew Vaughn.

Following its launch earlier this year, the Al Nassr forward said: "This is an exciting chapter for me, as I look ahead to new ventures."

Vaughn is no stranger to football, having invested in Brentford alongside his wife, model and actress Claudia Schiffer.



Ronaldo could now be set to forge an acting career once he decides to hang up his boots.

3 Ronaldo formed a production company with director Vaughn earlier this year Credit: Getty

His appearance in Day 1s will be his first ever acting credit outside of video games and adverts.

The 41-year-old's current Al Nassr deal runs until next summer, by which time he will be 42, having penned an extension in June 2025.

Sports.title: Al Hilal open talks with Premier League and World Cup star after Crysencio Summerville signing
Sports.content:
Al Hilal open talks with Premier League and World Cup star after Crysencio Summerville signing

Add us as preferred source

Al Hilal have opened talks with Everton forward Iliman Ndiaye, talkSPORT understands.

It follows their £68million deal to sign Crysencio Summerville from West Ham.

3 Ndiaye has been with Everton for two years Credit: Getty

The Netherlands international joined the Saudi Pro League side earlier this month following the Hammers' relegation.

Al Hilal are now looking to sign another star from last season's Premier League to bolster their attack.

Ndiaye scored six goals and provided three assists in 32 league appearances for the Toffees last term.

The 26-year-old was also part of Senegal's World Cup squad, scoring once and adding two assists as they reached the last 32.

Despite Al Hilal's talks with Ndiaye, Everton are yet to receive any formal communications from the club.

Meanwhile, the Toffees themselves have also been trying to extend his current deal.

Ndiaye, who signed from Marseille two years ago, is under contract until the summer of 2029.

Full-back Vitaliy Mykolenko has already penned a three-year extension this summer.

Toffees transfer business

David Moyes' side have also been busy in the transfer market themselves.

Former loanees Tyrique George and Merlin Rohl have both made their moves permanent ahead of next season.

3 Everton have been trying to tie the Senegal international down to a new deal Credit: Getty

Everton have also completed the signing of Championship Player of the Year Hayden Hackney.

The midfielder arrived from Middlesbrough in a deal worth £25million.

In terms of departures, Idrissa Gueye, Tyler Onyango and Seamus Coleman have all left the club on free transfers.

It comes after Moyes guided the Toffees to a 13th place finish last term.

Everton had been in the hunt for European qualification for the first time in eight years.

However, a run of one win in their final nine matches saw them finish four points adrift of a Conference League berth.

3 Ndiaye could follow Gueye out of the door at Everton this summer Credit: Getty

Moyes will be hoping to avoid a similar outcome during the upcoming campaign.

Everton begin the season at home to Crystal Palace on Saturday, August 22.

Sports.title: Phil Parkinson says Wrexham hope to complete first summer transfer this week
Sports.content:
Phil Parkinson says Wrexham hope to complete first summer transfer this week

Phil Parkinson has given Wrexham fans a positive transfer update as the club looks to make its first summer signing.

The Red Dragons are yet to add to their squad following last season's seventh place finish in the Championship.

4 Parkinson has revealed Wrexham hope to complete their first summer signing this week Credit: Getty

Parkinson's side missed out on the play-offs by just two points on their return to the second tier.

Several players have since left the club, including the likes of Paul Mullin, Jay Rodriguez and Andy Cannon.

Former loanee Issa Kabore also returned to parent club Manchester City at the end of the campaign.

Meanwhile, Wrexham also missed out on the signing of goalkeeper Pierce Charles, who has instead joined QPR on a season-long loan.

Wrexham transfer update

However, Parkinson has now revealed on talkSPORT's The Final Word with Alan Pardew and Majestic a first signing of the transfer window will 'hopefully' join the club this week.

Highlighting the different challenges faced compared to 12 months ago, he explained on Sunday: "I think last year we put 14 players in.

"You bring the players in different stages of pre-season. Some deals take longer than others, people moving into the area and it took us a while to find our feet in the division and also, I had players adapting to that.

"But I feel we've got a better, stronger squad in this pre-season and it's been great to work with the group so far, which we put together last season.

"However, I don't feel we're there yet in terms of the squad. We're not resting on our laurels and thinking, we're seventh and we're just going to naturally progress above that.

"We've got to work on the recruitment and we're closing in on our first signing, hopefully this week.

4 Parkinson is looking to build on his side's seventh place finish in the Championship last season Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

"You've got to be patient in your recruitment, but we still need to strengthen the squad for me to get a real feeling of confidence that we're ready to go and take it a step further.

"But we've got some good players and we were close. It's a very exciting season because it's going to be as competitive as ever."

The signing in question could be that of Fiorentina defender Matias Moreno.

Wrexham have reportedly agreed a £7.2million fee with the Serie A side for the 22-year-old.

His potential arrival would come less than two weeks before the club's first competitive fixture of the season.

The Red Dragons travel to face Middlesbrough in the first round of the Carabao Cup on Friday, August 7.

4 Wrexham begin their league campaign away to Cardiff City on August 17 Credit: Getty

They then begin their Championship campaign away to Welsh rivals Cardiff City on August 17.

Behind-the-scenes

Parkinson also lifted the lid on the challenges he faces whilst coaching on camera as part of Welcome to Wrexham.

The behind-the-scenes documentary series recently released its fifth season following the players, staff and fans of the club.

Asked what it is like to coach on camera, Parkinson added: "I think all you can be is just be yourself, and the best thing I can do to tell the story is to get the team to win games of football.

"It's about building relationships up with the producers, both over in Wrexham and over here in America.

"And we've done that, and there's an element of trust between both parties, and we know we've got to give them complete access to be able to tell the story.

4 Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney's involvement has helped Wrexham grow their profile hugely and shoot up the leagues Credit: Getty

"But also, they're very respectful as well. So we've worked together and the editing and the way they've told the story has been brilliant, because that's a great skill.

"But they're also appreciative of the drama the team's created, and the success has obviously impacted greatly on the success of the documentary as well."

Wrexham are currently on tour in the States where they will face Liverpool in New York at 12:30am GMT on Thursday before taking on Sunderland in Philadelphia on Sunday at 5pm GMT.

Sports.title: Vinicius Jr warned over major Premier League issue despite ‘Arsenal deal making sense for all parties’
Sports.content:
Vinicius Jr warned over major Premier League issue despite ‘Arsenal deal making sense for all parties’

Vinicius Junior has always been inconsistent, and he's not robust enough for the Premier League.

That is the verdict of South American football expert Jon Cotterill, after the news that Arsenal are considering a move for the Brazilian.



4 Vini Jr chipped in with five direct goal contributions at the World Cup in North America Credit: Getty

talkSPORT understands that the Gunners are yet to engage in club-to-club talks for the Real Madrid winger, with the player viewed as an option rather than their no.1 target.

The 26-year-old has also been offered to Liverpool; however, the Reds have opted against pursuing a deal for the 53-cap international.

Arsenal’s interest comes after Real Madrid moved for RB Leipzig's Yan Diomande, who is part of the same agency as Vinicius.



'I'd prefer someone like Julian Alvarez'

Discussing Vini Jr's situation in the market this summer, Cotterill was asked what other club would be interested in Los Blancos' No.7 if he does indeed become available to sign.

He told talkSPORT's Weekend Sports Breakfast with Katie Shanahan and Tony Cascarino: "I'm sure, like Flamengo, for example, in Brazil would love to get him, but there's no chance.



"He's too young; it's too expensive. But all the big names, it depends where he could fit into the plan if Arsenal have got a plan, for example, if anybody else in the Premier League also got a plan.

"For me, okay, 26 [years old], 22 goals for Real Madrid last season, had a decent enough campaign with Brazil, four goals in the World Cup.



"But for me it's always been inconsistent, and that's been an issue for me.

"I also think perhaps he might not be robust enough for the Premier League, and I'd prefer someone like Julian Alvarez, the Argentine who's at Atletico Madrid, who's had Premier League experience as well.

4 Alvarez's future at Atletico Madrid is becoming a major talking point Credit: Getty

"But yeah, Vini Junior of course, the clubs are limited who've got that kind of price tag, but again for me it's not only the price.



"What's he going to do? How is he going to fit in?

"Can he fit in around the team they've got, and can he fit into the style they've got as well?"

Cotterill also added that any deal for Vinicius is likely to cost north of £100million despite him having just one year left on his contract.

Cascarino told talkSPORT: "Well, the only thing I'd say is his agent will probably say, 'Vini, wait a year, you'll probably get 50 yourself before we even talk about salary.' I just don't see that being the case.

"And also, you talked about being robust - I remember watching him last season within the Champions League against Man City, scored two away from home, played really well.



4 Vinicius Junior scored to help send Real Madrid through to the quarter-finals at Man City's expense last season Credit: Getty

"I thought he really gave Man City a number of issues," Cascarino continued. "I then saw him. he backed it up.

"He played in the Super Cup, he played a game against Atletico Madrid and scored a brace straight afterwards.

"And I felt by the end of the season he was playing probably as well as he had done for a good 18 months to two years."



'Fabulous player but again I think inconsistent'

Cotterill replied: "Yeah, the technical side of things, there's no question about the skills he's got.

"He's an absolutely fabulous player, but again I think inconsistent. And I did see him actually before when he was at Flamengo, Flamengo's Under-17 side in the Copinha, the little cup as it's called, the biggest youth championship in Brazil.

"So I actually went to see him quite a few years ago now, and he was a standout player, just absolutely head and shoulders above everybody else on the pitch.

"But again for me it's that question of inconsistency."

4 Could the player end up at the Emirates this window?



Arsenal deal makes sense

Despite Cotterill's concerns, Spanish Football Journalist Phil Kitromilides argued that Vinicius to Arsenal makes sense for all parties.

"It's not that they've made a bid," he explained to talkSPORT's Transfer Insiders with Will Gavin and Luke Moore on Saturday evening.

"It's not that they've been speaking to Real Madrid. It's that they are interested in signing him, which is fair enough.

"And you know what, Vinicius to Arsenal makes a lot of sense actually on a lot of levels on both sides.



"Vinicius going into the final year of his contract hasn't necessarily felt like he's the main man at Real Madrid since the arrival of Kylian Mbappe.

"He's been asking, I've been told, for around €30million a year at Real Madrid, which is about €550k a week.

"Real Madrid aren't going to pay that. Can Arsenal come anywhere close to that?"

Sports.title: MLS desperate to improve ‘pitiful’ TV deal as guru warns league is ‘worst investment in sports’
Sports.content:
All recommendations within this article are informed by expert editorial opinion. If you click on a link in this story we will earn affiliate revenue.

The MLS is hoping to cash in on the success of the World Cup, but they may not be able to receive the financing they so desperately want.

MLS desperate to improve ‘pitiful’ TV deal as guru warns league is ‘worst investment in sports’

Major League Soccer may be in a slight bit of trouble.

The league was hoping to capitalize on the success of the 2026 World Cup that was held across the United States, Mexico, and Canada.

4 MLS is hoping to capitalize on the success of the World Cup Credit: Getty

With the new-found surge in popularity in the sport, which former U.S. Soccer President Alan Rothenberg believes will see it 'rocket launch' past other major sports leagues, including the NBA and MLB, over the next decade, MLS had optimism that they could attract more money.

It has seen a plethora of elite-level talent join over the last few years - perhaps none greater than Argentina superstar Lionel Messi - while Heung-min Son, Antoine Griezmann, and latest Inter Miami recruit Casemiro are other huge names to land in America.

But there is clearly an appetite for the sport after the record-breaking numbers brought in from a US audience at the World Cup, making FOX Sports' $485million gamble to secure the English-language broadcasting rights in the States look like a bargain.

With that in mind, MLS Commissioner Don Garber wants to cash in with the 30-team league now bringing in an estimated $2.5billion in revenue, according to Sportico.

In the weeks leading up to the World Cup Final where Spain triumphed over Messi and Argentina, MLS spent tens of millions of dollars on an ad campaign with a tag line which read: "Thanks, world. We'll take it from here."

But according to Global Football Rankings, the league ranks in at 10th as it pertains to being the highest-quality league in the world, despite MLS having 17 of the top 50 most valuable soccer franchises in the world.

Most of this added revenue has come from expansion teams, with the seven new teams added to MLS since 2019 having paid a collective fee in the region of $1.5bn.

Now, there is an ongoing debate of how to grow it further from here, with the most identifiable path to real - and organic - growth being through broadcast revenue.

However, this is where issues could arise.

Previously, MLS struggled with their rights negotiations the last time they hit the market, eventually settling for a ten-year deal with Apple TV in 2022 that saw them pay $250m over a decade-long span.

4 Messi is arguably the biggest name to ever come over to MLS Credit: Getty

For the consumer, this meant having to pay a subscription fee, which for a casual soccer fan, meant having to weigh up whether it was worth it.

Now, a report from ESPN's Ben Strauss suggests that MLS owners have expressed their desire for a new rights fee worth almost double annually.

"Owners have discussed a desire for a new rights fee in the $400million to $500million range, which would in effect triple the money teams are getting from Apple, according to two people with knowledge of the discussions," Strauss wrote.

"That, of course, is easier said than done."

Lack of 'world's best talent' a huge issue

Stefan Szymanski, co-author of the book 'Soccernomics', argues: "There is no major sports league in the world that does not rely primarily on broadcast revenues, and Major League Soccer has pitiful broadcast revenues.

"How do you become a major broadcast player in the world of sports? The answer is you have the world's best talent."

4 Son moved to MLS to join LAFC after a decade-long tenure at Premier League outfit Tottenham Hotspur Credit: Getty

4 Griezmann made the switch to MLS this summer Credit: Getty

The reality is, MLS can't attract the 'world's best talent' like Europe can, with their biggest stars having opted to move to the league to see out the twilight years of their careers as opposed to joining during their prime years.

"The hope would be that Americans get a taste for great world soccer this summer but not enough discernment to notice the soccer being put on in America -- except Lionel Messi -- isn't being played by world-class soccer players," Andy Schwarz, an economist at the firm OSKR, said.

"They need demand for soccer to grow so people start to appreciate soccer more, but not enough to notice the great players aren't here. It's a Goldilocks situation.

"The valuations have baked in a probability of that happening that is well above my pessimistic view. They could get rid of the salary cap and start spending like the Premier League, but I'm not sure how that generates positive cash flows, either."

As it stands, MLS' current salary cap sits at around $6.4m, though it does allow for additional spending, which sees most teams' payrolls sitting between $13m and $20m - Inter Miami's, though, is $46m.

"MLS is dominated by NFL ideology at the ownership level," one person involved in league business, said via ESPN's report.

"The quality of the player pool could go down by 25 per cent and it would have no impact on an NFL team's valuation. The quality of play doesn't matter. That's just not true in a global sport."

One lawyer who advises private wealth funds on sports investments even admitted that he actively tells his clients to avoid MLS.

"I advise all my clients to stay away from MLS," the lawyer said. "It's the worst investment they could make in sports."

Nonetheless, MLS Commissioner Don Garber remains bullish on the whole situation, and told a large group of reporters prior to the World Cup final that: "I'd rather be us than any other soccer league in the world."

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford told he must make Man United statement and accept new role
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford must make an 'almighty statement' to prove he still wants to be at Manchester United.

That's the view of former England international Micky Gray, who argues there could be a way back at Old Trafford for Rashford.

2 Rashford thrived on loan at Barcelona last season Credit: Getty

Rashford hasn't played for Man United since the back end of 2024, spending time on loan at Aston Villa then Barcelona.

However, with Barcelona not signing the England forward permanently this summer – having already bought his international teammate Anthony Gordon – Rashford is back with Man United for pre-season after helping his country to third place at the World Cup.

That's after talkSPORT's Jamie O'Hara urged Tottenham to 'break the bank' to sign him.

Rashford must show 'full commitment'

But if Rashford is to be reintegrated successfully into the Old Trafford set-up by Michael Carrick, he has to show he's all in.

Man United pre-season on MUTV Fans can watch Michael Carrick prepare for the new season and how the squad is shaping up across Finland, Norway, Sweden and Ireland. MUTV is the home of all Manchester United pre-season fixtures. It’s the opportunity to watch new faces, young players, returning names, tactical clues and the first signs of what United might become over the next season. MUTV on Sky: £7 extra a month. Existing Sky TV customers only. 31 day rolling contract. Cancel anytime with 31 days’ notice. Requires compatible Sky Q or Sky Stream boxes.

Speaking on talkSPORT's Sunday Session, host Hugh Woozencroft asked: "Will Marcus Rashford's reintegration send a message to the rest of the squad about what behaviour is going to be expected by Michael Carrick? It's not a group full of Roy Keanes; it's a very delicate changing room.

"Rashford said he wanted a new challenge and unless you can be 100 per cent sure he is completely committed to Man United… he's shown he wasn't fully committed the last time he was at the club… how can you be sure he's going to be this time around?"

Rashford first left Man United on loan to join Aston Villa for the second half of the 2024/25 season.

He subsequently spent the 2025/26 campaign with Barcelona, scoring 14 goals in all competitions that saw him win the LaLiga title and regain his spot in the England squad.

But Gray has warned the 28-year-old he'll have to accept playing less of a starring role back at Man United, as well as explain his past departure, should he remain there.

"There's a few things here," he replied to Woozencroft. "The most important one is, if Rashford has a future at Man United, he has to do an almighty statement of why he wants to be at Man United and what the reasons were to leave the club in the first place. I think that's a priority that he has to do.

2 Rashford took his England caps tally to 78 this summer Credit: Getty

"If he does stay then he's got to get used to being a bit-part player.

"He's not first on the list; he's not going to be playing every week...[Bryan] Mbuemo, [Matheus] Cunha, [Benjamin] Sesko, Amad to name a few. They've caught up to and if not surpassed Rashford.

"Spain is not England. He did very well, but he can play at Barcelona at a different level to what he can at Man United. He can't deny that the Premier League is 100mph – he's going to have to get himself super fit in pre-season.

"We saw the good and the bad of Rashford for England at the World Cup… can Man United utilise him in a way they can expect to see the good side and bad side? If they do that and he stays… Rashford has got to expect that he isn't going to play every game."

Rashford returns to find his number taken

Rashford appeared in six of England's eight matches at the World Cup, scoring in the Three Lions' opening 4-2 win over Croatia.

His last outing for Man United came in a Europa League victory away to Viktoria Plzen in December 2024.

The Red Devils academy product has yet to be allocated a squad number since returning to Old Trafford, with Matheus Cunha taking his old No.10 shirt last summer.

Sports.title: Besiktas need answer from Mohamed Salah after making their final offer, Saudi club Al-Rayyan target Jadon Sancho... and Inter confirm they want Cristian Romero from Tottenham: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Liverpool want compromise on Barcola

Liverpool are working to find agreement with Paris Saint-Germain over Bradley Barcola amid escalating valuations.

The 23-year-old France international has indicated he does not wish to sign a new contract with the European champions and is open to joining Liverpool who have a long-held interest.

PSG are considering his sale but he still has two years left on contract and they believe, based on his age, potential and current market prices, £140million is a fair reflection of his valuation.

Liverpool will seek a compromise on that with Barcola's price reputed to have been closer to £75m last summer when they first sounded out his representatives.

Read more on this story HERE

Bradley Barcola has indicated he will not sign a new contract at Paris Saint-Germain

Inter in for Tottenham star Romero

Inter Milan have confirmed they have entered talks with Tottenham over the potential signing of Cristian Romero.

The Spurs captain helped Argentina reach a second straight World Cup final this month, but as Daily Mail Sport reported last month is attracting interest from the Italian giants after they were made aware he could leave this summer.

The structure is complicated, though, as Spurs still want a significant fee for the 28-year-old after an eventful five-year spell.

Inter’s sporting director, Piero Ausilio, told Sky Italy: 'It’s definitely a deal we are trying to sign with the player and the club. These things take some time but there’s definitely interest. Let’s see.'

Is it yes or no, Mo? Besiktas waiting for Salah answer

Besiktas say they are awaiting Mohamed Salah's decision after submitting their final offer for the former Liverpool forward.

Club president Serdal Adali confirmed to Turkish media: 'We told Salah and his agent that we expect them to inform us of their decision shortly.

'Since our first meetings, we have evaluated every requested increase and amendment within the framework of Besiktas' interests and presented our final offer. The decision is now on the player's side, and we expect a response soon.'

He added that Besiktas had reviewed every requested increase and amendment throughout the negotiations while keeping the club's interests in mind before putting forward its last proposal.

It is understood Besiktas are the first choice for Salah, now 34, but he does have offers from elsewhere - including the MLS, where Sporting Kansas City have made a lucrative two-year contract proposal.

Mo Salah left Liverpool at the end of last season and has offers from more than one club

Saudi suitor for Sancho

Jason Sancho has emerged as a target for Qatari club Al-Rayyan.

The 26-year-old is a free agent after leaving Manchester United and has been keeping fit while awaiting offers to assess.

Atletico Madrid have also shown an interest in the England international.

Jadon Sancho had loan spells at Dortmund, Chelsea and Aston Villa in his final three seasons as a Manchester United player

Blackburn bag Finley after trial

Blackburn Rovers have signed former Brighton goalkeeper Finley Taylor after he impressed on trial.

The 18-year-old was a free agent having left Brighton, where he had been for five years.

Taylor said: 'At the end of last season, I came on trial, played against Manchester United and it was a good game. A tough game against obviously one of the best teams in England.

'After that, I found out I got signed. It was just a phone call, and it was a massive relief because, obviously, when you leave a club before, it's quite nerve-racking; you don't know what to expect. So, to get that call was a massive relief.'

Newcastle look at Hornicek after he rejected Hull move

Newcastle United have switched sights to Sporting Braga goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek.

The 24-year-old Czech Republic international was the subject of a failed bid by Hull City earlier in the window and Benfica have been making enquiries in the past week.

Hull even matched his £25.9m release clause but Hornicek turned down the move.

'We even had one [a concrete approach]. The player himself, Hornicek, refused. There was a proposal from England, from the Premier League, but the player felt he shouldn’t go to that club and we were happy for him to stay,' the Braga president António Salvador confirmed to Portuguese media.

Lukas Hornicek went to the World Cup with Czech Republic and has a £29.5m release clause at Braga

Hornicek was back in action in midweek as he starred in Braga's 1-0 win at Serbian side Zeleznicar Pancevo in their Europa Conference League qualifier.

Newcastle had been pursuing Manchester City's James Trafford but he is set on moving to Leeds United in a deal worth around £45m as he discusses inserting a release clause into his contract.

They had also held a meeting over Brighton keeper Carl Rushworth but ultimately Newcastle had reservations about his lack of top flight experience. Rushworth remains a target for Coventry City, where he was on loan last season. They have had bids worth £25m rejected so far.

Newcastle have now asked about Hornicek and the deal could be agreed quickly if all parties wish to proceed.

Wrexham in for Palace's Imray - but face competition

Wrexham have joined the clubs showing interest in Crystal Palace full-back Danny Imray.

The 22-year-old, who had loan spells with Blackpool and West Bromwich Albion last season, is wanted back by Albion while Stoke City have also posted interest.

Wrexham, though, are continuing to push the bar on their targets as they try to take that next step up into the Premier League.

They also remain in the chase for Leicester City's Harry Souttar. The Australia international has asked to leave but the Foxes want £10million which is deterring suitors such as Sheffield United, Stoke City and more.

Danny Imray is a potential target for Wrexham as well as other EFL clubs

Leicester in race against time for No 9

Leicester City are clear favourites to gain promotion from League One but are still to sign a striker - with barely three weeks to go until they kick-off the season against Notts County.

Manager Russell Martin may have overseen a 3-3 draw against La Liga side Malaga in Marbella on Saturday but that didn't mask what he thought the former Premier League champions were missing.

'The topline, both wide positions and a No 9, I think it’s really clear,' said the Foxes' boss when asked about priorities.

They have tried and failed to agree terms with former West Ham striker Danny Ings and, despite his appearance at first-team testing, Jamie Vardy is not planning a return. He still has aspirations to finish at the top.

Jamie Vardy has been training at Leicester but has his sights on a higher level than League One
