Sports.title: FIFA boss Gianni Infantino goes full Trump as he furiously slams World Cup critics for 'spreading hate' in blistering social media rant
Sports.content:
FIFA boss Gianni Infantino goes full Trump as he furiously slams World Cup critics for 'spreading hate' in blistering social media rant

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has launched a blistering attack on World Cup critics, claiming they've been 'consumed by hate' and telling them to 'meditate, pray or watch a football match' in order to 'find peace.'

With the six-week tournament officially over, Infantino took the time to address his detractors through a 15-slide post on Instagram – where he seemingly defended a number of controversies that occurred throughout the summer competition.

The outburst was posted across Infantino's personal Instagram account and cross-posted to FIFA's official page on Sunday night, reaching over 13 million followers.

Infantino, who didn't hold a press conference when the World Cup began, nor when it ended, began his outburst by calling out those 'who missed our beautiful game, the emotions, the celebrations, the laughter, the crying, the deception and the joy.'

He claimed that those who 'missed' out were 'so consumed by hate and criticism.'

The FIFA chief appeared to take aim at journalists as he claimed critics sat 'behind their pens and papers, behind their screens spreading hate and false rumors'.

FIFA president Gianni Infantino launched a blistering attack on World Cup critics on Sunday

In a 15-slide Instagram post, Infantino called out those who were 'so consumed by hate and criticism' that they 'missed our beautiful game, the emotions, the laughter and the joy'

View this post on Instagram

'I want to say that while you are sitting behind, we at FIFA are on the front lines organizing, working hard and delivering the best show in the world,' he continued.

Infantino, 56, then claimed: 'We experienced no violence, no incidents, 100 percent safety and security, only joy and happiness!'

However, critics online were quick to point out a number of violent incidents that occurred as a direct result of the six-week summer tournament.

In fact, the opening day of the 2026 FIFA World Cup was hit by violent protests as riot police fired tear gas at demonstrators prior to Mexico's game against South Africa.

The massive demonstrations were fueled by a coalition of multiple unions and activist groups marching to draw global eyes to the country's severe domestic issues.

The most prominent groups mobilizing include searching mothers' collectives, the CNTE teachers' union, federal judiciary workers and various transport organizations. In total, it was reported that eight simultaneous protests took place.

Away from the tournament's opening day, there were a number of violent incidents that occurred at fan parks and during post-match celebrations worldwide.

Most tragically, Infantino's claim of 'zero incidents' ignored the death of four supporters in Mexico City, who suffocated during chaotic street celebrations following Mexico's round of 32 victory over Ecuador.

Infantino claimed: 'We experienced no violence, no incidents, 100 percent safety and security'

However, there were a number of violent incidents throughout the tournament - such as when protestors clashed with riot police prior to the very first game of the 2026 World Cup

While Mexico secured a 2-0 victory over South Africa, thousands of protesters hit the capital

While Infantino previously offered condolences on social media, the day after the tragedy, his 15-slide post made no mention of the victims when boasting about tournament safety.

Meanwhile, other fans noted that FIFA opted to proceed with the tournament despite fans from four competing nations, Iran, Haiti, Senegal and Ivory Coast, facing US travel bans imposed by the Trump administration.

In another case, Somali referee Omar Artan saw his dreams of officiating in a World Cup crushed after being prohibited from entering the US on the tournament's eve.

Trump's administration then made a bombshell claim that Artan, who was named as Africa's best male referee last year, was denied entry due to terrorism fears.

Infantino appeared to address the controversy surrounding both the fans and the official.

He wrote: 'You mentioned the few people denied visas and overlooked the millions who were approved, from all parts of the world. Because football unites the world, and it was demonstrated impressively this summer.'

Elsewhere in his social media rant, Infantino claimed that 'Iran entered the United States without incident or conflict.'

However, fans noted that only four of the fifteen Iranian team staff members who were originally denied visas were later granted the right to travel into the country.

Despite a number of incidents regarding visas being denied, Infantino downplayed that aspect

Somali referee Omar Abdulkadir Artan was denied entry to the United States to officiate

The Iranian Football Federation alleged that the US and FIFA did not want them at the World Cup

US Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin also sparked fury after claiming that 'almost half' of Iran’s non-playing delegation had direct ties to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

'Iranians are used to the mistreatment and lies of US officials, so no one in Iran is surprised by these hostile remarks,' an official for the federation said, via The Telegraph.

'These remarks once again demonstrate that US officials have no commitment to international law or the principles expected of a host nation capable of organizing a global sporting event.'

Infantino also appeared to fire a direct shot at critics regarding the mid-tournament storm surrounding Donald Trump and USMNT forward Folarin Balogun.

The striker was sent off during the USA's 2-0 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina, meaning that he should have been unavailable for their next game against Belgium.

However, on the eve of the game, FIFA announced that they had postponed his suspension – sparking widespread fury from fans across the globe.

It was later revealed that Trump had phoned up Infantino, who previously presented the US president with an inaugural FIFA Peace Prize, and asked for the case to be reviewed, leading fans to launch accusations of political interference.

Addressing the controversy, Infantino wrote: 'Indeed, 'arguable' referees' decisions or 'strange' disciplinary rulings such as for instance potentially mistaken red or yellow cards or subsequent decisions not to ban players in certain situations are routine and widely accepted in some of the biggest leagues worldwide.

Hinting at the drama surrounding Folarin Balogun's postponed suspension, Infantino claimed that instances like that 'are routine and widely accepted in the biggest leagues worldwide'

The forward, who was sent off for this tackle, will now be available to face Belgium on Monday

It later emerged that Trump had called Infantino over the matter prior to a decision being made

'It's curious that the same countries employing these practices are the ones criticizing,' the FIFA chief added on the matter.

The unprecedented ruling sparked furious accusations of political favoritism from UEFA, the Belgian Football Association and countless European lawmakers.

The Norwegian Football Federation have also since confirmed plans to file a formal complaint over Trump's role in the decision.

He capped off his tirade by telling his detractors to step away from their computers and find peace.

'To those spending their time and energy hating us, please take a moment to reflect, meditate, pray, or watch a football match and truly observe the faces, the eyes, the emotions,' Infantino concluded.

'To the pens and papers, to all the screens, may you find love and peace where the people behind you couldn't. May you find peace; we at FIFA have found ours and we deliver it, by delivering the most outstanding FIFA World Cup. May football rise above all hate.'

Sports.title: Micky van de Ven warns Tottenham's rivals to prepare for a brand new Spurs after last season's relegation survivors splashed £237MILLION on new stars - and praises the club's 'ambition'
Sports.content:
Micky van de Ven warns Tottenham's rivals to prepare for a brand new Spurs after last season's relegation survivors splashed £237MILLION on new stars - and praises the club's 'ambition'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Micky van de Ven has warned their Premier League rivals to be prepared to see a new Tottenham Hotspur after their ambitious summer spending spree.

Spurs have already spent £237million on signing Sandro Tonali (£100m), Mateus Fernandes (£85m) and Jan Paul van Hecke (£52m). They have also brought in Andy Robertson and Marcos Senesi on free transfers after back-to-back 17th-placed finishes.

Those acquisitions have helped convince Van de Ven and Spurs’ existing players that they are ready to forget their relegation concerns and focus on a European push instead.

Speaking in Australia, where Spurs are set to face friendlies against Sydney FC and Chelsea this week, the 25-year-old Dutchman said: ‘It’s really good that you can see the club has made some changes. They have brought a really good new manager, and some really good new signings.

‘You can see the club has new ambition. It's something that's really important for players that have been there for a long time. It’s better when you go with a fresh mind into the new season.

'Last season was a stressful season so to leave everything of that behind and go into the new season fresh means a lot. Spurs is a team that needs to play Europe every year, so obviously the European spots are something we are going to aim for.

Micky van de Ven has warned their Premier League rivals to be prepared to see a new Spurs

Spurs have spent £237m on signings including Sandro Tonali (left) and Mateus Fernandes

'The most important thing is we play our football, and that we are a difficult team to play against.’

Spurs' summer signings may help convince Van de Ven to sign a new contract. His current deal runs until 2029. It has been reported that talks could open soon.

Spurs kickstarted their pre-season tour with a 2-0 win over A-League champions Auckland FC on Sunday. Having moved on from New Zealand to Australia, Van de Ven added that Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi will be bringing a brand new style of football – one far superior to that overseen by his predecessors, Igor Tudor and Thomas Frank.

Asked if we will see a different Spurs under De Zerbi, Van de Ven said: ‘I know that for sure.

'It’s going to be different compared to the former manager we had last season. It’s going to be more with the ball I think, more playing football. I think it’s going to be more enjoyable also for people to watch, when playing offensive football.

‘The last couple of weeks of last season, you saw he brought a lot of passion into our group, a lot mentality wise, passion wise, on the pitch. It is something we needed because everybody was a little bit down.

'We started to play a lot with the ball, because he loves us to be on the ball, he loves to play the football he wants to play, and that’s also something I really enjoy.

‘Hopefully it will be (a better season). It's something we are going to work really hard on. Make some differences because last season was a bit unacceptable from our side.’

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso backs Chelsea's £117m British record signing Morgan Rogers to have an 'instant impact' - but sends clear message to England star on his post-World Cup holiday
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso says Chelsea will be busy until the very end of the summer window – and has told Morgan Rogers and his other players yet to return from their World Cup breaks that they need to be ready for their first Premier League showdown with Fulham.

Rogers is currently enjoying downtime after representing England, having signed from Aston Villa for £117million, making him the most expensive British purchase ever.

Speaking for the first time since hijacking Arsenal’s interest to secure Rogers, Alonso said: ‘All the ones who come later because they reached the final stages of the World Cup, they will be ready. We have a few of them so they have to be ready. It’s a great signing.

‘In that position we needed an important player and I’m sure there were not many better options than Morgan Rogers. We were looking at him for a long time. He’s going to be a key player for the team. Luckily it happened quickly and now we have Morgan.

‘You need players who can have that almost instant impact, and I’m sure Morgan won’t need much time to adapt to the club, to the system, to his team-mates. That was the idea that we wanted and to get a top player and Morgan is one of them.’

Alonso was speaking from Sydney, Australia, where Chelsea are set to stage two friendlies against Western Sydney Wanderers and Tottenham Hotspur.

Xabi Alonso has backed £117m signing Morgan Rogers to have an 'instant impact' at Chelsea

The Spaniard admitted Chelsea had been looking at Rogers for 'a long time' before buying him

After Rogers, Chelsea are also set to sign Maxence Lacroix from Crystal Palace for around £52m. That announcement is believed to be imminent.

Asked about Lacroix, Alonso said: ‘We want to build a competitive team. We are in that process. We have great quality, great talent, and we need to know what it takes to compete in the Premier League. We want a squad with the right balance between quality and mentality. Those things need to match.

‘We have to be ready. The market is open for a few weeks. We need to be aware of different positions, different situations, so for sure, we have a plan, an idea, and we need to assess in the right moments. We can’t say what’s going to happen but some things might happen.’

A great deal of Chelsea’s concentration will need to fall on outgoings with their sporting leadership team in Australia with the squad. Once Lacroix is confirmed, he will be the 10th centre back on their books. The other nine are: Levi Colwill, Trevoh Chalobah, Aaron Anselmino, Wesley Fofana, Tosin Adarabioyo, Mamadou Sarr, Josh Acheampong, Axel Disasi and Benoit Badiashile.

‘We need to know that probably there will still be some movements,’ Alonso said. ‘We need to be flexible and quick to act. The main thing is that we have a clear idea, a clear plan that we have built. Probably it will change until the last day of the market being open.

‘I don’t want to talk too early about our goals. We want to have a good season. We want to deserve to be as high as possible. For that, we need to work hard, to develop this team, with new players, a new coach, new ideas. So far, we have good feelings.’

He has told Rogers to 'be ready' as the England star enjoys some downtime after the World Cup

Chelsea covered the least distance of all the clubs in the Premier League last season. While managing Bayer Leverkusen, Alonso’s side were towards the top of the running tables.

‘We need to compete,’ Alonso said. 'We need to have good energy. We need to run. We need to work hard. We need to have the sacrifices which are compulsory and mandatory in each Premier League game. To win each game, it's tough. We need to prepare for that and we are using this time. We will see in the first game.’

Chelsea face Fulham in their Premier League opener on August 24.

Sports.title: 'British cycling is like Hogwarts, it's got everything I need': Meet the Australian Commonwealth champion who is reaping rewards of defecting to England... and admits being closer to his girlfriend is a nice bonus!
Sports.content:
Back on his family farm in Australia, Matt Richardson has a 22-seat school bus locked up in one of the stables.

‘There’s an owl that lives on top of it, he kills all the rats and stops them chewing through the wires,’ explains the England cyclist, who is favourite for gold in Glasgow this week.

‘It’s a Toyota Coaster Bus and it’s an absolute tank. I bought it a few years ago to convert into a camper van but I haven’t got round to it yet. I keep it away from the elements in the shed. If you take care of it, they’re known to do a million kilometres.’

Richardson, it is fair to say, is not a conventional character.

So perhaps it is little surprise that he made the radical decision to switch racing allegiance from Australia to England after winning three medals at the 2024 Olympics.

The 27-year-old was born Maidstone, Kent, but moved Down Under aged nine when his father was offered a job promotion with IKEA. He carved out an impressive track career for Australia – winning gold at the 2022 Commonwealth Games – but his dual citizenship tested his loyalties.

Matt Richardson is all smiles as a GB and England athlete...

... after winning Olympic silver for Australia in the men's keirin in Paris in 2024

‘I’m always looking for more, whether that’s more weight in the gym, more efforts on track or creating more opportunities for myself,’ he explains. ‘Your career only lasts so long and I’ve been wired to really extract every opportunity out of the time that I have.

‘Whether that’s building a camper van to enjoy later in life, or moving country to try and maximise my career. I get bored very easily, so I’m always setting myself a new goal. Something to keep myself on my toes. A self-inflicted challenge. We always have challenges in World Champs and World Cups but it’s not enough, I want a little bit more. The Olympics only comes every four years so you want to keep it different year on year.’

Having a Welsh girlfriend, Emma Finucane – a fellow Olympic medallist – certainly helped with Richardson’s decision. Finucane will wear Welsh colours this week before they come together under the Team GB banner for the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles.

‘British cycling is an incredible place,’ says Richardson. ‘I’ve said this before: Aus cycling was like high school and British cycling is like Hogwarts. It’s incredible, it’s big, it’s magical. I have everything I need at my fingertips to be the best possible athlete I can be. There’s more resources, the equipment’s incredible, we have a wind tunnel next door. No expense is spared.

Richardson was back in Australia as an English competitor at the Track World Cup in Perth in March

‘The bike I ride here is a lot better. It’s fast, it’s stiff, it’s everything I need to break a world record. Whenever we travelled to a race from Adelaide, we had to take multiple flights. The European guys land in on the same day and have no jet lag. Things like that make a really big difference. It’s all on me now. There are no external factors.

‘Of course, being closer to your girlfriend is an added bonus. We live together in Manchester. It rains a little bit more than Australia but luckily I do an indoor sport!’

In a world of marginal gains, the benefits are already starting to show. Richardson became the first rider to break the nine-second barrier on the 200 metres flying lap last August, before finally beating his Dutch nemesis, Harrie Lavreysen, in February.

He has been able to pick the brains of Sir Chris Hoy and even spoken to Formula One superstar Lando Norris over lunch. ‘I guess there’s a shared element of danger with F1. We race shoulder to shoulder sometimes at 80kmh. You have a lot of adrenaline coursing through your veins but ultimately they are very different sports. As a kid I always enjoyed watching things that were dangerous. I loved nitrocircus. They have a mega ramp and launch motorbikes off it doing double backflips and crazy aerial tricks. I have a motorbike here in the UK.’

Richardson with his girlfriend Emma Finucane, an Olympic gold-medal-winning cyclist for Great Britain who is competing for Wales at these Commonwealths

But it has come at a cost. Richardson has made himself Public Enemy No 1 in the Australian camp. He will be branded a turncoat and a traitor, despite allegiance switches becoming commonplace in international sport. In the Sir Chris Hoy Velodrome this week, former Australia team-mate, Leigh Hoffman, will be one of his biggest rivals.

‘I knew it wasn’t going to be all sunshine and rainbows,’ he says. ‘You can’t make everyone happy. I was super stoked to have won two golds for Australia at the last Commonwealths. I was living in the moment and not really thinking about the next Games.

'But if someone had a crystal ball and said “In the next Commonwealth games, you’re going to be riding for England” then I wouldn’t have been that surprised. It was always a thing that I wanted to do.

‘The year before the Olympics, I was looking at the next four years, thinking what that could look like. If I was going to do it then now was the time. Waiting another Olympics would have been too late. The reaction is probably what I expected. But also, the way it rolled out for myself is what I expected. It’s been amazing from the onset.’

With a new support team behind him, Richardson is pedalling forward with grand ambitions. ‘My goal is to win gold at the Commonwealth Games, win gold at the World Championships.

'I’ve been chasing that individual sprint world title for a few years now. I feel like I’m in the form to do that this year – and I want to carry all the momentum I can into LA.’

Sports.title: Female referee left concussed after being knocked over by brawling men's players during melee in match in France
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A female referee reportedly suffered a concussion after being knocked to the ground during a melee in a men's friendly match in France.

Referee Mathilde Demoncay had taken charge of the friendly between Ligue 2 French side Metz and their Dutch opponents Fortuna Sittard on Sunday.

Demoncay had blown for a free kick to Fortuna Sittard in the 39th minute, after a Metz player had pulled the shirt of a breaking attacker.

The fouled Fortuna Sittard player was then seen squaring up to two Metz players following the incident.

This led to Demoncay racing over in an attempt to break up the incident, while players from both teams also ran in as the melee grew.

Footage showed Demoncay, 26, being knocked over backwards as more players pushed into the melee.

Referee Mathilde Demoncay suffered a concussion after being knocked to the ground during a melee between players during a friendly in France

Demoncay had attempted to intervene in the brawl but was knocked down as more players got involved

One player was seen signalling for medical attention with Demoncay appearing to have hit her head on the ground after falling

While unclear on the footage, Demoncay appeared to hit her head on the ground after falling.

One Fortuna player was quick to notice the stricken referee, as they stood by the official and motioned for medical staff to come to her aid.

Medical staff, assistant referees and security came onto the pitch, with Demoncay receiving assistance.

The footage showed Demoncay sitting up as medical staff began to assess her, while players appeared to have become concerned by the incident.

Demoncay was ultimately unable to continue the match, with one of her assistants forced to step in.

The incident, which played out with a sign in the background reading 'respect the referee', led to two players being booked.

Fortuna Sittard had described it as a 'remarkable moment' on the club's website.

Metz, who had been leading 1-0 at the time, went on to win 3-1 in the friendly.

Sports.title: Adam Ramsay-Peaty says getting back into Olympic medal contention is 'the hardest climb I've ever faced'... after breaking down in tears at Commonwealth Games bronze
Sports.content:
Adam Ramsay-Peaty claimed he faces the toughest challenge of his career to get back into medal contention for the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles.

The 31-year-old broke down in tears after finishing third in the men’s 100m breaststroke final, having held the world record since 2015.

Britain’s iconic swimmer will have another shot at gold over 50m on Monday night, having qualified second on his semi-final on Sunday evening, and he is desperate to prove that time has not caught up with him.

‘It's been hard,’ said Ramsay-Peaty after the 100m final. ‘There have been a multitude of things at play over the last few years — burnout, breaking my foot, fighting against something that you love.

'Coming back to where I am now and making the decision to go for LA, I think this is going to be the hardest climb I've ever faced and the hardest test. It's really hard to see the summit because it's so hard. I don't think anyone understands.’

Ramsay-Peaty’s wife, Holly – the daughter of celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay – has been in Glasgow to watch the races. Fatherhood has shifted the breast-stroker's priorities but he does not plan to retire before the next Olympics.

Adam Ramsay-Peaty has said getting back into Olympic medal contention is 'the hardest climb I've ever faced'

‘There are just a lot of personal and professional things that I need to pull together and work out what's important, and what the long-term goal is for my happiness and for my immediate family's happiness as well,' he added.

‘When your world record is three seconds away, we've got to seriously ask what's going wrong because that's not me. We need to look at it, interrogate it, look at the data, and ask whether it was an issue with race pace, fitness, or something else.

'I don't think it was fitness, but there are a lot of components that make us swim, so we really have to analyse it. Of course I'm committed. I've got a big fight in me, and normally it only takes me 24 hours to turn things around.’

He struck a more positive note after breezing into the 50m breaststroke final on Sunday evening, finishing second in his semi-final behind South Africa's Michael Houlie in a time of 26.82sec.

'I think the last 24 hours have been a bit of a whirlwind,' said Ramsay-Peaty. 'It's not something I'm used to, to be honest. I guess this sport is not really about when you get beaten because it's going to be inevitable. Essentially (what's important is) how long it takes you to look at it and turn it around for tonight. And we're really happy with that, we're on a great trajectory for tomorrow.

'Every time I race I am getting a little bit stronger - apart from yesterday - which is important, but I am getting more exposed to it. And people forget that I haven't done this for two years, you know. Even I forget that. So I think that perspective is a good thing to handle tomorrow. Tell you what, I'll just enjoy the crowd. It's an amazing crowd.'

Sports.title: Liverpool must back new boss Andoni Iraola in the transfer window to fix problem position otherwise he faces uphill struggle - with injuries mounting, two untried novices and an ageing captain, writes LEWIS STEELE
Sports.content:
Liverpool must back new boss Andoni Iraola in the transfer window to fix problem position otherwise he faces uphill struggle - with injuries mounting, two untried novices and an ageing captain, writes LEWIS STEELE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

There are two sliding doors moments when it comes to Liverpool and defenders.

Last summer, a deal for England international Marc Guehi was so close that media staff at his former club Crystal Palace had made a farewell video to go out on social channels, with a black-and-white filter featuring clips of him lifting the FA Cup with the headline ‘Thank you, skip’.

Guehi, as we now know, saw his move collapse at the 11th hour of Deadline Day, with chairman Steve Parish pulling the plug late in the day.

Then, in April, Ibrahima Konate told reporters that he was ‘close’ to signing a contract extension at Liverpool. Two months later, the Frenchman was waving farewell to Anfield and following in the footsteps of Trent Alexander-Arnold by moving to Real Madrid. Konate left on a free transfer.

It brings us here, in a position where there are four weeks until the Andoni Iraola era officially begins with a trip to Newcastle – an emotional game given the passing of Kevin Keegan, a legend at both clubs.

With just a month to go, Liverpool are already in something of a defensive crisis. If the opener was to be tomorrow, they would have just captain Virgil van Dijk as the only senior option – and he has not begun pre-season work yet having been given an extended break following the World Cup.

Liverpool need to back Andoni Iraola or risk the Spaniard being unable to reach his potential

New centre back signing Jeremy Jacquet is currently injured and missed the first pre-season game against Sunderland

Joe Gomez, the long-serving versatile defender, pulled up in the Reds’ pre-season opener against Sunderland here in Nashville. ‘Probably the worst news,’ was how Iraola put it, a few days on from when he admitted they were ‘very thin’ in defence.

Gomez is an admirable gentleman and is adored by many in the dressing room and fanbase but the cold, hard truth is that you cannot trust his body. Transfermarkt data records that this is his ninth separate lay-off since the start of the 2023-24 season.

He started seven league games last term, six the season before. We do not know the severity of his injury yet but whether it is two days or two months on the sidelines, the situation is clear.

Beyond those two senior defenders, Liverpool have two youngsters who they believe are two of the best defensive talents in world football. But they have zero Premier League minutes between them and – you guessed it – are both out of action right now.

Jeremy Jacquet, the 21-year-old who signed from Rennes for £55m in January, is here in the United States but is being carefully managed. Given he did not play for the French club beyond February 7 due to a shoulder problem, he is being afforded an extended training block before playing.

After sitting out the friendly with Sunderland, it is believed he will do the same against Wrexham in New York City on Wednesday and is eyeing a first Reds outing against Leeds in Chicago next weekend.

Giovanni Leoni is the other option. The 19-year-old signed this time last year from Parma and is a true Italian stallion with Terminator-like looks. But the comparisons stop there as he has spent the best part of a year out after tearing his cruciate ligament on debut in September.

Even when Jacquet and Leoni are back, which the club are hoping will not be too far away, they are unproven, inexperienced and would be better suited being eased in slowly. As it is, they are likely to need to dive head-first into the deep end.

Virgil van Dijk is currently the only fit centre back, but is 35 and yet to start pre-season

It has left teenagers Mor Talla Ndiaye and Ifeanyi Ndukwe needing to play there in pre-season, though the latter is lacking a work permit and is likely to be loaned out this term.

Van Dijk is now 35 and the captain is entering the final year of his deal, as is Gomez. The Dutchman remains one of the best defenders on the planet but cannot be relied on forever, as hard as that might be to admit for some Reds fans.

All of a sudden, the need to sign a defender rises to the top of Liverpool’s shopping list alongside recruiting the Mohamed Salah replacement on the right wing.

With Hugo Ekitike a long-term injury with a ruptured Achilles and Alexander Isak missing the majority of his first campaign on Merseyside with several problems, the Reds look extremely light at that end of the pitch, too.

Every criticism of Arne Slot last season was amplified given he had been backed with a mega £450million summer outlay with the big-money buys of Isak, Ekitike and Florian Wirtz.

A year on, it feels like Iraola is lacking several tools to achieve his – and Liverpool’s – lofty ambitions this season.

The Basque boss has impressed during his opening weeks at the club, both in his public addresses and in the opening friendly here in Tennessee.

Liverpool are back at base in Chicago and have been met by Wirtz, Isak and Ryan Gravenberch who have joined up with the squad after missing the first part of pre-season due to their participation in the World Cup.

But if Iraola is not backed with at least two or three more arrivals, then the former Bournemouth manager faces an uphill struggle to return Liverpool to glory.

With news this week circulating that Amazon billionaire Jeff Bezos is part of a consortium to buyout a £1.35billion stake in the club, Liverpool could do with a defender on next-day delivery.

Sports.title: Luke Littler fronts new Netflix show where darts fans can win eye-watering £501k prize
Sports.content:
Luke Littler fronts new Netflix show where darts fans can win eye-watering £501k prize

Luke Littler is in a league of his own at the top of professional darts, yet plucky fans will be hoping to get the better of 'The Nuke' on a new Netflix show which offers a huge prize

View 2 Images Luke Littler won the World Matchplay trophy on Sunday (Image: Ben Roberts Photo/Getty Images)

Darts fans will be given the chance to take on Luke Littler in a new Netflix show which is offering £501,000 to anyone who can beat the world No.1.

‌



Littler may only be 19 years old but he is already well established as the best player in the world - and one of the best of all time. His victory over Gerwyn Price in the World Matchplay final on Sunday night saw him continue his utter dominance of the sport and set new records.

‌



Littler won 18-9, claimed £225,000 in prize money and broke Phil Taylor's long-standing records for the highest average across the tournament and in the final. He has now claimed £3,143,500 over the PDC's two-year order of merit - and now is ready to give an everyday player the chance to pocket some serious cash.

‌



The Nuke will step up to the oche and take on pub players, with Netflix putting up a gigantic prize to anyone who can achieve the impossible. 'Beat Luke Littler' will be aired live on the streaming giant on October 30 and will include regional heats in Manchester and London in September before 20 competitors take on Littler in a single leg.

"Everyone thinks they can beat me," Littler said. "Now they get a chance to prove it. Bring it on."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Alan Shearer's daughter marries England star in lavish wedding ceremony READ MORE :

Adam Peaty breaks down in tears and makes heartbreaking comment about family feud READ MORE :

A statement from Netflix read: “The rules are simple: one night, one chance, and one perfect leg of 501. If an amateur can defeat darts prodigy Luke Littler, they will walk away with a life-changing £501,000.

“Produced in partnership with the PDC, the governing body behind professional darts, the show will be rooted in the authentic world of competitive darts, bringing the sport’s electric atmosphere live on Netflix.

“To kick off the launch, Netflix has officially opened the nationwide recruitment search to find the 20 competitors brave enough to step up."

‌



View 2 Images Luke Littler is in ridiculous form right now (Image: Ben Roberts Photo/Getty Images)

Littler is operating on an entirely different level in darts, having won the World Championship, UK Open, Premier League and the Masters already in 2026. He's earned £2.13m more than world No.2 Luke Humphries in the current PDC cycle and believes there's still room for improvement.

“I can still get better,” he said in Blackpool after beating Price. “I can get a lot better. Through the matches, I was up to a 120 average at one point and I didn’t make it stick. Maybe in a few years’ time I will stick it and go up to a 120 average.

Article continues below

“At the minute I’m playing some of the best stuff and I’ve just got to keep it there… The main goal was to win every major once. I don’t know how many years are left in me. We’re still only two and a half years into my professional career. It’s far from done.”

Price, who averaged an impressive 104.97 in the final but was still way off Littler's standards, issued a warning to potential competitors. "Luke is one in a million, I threw everything at him," the Welshman said.

"He's fantastic for the sport. I wish he wasn't as good as he is - I would have won a couple more tournaments. I hope there's no-one else like him coming through because he's ridiculous!"

Sports.title: Former England rugby captain teams up with Strictly star for triathlon challenge
Sports.content:
Former England rugby captain teams up with Strictly star for triathlon challenge

Chris Robshaw and Julian Caillon were among those to take part in the London T100 Triathlon weekend.

View Image Former England rugby captain Chris Robshaw in action during the London T100 Triathlon.

Chris Robshaw swapped his rugby boots for his swimming cap, bike and running shoes as he completed his first ever triathlon at the London T100 Triathlon this weekend.

‌



The former England rugby captain raced alongside his BBC Strictly Come Dancing co-star and professional dancer Julian Caillon at the ExCeL arena in a bid to raise money for the Kerslake-Robshaw Foundation. The charity funds projects across the UK that help young people facing barriers build confidence, improve wellbeing, find belonging and unlock their potential.

‌



Robshaw and Caillon both took part in the Olympic distance triathlon, which included a 1.5km swim in Royal Victoria Dock, a 40km bike ride around the Docklands and then a 10km run around London’s ExCeL Centre. The 40-year-old was aiming to break the four-hour mark and subsequently smashed his expectations as he came home in a time of 3:14:59.

‌



“I was excited when I got here,” said Robshaw, who made 66 appearances for his county and finished 13th in last year’s series of Strictly. “But then I got in the water, and honestly, on my first lap, it’s like I forgot how to swim.”

“I couldn’t breathe, and it was so hard. That first lap was so hard. I thought I might not get back in. Then I got back in and the second lap was all right, and the bike and the run were actually the quickest I’ve done. To finish with 3:14:59, I’m really pleased with that, considering I wanted to do sub-four hours.”

“It’s been a great experience. The crowd’s been amazing. I’m still in one piece, which is important… and loved it.”

‌



Australian Caillon, who has done multiple triathlons previously, finished in 2:38:38, while his fiancée Sofia Ochoa, also racing for the Kerslake-Robshaw team, finished in 2:39:01.

“This was actually my first Olympic distance triathlon. I’ve done a couple of other distances, but this was my first Olympic and my first T100 Triathlon event, and I was really, really excited for it,” said Caillon.

“Today was really good. I had a lot of fun. I went the wrong way on the swim [laughs] which happens to me every time. But, no, it was an awesome vibe. The weather was great. It was a lot of fun. I was a bit crampy on the run, but apart from that, yeah, awesome finish. Here in the ExCeL as well, finishing off and everyone cheering for you. Yeah, it was a really, really fun day.”

‌



“The Kerslake-Robshaw Foundation is obviously Chris and Camilla’s foundation, and they use sport and music to help young people and so we’re trying to raise money, raise awareness as well. It’s a great cause. They do a lot of great work with the community.

“I think triathlon can help everyone in so many different ways. I think the beauty of it is you’ve got three disciplines. So you’ve just got to hope that you’re somewhat good at one of them! But, to be honest, I think the community aspect is what’s drawn me into it.”

Robshaw and Caillon were the amateur ‘starter’ before the world’s best short distance triathletes competed in the World Triathlon Championship Series (WTCS) London.

Article continues below

Australian Matthew Hauser won the elite men’s race while Frenchwoman Cassandre Beaugrand took the spoils in the women’s event. British stars Alex Yee, Georgia Taylor-Brown and Beth Potter all took part too, with Yee coming home in 14th while Taylor-Brown and Potter finished sixth and fourth respectively.

In total, 5,300 amateur triathletes will take part across the weekend, from experienced triathletes tackling the T100 distance on Sunday to first-time swim, bike and run participants taking on the shorter Super Sprint, Sprint and Olympic distance triathlons as well as Team Relays.

British stars, including Alex Yee, Beth Potter, Georgia Taylor-Brown, and Sophie Evans, competed at the World Triathlon Championship Series (WTCS) London, with Olympic qualifying points on the line. For more information visit Triathlonlive.tv and TNT Sports in the UK.

Sports.title: Alex Yee denied dream homecoming as Olympic champion crashes bike in London T100
Sports.content:
Alex Yee denied dream homecoming as Olympic champion crashes bike in London T100

The Olympic champion loved racing in his home city but was unable to finish on the podium

View Image Alex Yee races through the run leg during the World Triathlon Championship Series event in London.

Alex Yee was unable to produce the podium finish he wanted on his return to World Triathlon Championship Series racing in London as he came home in 14th.

‌



The Olympic champion faced a difficult afternoon after struggling in the swim, before a crash during the bike stage left him well back heading into the final discipline. Despite the setbacks, Yee delivered the quickest run of any athlete (13:52) to fight his way back through the field and give the passionate British crowd something to shout about as he crossed the line.

‌



“It’s just not quite the swim delivery I wanted,” said Yee. “After about 100 metres of the swim, I just got very much caught up between two or three guys, just literally kind of shoulder-to-shoulder. From that point, it was very much trying to salvage my swim rather than try and be positive with it. I managed to move up well through the boys and then lose a little bit on the way back in.

‌



“I was able to ride fairly well. I was able to move up a little bit on the bike into that second group. At one point, I thought we were going to progress pretty well, but then they got working at the front. Maybe a little bit of motorbike assistance as well came into play.

“Unfortunately, I had a little bit of a crash on the way back into T2, but these things happen.”

Dylan Fletcher sees positives despite Team Emirates GBR suffering SailGP disappointment READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino slams FIFA critics in bizarre letter that glosses over World Cup issues READ MORE :

Matthew Hauser claimed the WTCS London victory after a strong all-round performance, with Vasco Vilaça finishing second and Csongor Lehmann third.

‌



The Australian’s win moved him to third in the overall standings while Max Stapley was the best-finishing Brit in 12th.

While the result was not what he had hoped for, Yee said being able to complete the race on home soil and test himself again was an important step forward after a difficult period.

“I was able to be inspired by the amazing crowd that came out here, that pushed me through that run,” he continued. “I’m proud to just be able to finish a race, to be honest, and be able to push myself to the limit, because there’s been a few reasons why I haven’t been able to do that before.”

‌



Yee also praised the return of WTCS racing to London, with the unique venue of the ExCeL allowing athletes to race close to the fans and create a memorable atmosphere.

He said: “I think massive kudos to World Triathlon that we were able to have a race back here. I hope it stays, and we can continue having this for many years to come. London 2012 is something which left an impact on me, and hopefully this can light a fire for someone else watching.”

Looking ahead, Yee remains focused on his long-term goals, including the challenge of qualifying for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics. But he knows there is still work to do, particularly in the swim, where he believes he is currently below his best level.

Article continues below

“I’d say pride, to be honest,” Yee said when asked about his emotions after the race. “I’m proud that I was able to give it 100%. You can’t be one per cent off in any of these disciplines, and I’m probably five per cent off where I need to be in the swim, or where I have been in the swim.”

Sports.title: Dylan Fletcher sees positives despite Team Emirates GBR suffering SailGP disappointment
Sports.content:
Dylan Fletcher sees positives despite Team Emirates GBR suffering SailGP disappointment

Dylan Fletcher believes Team Emirates GBR were unfortunate to miss the SailGP final in Portsmouth, with the reigning champions finishing bottom of their group despite flashes of promise on home waters.

View Image Team Emirates GBR driver Dylan Fletcher competes on the Solent during the SailGP event in Portsmouth.

Driver Dylan Fletcher felt Team Emirates GBR were unfortunate to finish bottom of Group B at their home SailGP race in front of a 20,000-strong crowd on the Solent.

‌



The British boat finished fifth and sixth in their two group fleet races, missing out on qualification for the final at the Emirates Great Britain Sail Grand Prix in Portsmouth by eight points, with the Swedish and Swiss boats progressing instead. Fletcher did see his crew storm off the line in the final race, only to be pipped to the first mark by the Swiss, resulting in a terminal loss of speed and falling off the foils.

‌



He said: “It was difficult. In the first race we just got boxed around a bit and didn't really have the opportunity very often to go where we wanted, and the second race was over after mark one for us. We know we chipped away and got back into the fleet a bit but ultimately we were miles behind after being off the foils.

‌



“Yesterday we didn't start well enough in two races and from there the level was higher in our fleet than the other fleet.

BONDS Flying Roos, the season championship leaders from Australia, were unable to progress too, instead ceding the top two positions to Canada’s NorthStar and Spain’s Los Gallos. And it was the Spanish who clinched their second consecutive victory and went clear of reigning SailGP champions Emirates GBR in second place, with USA SailGP Team and Sweden’s Artemis both leapfrogging the Brits in the championship too.

Fletcher said: “Especially yesterday, there weren't many overtaking lanes so it's very difficult for us to come back from those poor starts. It was different today - we managed to get on top of the starts and worked with the whole team to remedy that. That was nice to see, so as frustrating as it is, there are some little positives to take away from the weekend but it unravelled after that in both races.

‌



“It was a fairly slow bleed in the first race and I can't quite put my finger on what happened. Then in the second race, there was a fundamental mistake round mark one. I don't know exactly what it was but effectively, that was race over at that point.”

The previous race in Halifax saw teams split into two groups for the fleet racing, a format that SailGP is set to continue until the end of the season.

Fletcher said: “The longer group racing goes on, the fairer it becomes. You inevitably end up with a higher quality and lower quality fleet each weekend, and it can just be down to conditions and what goes on.

Article continues below

“I think the B fleet was the tougher fleet this time around, but next time around it might be different.

“I thought it was a fantastic course today with really interesting racing opportunities and great positioning in front of the crowd.”

The Emirates Great Britain Sail Grand Prix returned to Portsmouth at the weekend. For more information about what happened, please visit //SailGP.com/Portsmouth

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford told to release 'almighty statement' to save Man Utd career
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford told to release 'almighty statement' to save Man Utd career

Marcus Rashford saw a dream move to Barcelona fall through following his loan spell and the forward is expected to return to parent side Manchester United in the coming weeks

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford is due to return to Manchester United after his World Cup commitments (Image: Getty Images)

Marcus Rashford has been told to release an 'almighty statement' in a last-ditch effort to save his Manchester United career - but even that might only be enough for a bit-part role.

‌



The Red Devils academy graduate has fallen down the pecking order at Old Trafford over the past few years. He was initially sent out on loan to Aston Villa, before joining Barcelona on a season-long loan deal last term.

‌



The Spanish giants had an option to sign him permanently but decided against it in the end. That decision will see Rashford return to Manchester over the coming weeks, once he rounds off a holiday following his commitments with England at the World Cup.

‌



However, former England international Micky Gray believes Rashford needs to release a lengthy statement re-affirming his commitment to United.

Jadon Sancho finally receives shock contract offer months after Man Utd exit READ MORE :

Free agent XI including Man Utd flop, Liverpool legend and current England star READ MORE :

Speaking on talkSPORT, he said: "There's a few things here. The most important one is, if Rashford has a future at Man United, he has to do an almighty statement of why he wants to be at Man United and what the reasons were to leave the club in the first place.

“I think that's a priority that he has to do. If he does stay then he's got to get used to being a bit-part player.

‌



"He's not first on the list; he's not going to be playing every week...[Bryan] Mbuemo, [Matheus] Cunha, [Benjamin] Sesko, Amad to name a few. They've caught up to and if not surpassed Rashford.

"Spain is not England. He did very well, but he can play at Barcelona at a different level to what he can at Man United. He can't deny that the Premier League is 100mph – he's going to have to get himself super fit in pre-season.

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford has not played for Manchester United in nearly two years (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"We saw the good and the bad of Rashford for England at the World Cup… can Man United utilise him in a way they can expect to see the good side and bad side? If they do that and he stays… Rashford has got to expect that he isn't going to play every game."

Rashford still has two years remaining on his contract with United, having only penned a new deal in 2023. He reportedly earns around £325,000 per week at Old Trafford.

It has been suggested that the Red Devils have set his price at around £40m despite Barcelona having had an option of £25m to sign him permanently in the summer.

Sports.title: Eduardo Saverin's huge net worth as Facebook co-founder approached over Liverpool investment
Sports.content:
Eduardo Saverin's huge net worth as Facebook co-founder approached over Liverpool investment

The transfer window is normally focused on the players on the pitch, but a recent report has suggested there may be a change coming in Liverpool's ownership

View 3 Images Eduardo Saverin has reportedly been approached to invest in Liverpool FC (Image: Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin has been approached by a consortium looking to purchase a share in Liverpool. Saverin, 44, is understood to have a net worth of around £24.3billion.

‌



Were he to involve himself in investing in the club, he would become the third wealthiest owner/co-owner in the Premier League. Only Newcastle United's Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund owners (£723.3bn) and Manchester City's 'City Football Group' bosses (£24.5bn) would boast a bigger net-worth than Saverin.

‌



In 2022, Saverin was part of a consortium which failed in an attempt to takeover Chelsea after Roman Abramovich was forced to sell the club.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

His £24.3bn net worth, according to Bloomberg Billionaires Index, would be more than welcome by the consortium looking to purchase a stake in the club. It's understood the syndicate could look to become the second-largest shareholder at Anfield.

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos was also reported as another potential investor in the aforementioned consortium. At present, nothing has been decided in regards to Saverin being involved in the consortium.

‌



What is known is that it's currently being spearheaded by Amit Bhatia, the son-in-law of steel billionaire Lakshmi Mittal. The figure the consortium may look to purchase is understood to be around 30 per cent.

View 3 Images Eduardo Saverin has an enormous net worth (Image: Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Fenway Sports Group have been the majority stakeholders in Liverpool since 2010. A potential purchase could value the Reds at a whopping $6bn (£4.5bn) which would rank amongst the most lucrative deals in English football history.

‌



At present, Chelsea's takeover by the BlueCo consortium is the largest club purchase in English football history. When they won the bidding process at Stamford Bridge, the purported sale was worth around £4.25bn.

A spokesperson for FSG said last week: "An investment consortium led, managed, and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club."

View 3 Images Jeff Bezos has also been approached over investing in Liverpool FC (Image: Anadolu, Anadolu via Getty Images)

‌



In 2023, Dynasty Equity purchased a small stake which valued Liverpool at $4.5bn. This came one year after the club said they were open to a full sale of the club, which was confirmed in a statement.

At the time, they said: "FSG has frequently received expressions of interest from third parties seeking to become shareholders in Liverpool. FSG has said before that under the right terms and conditions, we would consider new shareholders if it was in the best interests of Liverpool as a club."

Sports.title: Jadon Sancho finally receives shock contract offer months after Man Utd exit
Sports.content:
Jadon Sancho finally receives shock contract offer months after Man Utd exit

Jadon Sancho has been without a club since letting his deal at Old Trafford expire but it appears that the former Manchester United might not be out of work for much longer

View 2 Images Jadon Sancho could be Qatar-bound (Image: Getty Images)

Jadon Sancho has been handed the chance to complete a sensational move to Qatar after receiving a contract offer from Al-Rayyan. The former £85m man has been without a club since leaving Manchester United at the end of his contract.

‌



Sancho, 26, has been on the lookout for fresh employment since then but with little luck. But it appears he has now been offered a fresh chance to relaunch his career in the Middle East.

‌



According to the French outlet Foot Mercato, Qatari side Al-Rayyan have offered him a deal to sign him on a free transfer. They want the English wideman to be the leading face of their project to dominate football within the country.

‌



It is not revealed whether Sancho is tempted by the move as it stands, but either way, he appears to be closing in on a new club. The winger has also been linked with a return to German side Borussia Dortmund; Sancho having enjoyed a productive spell in the Bundesliga ahead of his big-money switch to Old Trafford.

Free agent XI including Man Utd flop, Liverpool legend and current England star READ MORE :

Since then, Sancho has had loan spells with his former club, Chelsea and Aston Villa. He has had mixed success with his temporary employers, Chelsea having chosen not to sign him permanently despite agreeing an obligation to buy clause with United.

He scored just five goals at Stamford Bridge, while Sancho only got on the scoresheet once during his time at Villa Park.

‌



Speaking last season, Dortmund managing director Lars Ricken suggested that they were interested in signing Sancho a third time. "We are currently looking at a lot of players and analysing them," Ricken said.

"We are assessing whether they can improve our team. We are doing the same with Jadon. Of course, we are looking for an offensive player who brings quality, can help us immediately, and doesn't require an unrealistic transfer fee.”

View 2 Images Jadon Sancho was last with Aston Villa where he won the Europa League (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Elsewhere, former Premier League boss Alan Pardew revealed what managers would be taking into consideration as they mull over a move for Sancho.

Speaking with talkSPORT, he said: "He hasn't really done enough to warrant a massive, massive contract like he was on at Man United, but he'll get a good move.

"When you get to the end of the season, it is an opportunity. You have to make some really tough calls on who to renegotiate with because obviously there's a value to the football club.

Article continues below

"You might actually as a manager want them to go, but the club have a financial interest in them, and wants some money back and get them to re-sign one more year. Let's see if we can move him on. It'll be good for you for the year.’ You have to have all those kinds of debates."

Sports.title: Vinicius Junior transfer: Arsenal ready to break salary record to sign Real Madrid star
Sports.content:
Vinicius Junior transfer: Arsenal ready to break salary record to sign Real Madrid star

Arsenal are lining up a sensational swoop for Vinicius Junior and will offer the Real Madrid star a record-breaking salary in order to prise him away from the Bernabeu

View 2 Images Vinicius Junior currently earns a whopping £400,000 per week (Image: Bruno Penas/Quality Sport Images/Getty Images)

Arsenal would be willing to offer Real Madrid star Vinicius Junior the biggest contract in the club's history in order to complete a mega transfer deal. Vinicius, 26, has emerged as an ambitious target for Arsenal, who are closely monitoring developments regarding his uncertain future in Madrid.

‌



The winger has entered the final year of his contract with Real, who are due to pay him a lucrative loyalty bonus if he stays for the 2026-27 season. Los Blancos risk losing Vinicius on a free transfer next summer if they don't tie him down to a new deal.

‌



A report from the Telegraph states that his eye-watering salary of £400,000 per week wouldn't be a problem for Arsenal. In fact, Emirates chiefs would look to improve those figures in an effort to strengthen their chances of signing the Brazil international.

‌



Vinicius' prospective wages would dwarf those of Arsenal's current highest earner, Bukayo Saka, who signed up to a £365,000-a-week contract in February which will rise each season. The Gunners want to build on their Premier League title win and go one step further in the Champions League, having lost on penalties to Paris Saint-Germain in last season's final.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal learn fee and transfer conditions to sign Vinicius Jr from Real Madrid READ MORE :

Left wing is a position which Mikel Arteta is keen to strengthen, having sold Leandro Trossard to Besiktas. Arsenal have already brought in Christos Tzolis, who can play on both sides of attack, for £34m but don't plan on stopping there.

‌



PSG's Bradley Barcola has been looked at in detail, with Premier League rivals Liverpool also interested in the Frenchman. However, both clubs have been quoted £145m.

Arsenal and Real haven't engaged in direct contact over Vinicius, who Jose Mourinho would be opposed to selling at the start of his second spell in Madrid. But concerns linger over how an attack containing both Vinicius and Kylian Mbappe can work at the highest level.

How much should Arsenal pay for Vinicius Junior? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Jose Mourinho wants to keep Vinicius Junior (Image: Maria Jimenez - Real Madrid/Real Madrid)

Since Mbappe joined Real from PSG in July 2024, weeks after they secured an historic La Liga and Champions League double with Vinicius at the heart of their success, they've failed to win a trophy and been through three permanent managers. Meanwhile, arch enemies Barcelona have won five of the six domestic trophies available.

Real will play their first pre-season friendly on Tuesday, hosting fellow Madrid-based side Leganes. Vinicius won't be involved, as he's still on holiday after the World Cup.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
