World.title: Search intensifies for North Carolina physical therapist who vanished during Caribbean getaway
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A North Carolina woman has vanished while on a trip to the Caribbean island of Grenada, sparking an urgent search as her family, friends and loved ones plead for her safe return.

Elizabeth "Liz" Waddell, 44, was last seen Wednesday at Grand Anse Beach in St. George's, near where she was staying in the Grand Anse area, according to the Royal Grenada Police Force.

Waddell, a physical therapist, wife and mother from the Raleigh area, is described as 5 feet 5 inches tall with short blonde hair. Authorities also released a photo showing Waddell with pink hair as they asked the public for help locating her.

According to her professional website, Waddell is the founder of Art of Movement Physical Therapy and earned a doctorate in physical therapy from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.

SEARCH UNDERWAY FOR AUSTRALIAN WOMAN WHO VANISHED AFTER SENDING MESSAGE ABOUT GOING FOR A HIKE NEAR LAS VEGAS

According to a friend who said she has known Waddell and her husband for more than 20 years, Waddell traveled to Grenada for a vacation with another friend, WRAL News reported.

Waddell's friend reportedly lost sight of her after remaining at their Airbnb to take an online course while Waddell went outside, apparently for a swim.

"She had her swimsuit on, and she went outside their Airbnb," Amanda Romano-Harmon said, according to the local outlet. "They had a pool that overlooked the bay. Liz was set up out there just sightseeing from the pool, and her friend was taking her online course. When she got through with her course, she looked up and she didn't see Liz outside, so she went outside to walk around and see where she went, and she saw her towel down on the pier. So the only thing we can think is maybe she went for a swim."

The friend reportedly became increasingly concerned over the next several hours, knowing Waddell did not have her phone with her, and eventually filed a missing-persons report.

THREE SISTERS FOUND DEAD IN OCEAN AT POPULAR TOURIST BEACH AS POLICE PROBE MYSTERIOUS TRAGEDY

Waddell's husband, Cailen, was at work when he received the call about his wife's disappearance, according to the report.

He said on social media Friday that he was heading to the area to assist in the search and urged anyone with connections to the island to share information that could help locate her.

He also described Waddell as a kind-hearted person while speaking with local Grenada media outlets.

"My wife is a loving, free-spirited person. She could make friends with anyone. She often did," he told Grenada Broadcasting Network (GBN).

Police are urging anyone with information about Waddell's whereabouts to come forward, specifically asking fishermen, boat operators and residents along Grenada's southern coastline to report any sightings that could assist in the search.

KENTUCKY MAN CHARGED WITH BOATING UNDER THE INFLUENCE AFTER FEMALE PASSENGER, 19, GOES MISSING

According to GBN, an extensive search effort is underway with the assistance of police officers, divers and students from St. George's University.

The U.S. State Department told Fox News Digital on Sunday that officials are aware of reports of a missing American citizen in Grenada and emphasized that the Trump Administration has no higher priority than the safety and security of U.S. citizens abroad.

The State Department declined to provide additional details due to privacy considerations but said it can assist families and friends with filing missing persons reports and help them understand local procedures.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Aradia Fitness, where Waddell also works as a fitness instructor, called the news of her disappearance "disheartening" in a social media post and said the community is praying for her safe return.

Anyone with information is urged to contact the South Saint George Police Station at 444-4454, the Criminal Investigation Department at 440-3921, the police emergency line at 911, or the nearest police station, the Royal Grenada Police Force said.

World.title: Shootout at Seattle food festival kills 3; police arrest gunman and search for another
World.content:
Three people were killed and four others were injured in what police believe was a shootout between a pair of gunmen at a major food festival in Seattle on Sunday night.

Subscribe to read this story ad-free Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.

One gunman surrendered after being confronted by police while another gunman is being searched for after fleeing Seattle Center, which was hosting the Bite of Seattle event, Assistant Seattle Police Chief Tyrone Davis said during a late night news conference.

“There were two people who we believe were shooting at each other,” Davis said.

Seven people had been shot, he said, two of whom died at the scene at the civic center complex, which is also home to the city’s Space Needle.

Four people who were injured, including a toddler, were taken to Harborview Medical Center, the region’s top-level trauma center, where one of them died, Davis said. Hospital spokesperson Susan Gregg said the victims had injuries including gunshot wounds to an arm, leg, abdomen and lower leg.

Another person arrived later at University of Washington Medical Center with a gunshot wound, Davis said, adding that all the injured had been stabilized.

Gregg said earlier that one woman was in critical condition and in surgery; it was unclear if that woman was the third victim who died. “The other patients are in satisfactory condition (a pediatric male patient, a 23-year-old male and a 39-year-old female),” Gregg said by email.

Seattle Fire Department spokesperson Grace Nuñez said one patient, a 40-year-old woman with minor injuries, declined to be taken to a hospital.

A police officer responding to the shooting at the Bite of Seattle food festival Sunday. Lindsey Wasson / AP

Davis said the gunman taken into custody was being question and is “a young person.” That person was the only one officers saw opening fire, the assistant chief said, noting that police did not discharge their own weapons during the confrontation.

While a second person fled, Davis said that, “We believe that we have no outstanding threat to the community.”

Two guns were recovered at the scene, he said.

Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson called the shooting “an unbelievable tragedy, a horrific act of violence.”

“My heart right now is with the victims and their families, and with everyone in our community who is reeling from what happened here today,” she said during the news conference.

In a statement earlier, she thanked first responders, including firefighters, event staff and bystanders who helped people get to safety, as well as hospital staff who treated the wounded.

The Seattle office of the U.S. ⁠Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives said on X that some of its special agents were at the scene assisting Seattle police with the investigation.

Rep. Pramila Jayapal, D-Wash., said officials would work to get federal resources.

The food festival was wrapping up its annual event Sunday, the final of its three days.

Estan Wakonabo was waiting in line with his girlfriend for a photo booth when people around them started running furiously, he told NBC affiliate KING of Seattle.

“It was a stampede,” he said.

Not long afterward, Wakonabo said, he noticed people on the ground, some with obvious gunshot wounds.

“There’s bodies everywhere,” he said of those on the ground who appeared to be injured. “I mean, I counted eight.”

Paul Skinner was helping operate a Bite of Seattle booth for the food truck Crave when chaos erupted, he said.

“We just heard what at first sounded like firecrackers, but it’s just a little too crowded for that kind of thing,” he told KING. “So then, when the crowd started moving quickly in herds, you knew it was something was happening.”

He added, “We all got down and took cover.”

The entrance to Bite of Seattle at Seattle Center on Sunday. Lindsey Wasson / AP

Isaiah Flores Sanches described hearing the gunfire.

“It went from something being so playful and so joyful to being something so horrific, and I seen people on the floor trying to take cover,” he told KING.

Bite of Seattle says it draws more than 350,000 people to its annual three-day festival, for which admission is free. “The Bite of Seattle is a very positive event,” Davis said. “We haven’t had any issue in recent years.”

Organizers did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The civic center complex that grew into Seattle Center included core structures erected for the 1962 Seattle World’s Fair, including the Coliseum, the Seattle Center Monorail and the Space Needle.

World.title: Minnesota state Sen. John Hoffman says Angie Craig sought his endorsement while he was in ICU
World.content:
Democratic Minnesota state Sen. John Hoffman said Friday that Rep. Angie Craig, D-Minn., sought his endorsement for her U.S. Senate campaign while he was in intensive care following the June 2025 attempt on his life.

Subscribe to read this story ad-free Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.

Hoffman said in a statement to NBC News on Sunday that a “dear and trusted friend” approached him for an endorsement twice — once while he was in the intensive care unit and the second time while he was recovering at home — and that the friend “confirmed that the endorsement requests came from Congresswoman Craig.”

Hoffman’s remarks came at a campaign event for Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan, who is also seeking the Democratic Senate nomination.

“When [Craig] said she wanted my endorsement, she was doing that during moments when our family’s story had high visibility, and that’s all you need to know that the difference is between the opponent that Peggy has and Peggy Flanagan. Because Peggy Flanagan, she checked on us out of her love for how we were doing and if we were OK,” Hoffman said at a rally Friday in St. Paul, at which Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., was also present.

Asked about the allegations, a spokesperson for Flanagan said, “That’s a matter between Congresswoman Craig and the Hoffmans.”

A spokesperson for Craig said in a statement that “the claim is categorically false.”

“The Congresswoman reached out to Senator Hoffman only expressing deep sympathy from her and her wife, Cheryl, after their horrific shooting while he was in the ICU and did not reach out again until August 5, after he began making political endorsements in other races again,” the spokesperson said. “The Congresswoman continues to pray and keeps John, Yvette and Hope Hoffman in her thoughts and is grateful for their continued recovery.”

Craig denied Hoffman’s claims in an interview with KMSP-TV of Minneapolis, to which Hoffman responded in his statement.

“Let me be equally clear: I told the truth about what Yvette and I experienced,” Hoffman said about himself and his wife, who was also shot during the assassination attempt.

Rep. Angie Craig, D-Minn., at the U.S. Capitol last year. Chip Somodevilla / Getty Images file

In text messages the Craig campaign provided to NBC News, Craig expresses well-wishes for the Hoffmans on June 14 — the day of the shooting — and she later sends an Aug. 5 message saying she “would love to talk with you about the open Senate race when you’re up to it.”

Hoffman was released from the intensive care unit on July 7.

NBC News has made attempts to contact and confirm the identity of the “dear and trusted friend” Hoffman referred to in his statement as having visited him in the intensive care unit.

Hoffman added in his statement that he “acknowledged” Craig sent a message expressing sympathy following the shooting, but he said his campaign remarks were in reference to subsequent endorsement requests “and the painful impression those requests left on our family while we were trying to survive and recover.”

“It is dishonest to give condolences and then immediately ask for endorsement like her text showed,” Hoffman wrote.

State Sen. Erin Maye Quade said in an interview with NBC News on Sunday that when she visited Hoffman at the intensive care unit rehabilitation facility in late July, he shared the story about someone seeking an endorsement on behalf of Craig.

“He had mentioned that there was a friend of his that had come, who was also a surrogate and working with Angie’s campaign, and had asked him for his endorsement. We were both like, ‘Oh, it’s so inappropriate,’ and he was like: ‘I know. I think he felt really bad about doing it,’” Quade said, adding that the story has not been “secret or private” since then and that Hoffman has mentioned it to other people “at various points over the last year.”

Hoffman added in his statement Sunday that Flanagan’s contact with the Hoffmans was “different” and said she had reached out to check in on the family and “sought nothing in return.”

“My remarks were about that contrast, and I remain accountable for every word I said,” Hoffman wrote. “Congresswoman Craig may disagree with my endorsement. She may defend her campaign’s conduct. But she does not get to rewrite what my family experienced or publicly attack my honesty.”

Vance Boelter, 59, pleaded guilty last month to six federal counts in connection with the stalking and shooting of the Hoffmans, in addition to the murders of House Speaker Emerita Melissa Hortman and her husband, Mark Hortman. Boelter was sentenced to two consecutive terms of life in prison and an additional 40 years, the maximum sentence short of the death penalty.

World.title: 3 killed, 4 wounded in shooting near Seattle's Space Needle, authorities say
World.content:
Three people were killed and four others wounded in a shooting at a food festival near Seattle's Space Needle on Sunday evening, police said. A suspect was arrested and another was being sought, they said.

Seattle Assistant Police Chief Tyrone Davis told a late night press conference the incident involved two people they believe were shooting at each other — one was taken into custody and the other was still on the loose, but they didn't think there was an ongoing threat to the public.

Davis said officers working in the area rushed in and confronted one shooter, which kept more people from being wounded. Two guns were recovered, he added.

Davis said seven people were shot in all. CPR on two wasn't successful and they were pronounced dead at the scene and a third, a 56-year-old woman, later died at Harborview Medical Center. The hospital had said earlier that she was in surgery.

A two-year-old boy, 39-year-old woman and 23-year-old man were also taken to Harborview and were in stable condition, Davis said, adding that a 40-year-old woman with minor injuries didn't want to go to the hospital but showed up later at the University of Washington Medical Center.

The shooting occurred around 6 p.m. local time.

Police cover a person after a shooting at Seattle Center during the Bite of Seattle food festival on Sunday, July 26, 2026, in Seattle, Washington. Estan Wakonabo

The federal Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives said Sunday night that several of its agents were at the scene and that Seattle police would lead the investigation. Washington Gov. Bob Ferguson said the state SWAT team was en route, at the request of Seattle police.

The Seattle Center is a popular tourist location that includes the iconic Space Needle and Climate Pledge Arena, home of the Seattle Kraken and Seattle Storm. The area was filled with people attending the annual Bite of Seattle food festival when the gunfire rang out.

Several witnesses told CBS Seattle affiliate KIRO-TV they heard multiple shots before running away.

"At first, thought there were fireworks, and then everybody flooded and ran past us," Nick Bate told the station.

Leanne Coles told KIRO, "Everybody started running, and so we just ran too, and we ran through the garden and we ducked and we decided to keep running with the crowd until we got- I looked up for the Space Needle to try to keep track of where we were. It was really scary."

World.title: Pentagon lists 4 killed in Iran war under "Overseas Operations Casualties"
World.content:
The Pentagon website that informs the public about the dead and wounded in military conflicts now lists four service members killed in Jordan and Iraq in July under "Overseas Operations Casualties" — separate from 14 other service members who have been killed during the war with Iran.

The other 14 appear in the database as casualties of Operation Epic Fury, the Defense Department's name for the conflict. At one point last week, the four service members' deaths also appeared on that list, but by last Thursday, their names no longer appeared there, and the database said that 14 were killed in the war with Iran, as opposed to 18.

The New York Times first reported the database's missing numbers and cited three sources who said it was because the four service members who were most recently killed died after the Trump administration had declared a ceasefire in April.

But the four service members were killed about a week after President Trump notified Congress by letter that the ceasefire was over and military action had resumed on July 7. The four who died are 1st Lt. Tyler James Feehan, Sgt. Angel S. Rampersad, Pvt. Isabella Gonzales and Sgt. Michael Emmanuel Swinton.

Sean Parnell, the chief Pentagon spokesperson, in a statement shared on X last Thursday, blamed "site errors on the Defense Casualty Analysis System" on "a temporary data disruption" and said the "site anomalies are currently being resolved in coordination with the Military Services." Parnell in his statement slammed the New York Times for "colluding with anonymous sources to push a completely fake story."

When the Pentagon first released the names of two of the three killed in an Iranian attack in Jordan earlier this month, it initially classified them as deaths under Operation Inherent Resolve, the name for the years-long mission targeting ISIS. Later, the Defense Department amended the releases to say the service members had died in "overseas operations."

Throughout the war with Iran, the Pentagon has been slow to provide information about injuries. After the New York Times reported earlier this week that dozens of troops had been injured in attacks in the Middle East, the Pentagon initially referred reporters with questions on the wounded to the website — even though it had not been updated in several days and did not account for the recent deaths.

Defense officials have not briefed reporters on the Iran war since May, and they have not commented on the categorization of the deaths of the four service members.

CBS News first reported and Parnell confirmed that nearly 100 U.S. service members had been injured since July 7. In a statement on X, he said that among those injured, 96% had returned to duty and the vast majority of injuries experienced "were minor concussions." Minor concussions can often be traumatic brain injuries that vary in severity and can display symptoms some time after the initial injury.

He concluded by saying that "further updates will be posted on the Defense Casualty Analysis System."

As of Sunday, the site said 417 service members have been wounded in the war with Iran, which is dozens fewer than the 482 it listed early last week. Now, 207 service members are listed as having been wounded in Overseas Operations.

World.title: Colorado River reservoirs hit record lows as government threatens major cuts
World.content:
A deepening water crisis in the Western United States has reached an impasse as disagreement among affected states is grinding progress to a halt, and the well of potential solutions is close to running dry.

The nation's two largest reservoirs — Lake Mead and Lake Powell on the Colorado River — have fallen to their lowest levels on record. It's a moment of reckoning in the drought-stricken West as seven states can't agree on how to share the rapidly shrinking water supply.

The Colorado River is a lifeline for the region, and it's the line dividing the upper basin states, Colorado, Wyoming, Utah and New Mexico, and the lower basin states, California, Arizona and Nevada.

Kelly Shannon McNeill, the managing director of LA Waterkeeper, an organization that serves as a water watchdog, told CBS News that California and other lower basin states have cut use of the Colorado River by nearly 20% since 2015. But the upper basin states "have gone in the opposite direction," McNeill said.

"In the last year alone, they've increased their use over the same period and say they can't afford cuts. And so this is really, you know, it's about political will," she said.

FILE - A record-low snowpack across the Colorado River Basin is intensifying concerns at Lake Powell, where water levels remain low near Page, Arizona. RJ Sangosti/MediaNews Group/The Denver Post via Getty Images

After years of failed negotiations between the states, the Trump administration is now poised to impose sweeping cuts.

California, Arizona and Nevada have offered to cut their use by about 1.6 million acre-feet, or roughly 500 billion gallons, a year for the next two years.

However, federal officials who control the water flow are considering cuts nearly twice that amount. The major cuts would likely mean higher costs for cities trying to secure water, tighter restrictions on outdoor water and significant changes for farmers who use the majority of the river's supply.

"I would urge those people living in those states to contact their elected representatives and their negotiators at the table, and really urge them to come to the table ... and come up with some sort of agreement," McNeill said.

Water in the Colorado River begins as snow in the Rocky Mountains, but a warming climate has led to less snowpack and less snowmelt feeding the river each spring. Population growth in the region has also amplified the crisis.

The two Arizona Intake Towers (L) and two Nevada Intake Towers on the upstream side of the Hoover Dam are shown on July 25, 2026 in the Lake Mead National Recreation Area, Arizona. Ethan Miller / Getty Images

If the water in Lake Powell falls just 33 more feet, the reservoir will no longer meet the water levels needed to generate hydroelectric power, meaning the water can't move through the dam into the Colorado River.

And with both Lake Mead and Lake Powell at less than 30% full, residents can't afford for decision makers to waste time.
