World.title: Iraqi oil exports continue as Red Sea and Hormuz shipping slows
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Shipping activity through two of the world’s most critical maritime chokepoints has slowed sharply following renewed security concerns in the Middle East, according to new data from maritime analytics firm Kpler.

The latest figures show vessel traffic through both the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and the Strait of Hormuz has fallen to its lowest levels in months, as shipping companies remain cautious despite changing regional dynamics.

According to Kpler, traffic through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait slowed significantly after Houthi forces launched attacks on Saudi Aramco oil facilities in Jizan and Yanbu.

The attacks have added fresh uncertainty to Red Sea shipping routes, prompting many operators to reassess transit schedules and security risks. The Red Sea remains one of the world’s busiest energy corridors, making any disruption closely watched by global oil markets.

Shipping activity through the Strait of Hormuz also remained subdued, even after direct military strikes between the United States and Iran came to a halt.

Kpler data shows vessel movements stayed limited over the weekend, reflecting continued caution among shipping companies despite the easing of immediate hostilities. Security concerns continue to influence routing decisions, insurance costs, and freight rates across the Gulf.

Despite the ongoing maritime disruptions, Iraq’s oil exports continue to move through the Strait of Hormuz. According to Kpler, two Very Large Crude Carriers (VLCCs) carrying Iraqi and Emirati crude successfully transited the strategic waterway on Friday as part of outbound shipments from the Gulf.

The movements indicate that Iraqi crude exports are continuing, although regional security risks remain elevated.

Several additional oil tankers departed the Red Sea carrying Saudi, Emirati, and Russian crude destined for China. Another tanker loaded with Saudi crude also departed for Pakistan, highlighting that regional energy exports continue despite heightened security concerns.

However, markets remain focused on whether prolonged disruptions could tighten global energy supplies and push shipping costs even higher.

The combined slowdown in Bab el-Mandeb and Hormuz underscores the growing impact geopolitical tensions are having on global trade. Both waterways are vital for international energy supplies, and prolonged instability could reshape shipping patterns, increase transportation costs, and place additional pressure on global oil markets.

For Iraq, maintaining uninterrupted crude exports through Hormuz remains critical, as oil revenues continue to account for the vast majority of government income.

World.title: Iraq weather forecast: Temperatures to rise again, with southern provinces to hit 47°C
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Temperatures are set to climb across Iraq once again this week, with the Iraqi Meteorological Authority forecasting another spell of intense summer heat beginning on Tuesday.

According to the latest forecast, most parts of the country will experience clear skies, while northern provinces are expected to see occasional cloud cover. The renewed rise in temperatures comes after a brief period of relatively milder conditions, with southern Iraq once again expected to record the highest readings.

The Meteorological Authority said Tuesday and Wednesday will be mostly sunny nationwide, with some clouds over northern Iraq. Temperatures are expected to increase slightly compared to previous days across all regions.

Maximum temperatures for Tuesday

Duhok, Sulaymaniyah: 42°C

Erbil, Anbar: 43°C

Baghdad, Kirkuk, Karbala, Nineveh, Salahaddin, Diyala: 44°C

Wasit, Najaf, Babil, Diwaniyah, Muthanna: 45°C

Basra, Dhi Qar, Maysan: 47°C

Southern provinces will remain the hottest areas in the country, with temperatures approaching the upper 40s.

The weather is expected to remain clear across most of Iraq through Thursday and Friday. Northern areas will continue to experience intermittent cloud cover, while the central region is forecast to see a slight increase in temperatures on Thursday.

By Friday, temperatures are expected to remain largely unchanged across the country, maintaining the hot summer conditions.

The latest forecast indicates that Iraq will continue to experience typical peak-summer weather, with daytime temperatures remaining well above 40°C in most provinces.

Authorities generally advise residents to avoid prolonged outdoor activities during peak afternoon hours, stay hydrated, and take precautions against heat-related illnesses as temperatures remain exceptionally high.

World.title: Berlin police shoot dead chief suspect in deadly Islamist Pride attack
World.content:
Berlin – German police said Sunday they had shot and killed the chief suspect in what officials described as a deadly Islamist attack near the Berlin Pride parade the previous night, the latest ramming assault to hit the country.

The attack late Saturday — the first such incident to target the German capital’s LGBTQ community — killed one woman and wounded 29 others.

Berlin police said on X that they had traced the chief suspect, 21-year old Abdul Ballout, to an allotment complex in the western Spandau district at around 6:00 pm (1600 GMT) on Sunday.

Ballout “ran towards them with a bladed weapon”, the police said, prompting officers to open fire, “injuring the suspect so that he died at the scene despite attempts to rescusitate him”.

Earlier, prosecutors had said that Ballout, a German citizen of Lebanese origin, had been a supporter of the so-called Islamic State group (IS) with several criminal convictions, the latest dating from May.

Saturday’s attack shattered what had been a day of celebration for hundreds of thousands attending Christopher Street Day (CSD), one of Europe’s largest Pride events.

Politicians in Germany and elsewhere in Europe widely condemned the attack, while the flag at the German Bundestag was lowered to half mast.

Speaking before a memorial service for the victims at Berlin’s Marienkirche church, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz appealed to those targeted by the attack to “not let yourselves be intimidated”.

– Suspect’s criminal past –

Shortly before 10:00 pm (2000 GMT) on Saturday a white minivan ran into people on the southern edge of central Berlin’s Tiergarten park before crashing into a tree.

Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said Ballout was suspected of having then used a machete to attack more people.

Dobrindt said 29 people were injured, some seriously.

Merz said Sunday evening that none of the victims were any longer in a life-threatening condition.

The attack took place several hundred metres away from the end of the tightly guarded CSD parade route and the event’s main stage at Berlin’s Brandenburg Gate.

Dobrindt said Ballout had been known to the authorities for a “high number” of previous crimes and for being radicalised.

“Everything we see here indicates that this was an Islamist terror attack,” he said.

Prosecutors said Ballout had previous convictions for bodily harm and extortion committed in 2019, and one for robbery in 2020.

They say that in 2024 he shared IS propaganda on Instagram and the following year travelled to Lebanon in order to fight for the militia in Syria.

He was arrested in Lebanon and sentenced to three months’ prison.

On his return to Germany in November he was arrested and held until his conviction in May for “preparing a serious act of subversive violence”.

But his sentence of one year and ten months in jail was suspended, partially in recognition of the time he had spent in jail in Lebanon and pre-trial detention, and partially because he had admitted to the crimes and distanced himself from IS.

– ‘Won’t beat us down’ –

In a vigil on Sunday afternoon, hundreds of people packed the square in front of the Brandenburg Gate holding rainbow flags and flowers with more gathering nearby.

Luka, a 23-year-old student, told AFP she hoped the attack wouldn’t be exploited by the surging anti-immigration far-right ahead of elections in the capital and in several regions in September.

At the scene of the attack itself people left flowers and hand-written messages of condolence and support.

Armin Duenhoelter, 49 from Wolfsburg, who works as a drag artist, was backstage at the main stage when the attack cut short the celebrations.

He told AFP early Sunday that he was still shocked but vowed to be back for next year’s CSD.

“We won’t let it beat us down,” he said.

– Spate of attacks –

Saturday’s attack revived memories of a string of similar incidents which have shaken Germany in recent years and inflamed debate on immigration, with several of the perpetrators being from outside Germany.

Martin Hess, a lawmaker from the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), denounced the attack as a result of “a complete failure of the government’s security policies”.

The deadliest attack in recent years was a truck rampage at a Berlin Christmas market in December 2016 by a Tunisian man with jihadist motives that killed 13 people.

The run-up to last year’s general election saw a spate of attacks in public places, including by attackers with Islamist motives.

In 2024, a Saudi psychiatrist and anti-Islam activist killed six people and wounded more than 300 in a car-ramming at a busy Christmas market in the eastern city of Magdeburg.

World.title: Iraq, Lebanon discuss economic partnerships
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi said on Sunday that it is important to establish economic partnerships with Lebanon in different sectors.

Al-Zaidi’s remarks took place during discussions held in Baghdad with Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam and his accompanying delegation, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The two leaders co-chaired discussions between the two countries, where ministers from both sides attended.

The discussions focused on improving bilateral ties in economic, political, and security areas. They also addressed approaches to strengthen the two countries’ partnership to promote comprehensive and long-term development and benefit both the Iraqi and Lebanese people.

Al-Zaidi also highlighted Iraq and Lebanon’s close friendship, dedication to development, and the need to form beneficial economic collaborations across all development areas.

The prime minister also emphasized the importance of joint coordination between the two nations in addressing regional challenges and supporting efforts to boost stability, reduce tensions, and resolve disputes.

World.title: Washington rejects Iraq’s deal with Turkmenistan to import gas
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s plan to purchase Turkmen gas has encountered another obstacle, as the US has raised objections to Baghdad’s proposal to transport the supplies through Iranian territory.

A source told Attaqa News that the United States has connected the agreement’s execution to negotiating a comprehensive political solution with Tehran, complicating the issue of obtaining the fuel required to run Iraq’s power plants.

The US position emerged during talks held in Washington by a government delegation accompanying Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, which included Electricity Minister Ali Wahib and Oil Minister Basim Khudair.

The two sides discussed energy and economic cooperation, but the Turkmen gas sale to Iraq via Iran drew strong American opposition, despite Baghdad’s urgent need for new fuel sources amid a worsening electricity crisis.

The rejection comes amid escalating military operations in the Middle East, with the United States and Iran exchanging attacks, as well as rising tensions in the Arabian Gulf, which have affected maritime security in the Strait of Hormuz.

Iraq signed a memorandum of understanding in 2023 with Turkmenistan to import the necessary gas for its power plants, as stated by the Ministry of Electricity. The ministry indicated that the initiative will necessitate additional negotiations regarding the transportation of gas through Iran.

Power plants in Iraq depend on gas imports from Iran, which cover one-third of the country’s energy needs.

This agreement permits Iran to receive a quarter of the gas supplied across its borders.

The gas supply agreement with Turkmenistan aims to provide Iraq with an average of 20 million cubic meters per day.

World.title: Iraqi court seizes IQD 27 billion in Jumaili’s case
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s anti-corruption judiciary has seized IQD 27 billion in cash as part of an ongoing investigation involving Adnan Al-Jumaili, the detained former Deputy Oil Minister for Refining Affairs, in one of the country’s latest high-profile corruption cases.

Judicial authorities said the money was recovered during investigations into alleged financial losses linked to projects overseen by the former official and other individuals connected to the case.

In a statement issued on Sunday, the media office of Iraq’s judiciary said Judge Diaa Jaafar, the investigating judge at the Central Anti-Corruption Criminal Court, confirmed the seizure of IQD 27 billion.

According to the court, the funds were discovered after investigators traced financial proceeds allegedly generated through waste and irregularities in projects associated with Al-Jumaili and other suspects.

Officials said the cash had been hidden by several individuals believed to be involved in the case. The court said investigators are continuing to pursue additional suspects and trace other assets that may be linked to the alleged offenses.

Judicial authorities indicated that the investigation remains active as efforts continue to identify everyone involved and recover additional public funds, if any are found.

The judiciary also released photographs showing stacks of newly recovered banknotes arranged in large piles following the seizure. According to the statement, the images document the IQD 27 billion recovered during Sunday’s operation, which authorities said had been concealed by individuals connected to the former deputy minister.

Officials did not disclose how many people are under investigation or provide further details about the locations where the money was found.

The case is among several recent corruption investigations pursued by Iraq’s anti-corruption courts as authorities seek to recover public funds and hold officials accountable for alleged financial crimes.

The judiciary reiterated that investigations remain ongoing and that further legal action could follow as additional evidence emerges.

World.title: Iraq completes initial designs for Development Road Project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has completed the preliminary designs for its flagship Development Road Project and railway corridor, marking a major milestone as the government prepares to advance one of its largest infrastructure initiatives into the implementation phase.

The Ministry of Transport announced on Sunday that the initial designs are now 100% complete, with work shifting to detailed engineering plans covering infrastructure, bridges, railway stations, and technical facilities along the project’s route.

According to a source at the ministry’s media office, engineers have begun preparing the project’s detailed designs to ensure the corridor meets international engineering and construction standards. The next phase includes finalizing plans for the railway network, highways, bridges, stations, and supporting infrastructure before construction begins.

Officials described the transition as a key step toward launching the long-awaited project after completing the necessary preparatory stages.

The announcement follows a recent visit by Turkish Transport Minister Abdulkadir Uraloğlu to Baghdad on July 21, where he held talks with Iraqi officials on strengthening cooperation in transport and communications.

During the meetings, Iraqi Transport Minister Wahb Al-Hassani and his Turkish counterpart agreed to accelerate technical planning and implementation procedures for the Development Road Project.

The ministry said both sides consider the corridor a transformative initiative that could reshape regional trade and economic cooperation. The ministry also revealed that Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi has instructed officials to prepare a comprehensive financing mechanism for the project.

Securing funding will be a priority ahead of the project’s implementation and is expected to feature prominently during Al-Zaidi’s upcoming visit to Ankara, where discussions with Turkish officials will focus on advancing strategic cooperation and moving the project toward construction.

The Development Road Project is designed to create a major transport corridor linking Iraq’s ports with regional and international markets. The combined railway and highway network aims to connect the Grand Faw Port in southern Iraq with Turkey and Europe, positioning Iraq as a key logistics hub between Asia and Europe.

Officials say the corridor will significantly improve trade flows while strengthening Iraq’s role in global supply chains. Alongside the engineering work, the Ministry of Transport is preparing the project’s economic model to maximize investment returns and attract local and international partners.

The ministry said the framework will also align with the government’s broader reform agenda, including digital transformation and modern project management systems.

The government views the Development Road Project as one of Iraq’s most important strategic investments. Officials expect it to diversify the economy beyond oil, generate new non-oil revenues, attract foreign investment, and create thousands of jobs across multiple sectors.

By leveraging Iraq’s geographic position between East and West, the project is also expected to strengthen the country’s role as a regional center for transportation, logistics, and international trade.

World.title: Iraq’s non-oil revenues jump to 16%
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Eco Iraq Observatory, which studies economic performance indicators, disclosed on Saturday that non-oil income now accounts for 16 percent of Iraq’s overall financial revenues, the highest percentage recorded so far.

According to a statement released by the observatory, this is the first time that the percentage of non-oil earnings has climbed to 16 percent during the months of May and June, having not exceeded five percent in years.

Eco Iraq noted that the proportion originally grew to roughly 10 percent between May 2020 and October 2022, then remained stable at that level during Mohammed Shia Al-Sudani’s leadership before recently hitting its peak.

The statement highlighted that non-oil revenues are divided into commodity taxes, production fees, general fees, income and wealth taxes, transfer revenues, and other sources.

Iraqi Kurdistan’s income, which it distributes to the federal government in Baghdad, accounts for around 5.5 percent of overall non-oil revenues.

As part of the government’s efforts to diversify the economy and achieve Iraq’s long-term development goals, Mazhar Saleh, the Prime Minister’s Advisor for Financial Affairs, stated in early June that an initiative would be launched. This initiative aims to create an integrated link between enhancing the structure of non-oil revenues within the framework of state finances and diversifying the non-oil GDP.

The Iraqi government established the ambitious goal, referred to as ‘Iraq 2035,’ in May. It includes both public finance reforms and social market economy policies, which aim to facilitate a gradual structural transformation of the national economy, as stated by Saleh.

The vision transforms fiscal policy to ensure that non-oil income accounts for at least 46 percent of total governmental revenues. This will improve budgetary sustainability and reduce the volatility caused by overreliance on oil earnings.

World.title: 'Dharmendra Pradhan Zindabad': Ex-education minister gets rousing welcome in Parliament; oppn fumes
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Resignation may have ended Dharmendra Pradhan's stint as Union education minister, but not his standing within the NDA. Returning to Parliament on Monday, just two days after stepping down over the alleged NEET paper leak controversy, the BJP MP was greeted with chants of "Dharmendra Pradhan zindabad" and a hero's welcome from party colleagues.

The show of solidarity from the ruling alliance triggered sharp criticism from the opposition, with Congress accusing the BJP of glorifying a leader who resigned amid a major examination crisis.

Pradhan arrived at Parliament to chants of "Dharmendra Pradhan zindabad", with BJP and NDA MPs gathering at the Makar Dwar entrance to receive him. Smiling, he folded his hands in a namaste as colleagues escorted him into the Parliament complex.

Several MPs felicitated him with a traditional cap and shawl in a symbolic display of support.

The welcome came just days after Pradhan resigned as Union education minister amid mounting pressure from the CJP-led nationwide protests, which had made accountability for the alleged NEET paper leak and his resignation two of their central demands. On Sunday, Union minister Prahlad Joshi officially assumed charge of the Ministry of Education at Kartavya Bhavan.





At the same time, Opposition MPs led by Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra staged a protest inside the Parliament complex over the alleged use of force against students during the nationwide demonstrations.

Raising slogans of "Shiksha Chori", opposition leaders also demanded that home minister Amit Shah apologise for what they described as police action against peaceful protesters.

The political confrontation unfolded as Parliament prepared to take up the public examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) amendment bill, 2026, which seeks to further strengthen the country's anti-paper leak framework following the examination controversy.

Reacting to the BJP's reception for Pradhan, Congress Rajya Sabha MP Renuka Chowdhury launched a scathing attack on the ruling party. Citing the Bilkis Bano case, she said the gesture was unsurprising and reflected the government's political culture.

"Yes, why not? Isn't this the same government that welcomes the killers and rapists of Bilkis Bano? This is the same Swami ji who used to garland those who raped girls, insulted them in the name of God, and granted them bail.

No, what's the big deal? This is exactly what is expected to happen," she said.

Her remarks referred to the controversy surrounding the 2022 remission granted to 11 men convicted in the Bilkis Bano case, whose release had drawn widespread criticism after visuals emerged showing them being welcomed outside jail.

Pradhan had announced his resignation on Saturday in a post on X, saying, "I have sent my resignation letter to the Prime Minister."

He added, "I am pained to see the events of the past 10 days. This is not a matter of personal prestige for me."

Following the protests over the alleged paper leak, the centre announced a series of measures to overhaul the examination system. On July 23, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the establishment of fast track courts to ensure swift and stringent punishment for those involved in paper leak cases. The government has also constituted a high-powered committee on examination reforms and introduced legislative changes aimed at strengthening safeguards against examination malpractice.

World.title: NEET UG leak case: Delhi court asks CBI to appoint public prosecutor
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The special fast track court at Delhi's Rouse Avenue Courts on Monday directed the director of prosecution to appoint a public prosecutor to represent the State (CBI) in the NEET UG 2026 paper leak case.

The direction came after no one appeared on behalf of the CBI during the hearing.

The court subsequently adjourned the bail pleas of accused Dinesh Biwal and Vikas Biwal to August 3.

Special judge Anu Grover Baliga passed the direction while hearing the bail applications of the two accused before the newly constituted fast track court set up under the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024.

According to news agency ANI, the proceedings marked the first hearing in the NEET UG paper leak case before the designated fast track court.

However, the matter could not proceed after the absence of representation for the CBI. Advocate AP Singh appeared on behalf of the accused.

The fast track court was constituted on July 23 to exclusively try offences under the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, along with connected offences. All pending cases under the Act are to be transferred to the newly designated court.

Earlier, on July 17, the predecessor court had sought the CBI's response to the bail applications filed by Dinesh Biwal and Vikas Biwal.





According to the CBI, Dinesh Biwal and Vikas Biwal are among 13 accused arrested in connection with the alleged leak of the NEET UG question paper before the examination. All the accused are currently in judicial custody till August 6.

The agency alleged that Mangilal Biwal contacted Shubham Khairnar to procure the NEET UG question paper for his son, Vikas Biwal. It further claimed that the leaked question paper was recovered from Mangilal Biwal's mobile phone.

According to the investigation, Mangilal allegedly obtained the paper from Yash Yadav for Rs 10 lakh. During interrogation, Vikas Biwal allegedly told investigators that he had come into contact with Yash Yadav while attending coaching classes in Sikar, Rajasthan.

The CBI further alleged that the leaked paper was circulated through a chain involving Shubham Khairnar, Yash Yadav, Mangilal Biwal, Vikas Biwal and Dinesh Biwal.

Investigators have also alleged that Mangilal subsequently sold the leaked paper to several candidates for Rs 12 lakh each.

An FIR in the case was registered on May 12, 2026, on the complaint of a government official under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the Prevention of Corruption Act and the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024.

The matter will next be taken up on August 3, when the court is expected to hear the bail pleas after the prosecution enters appearance.

World.title: ‘Build new NTA’: Exam body begins major revamp, seeks experts for four senior roles
World.content:
The

(

) has begun a major leadership overhaul as it moves to rebuild its examination framework, strengthen security systems and restore confidence in the country's competitive examination process.

As part of its "Build New NTA" initiative, the testing body has invited applications for four senior leadership roles focused on assessment, operations, cyber security and investigation.

The revamp comes amid months of protests over the alleged NEET paper leak, which led to demands for accountability and the resignation of then education minister Dharmendra Pradhan. The Centre has since announced a series of measures to strengthen examination systems, including the introduction of an anti-paper leak law and the establishment of fast-track courts to hear related cases.

In a LinkedIn post announcing the recruitment drive, the NTA said, "We are hiring for four senior leadership roles. And we are looking for the best India has to offer."

The agency said the initiative was aimed at rebuilding an institution that conducts examinations affecting millions of students every year.

"Every year, more than 1 crore young Indians take a National Testing Agency examination," the NTA said.

It added that the future of candidates depends on the "integrity, fairness and quality" of its examination process, as the results influence their education, careers and future opportunities.





Emphasising the need for reform, the agency wrote, "It is a responsibility we take very seriously. And it is a responsibility we are rebuilding NTA to be worthy of."

The NTA said the restructuring exercise follows the recommendations of the High-Level Committee of Experts (HLCE), chaired by K Radhakrishnan.

It added, "Across academic rigour, technology, security, operations and governance, we are rebuilding the Agency to serve crores of candidates with the credibility they deserve."

As part of the overhaul, the NTA is seeking candidates for four senior positions:

General Manager, Assessment R&D and Psychometrics

General Manager, Test Centre Network & Operations

General Manager, Information Security (Chief Information Security Officer)

General Manager, Vigilance, Investigation & Forensics

The agency said the vigilance and forensics head would oversee investigations into examination malpractice, coordinate with agencies including the CBI, IB, ED and state police, and operate under the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024.

The NTA conducts several major entrance examinations, including Neet, Jee and Cuet.

Highlighting the broader purpose of the reforms, the NTA said, "The candidates who write NTA examinations are the future of India. They are the engineers who will build our infrastructure, the doctors who will care for our people, the teachers who will educate the next generation, and the researchers who will drive our discovery."

The agency has also invited applications for Young Professionals through the UPSC's Pratibha Setu portal, with 12 positions in Academic Research, two in Legal Research and two in Finance & Accounts Research.

According to the NTA, applications for the senior leadership positions can be submitted by email to dir-admin@nta.gov.in, with the deadline set at 30 days from July 25, 2026.

The recruitment drive notification comes as Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced a high-powered committee headed by Nandan Nilekani to recommend measures for leak-proof and technology-driven examinations.

Later, home minister Amit Shah said on X, "The Modi govt follows the principle of constant reform to safeguard the future of our new generation."

Shah added, "We will impose exemplary punishment on the culprits of paper leak and ensure that no one ever dares to commit this crime."

World.title: 'Agitation does not mean lathicharge': SC on police action against students protesting paper leak
World.content:
CJI said the Constitution guarantees the right to peaceful protest.

Poll Vote & Share your view Should there be a uniform nationwide protocol for peaceful protests? Strongly agree Disagree 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday said the right to peaceful protest is constitutionally guaranteed and that the mere existence of an agitation cannot justify alleged police excesses against demonstrators.A bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant made the observations while hearing pleas alleging police excesses against students during the July 20 protests over the NEET paper leak.The bench also indicated that a uniform nationwide protocol was needed to facilitate peaceful protests while enabling authorities to act against anti-social elements."Right to peaceful protests is in the Constitution. Right to peaceful protest is absolutely guaranteed. That cannot be denied. Merely because there is agitation cannot justify police excess," the CJI observed.Emphasising the need to protect both protesters and law enforcement personnel, the bench said, "Agitation does not mean lathicharge. Also, agitation does not mean violence."The court said pan-India guidelines should be framed on the issue without either the petitioners or governments adopting an adversarial approach.The bench, however, also expressed concern over allegations of attacks on police personnel during protests.When a lawyer referred to injuries suffered by police personnel and alleged attacks on their families by an unruly mob, Justice Joymalya Bagchi said, "Injury to police is of equal concern. We may call upon the State to respond why adequate safeguards were not providedâ¦"The CJI said there should be a clear protocol governing peaceful protests across the country, including the provision of designated spaces for demonstrations."There should be a protocol when someone wants to agitate peacefully. Proper space for that. There is no impediment in that regard. But if there is any anti-social element that can be dealt with," the CJI said.The court observed that the matter required an all-India approach and indicated that mandatory guidelines could be evolved to ensure uniformity."Itâs a question of all Indiaâ¦ this uniformity in protocol is alsoâ¦ Self-discipline is integral to the entire process," the CJI observed.The matter has been listed for further hearing on Tuesday.

World.title: 'Former minister will be exposed': Vijay-led Tamil Nadu govt on DMK 'corruption' audit report
World.content:
Tamil Nadu finance minister N Marie Wilson (PTI file photo)

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu finance minister N Marie Wilson on Sunday said the state government will table an "audit report on corruption" during the upcoming Budget session, alleging that it will expose irregularities in the collection of "party funds" during the previous MK Stalin-led DMK regime.The Vijay-led cabinet's minister made the remarks while addressing an event in Chennai's Harbour Assembly constituency, taking a swipe at the opposition DMK over what he described as attempts to feign ignorance regarding the alleged irregularities. Though he did not name anyone directly, Wilson appeared to target former DMK minister and current Harbour MLA PK Sekar Babu."The former minister who currently represents this constituency now is feigning ignorance about the party funds collected during the DMK rule. He has asked 'what is party funds?' I am constrained to react, since I am addressing my first event in Harbour constituency. We are preparing an audit report on corruption made under the pretext of raising party funds during the previous DMK rule. It will be presented in the upcoming Budget session," Wilson said.In another apparent reference to Sekar Babu, the finance minister added, "It will contain a list of corruption made.Then, this former minister will be exposed."Speaking at the same event, Wilson also reiterated the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government's commitment to abolishing the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET). He claimed that just as Tamil Nadu witnessed a major political shift in 2026 with the TVK coming to power, a similar change would take place at the national level after the 2029 Lok Sabha elections."There will be a permanent solution for the NEET exam. Our party (TVK) leadership is actively working on a plan to ensure that this exam will be completely abolished. This change will be visible across India," he said while addressing a function organised to distribute commendation certificates to Class 10 and Class 12 students.When asked by reporters to elaborate on the proposed audit report, Wilson declined to share further details, saying, "wait and watch," and indicated that chief minister Vijay would make an announcement on the matter.The first Budget of the Vijay-led TVK government will be presented in the Tamil Nadu assembly on August 5 by Wilson. The assembly's Business Advisory Committee will meet the same day to decide the duration of the Budget session.

World.title: DMK demands immediate NEET ban, seeks probe into Jantar Mantar violence
World.content:
NEW DELHI: MK Stalin-led DMK has demanded an immediate ban on the nationwide medical entrance examination NEET.

DMK MP TR Baalu on Monday submitted an adjournment motion notice in the Lok Sabha, seeking a ban on NEET in ongoing Monsoon Session.

The demand comes in the wake of the NEET UG paper leak in May, which triggered nationwide outrage and over a month of student protests that eventually led to the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

The DMK also demanded an inquiry into the alleged indiscriminate use of lethal weapons against protesting students at New Delhi's Jantar Mantar.

On the same day as Pradhan's resignation, the PM Modi-led Centre appointed Pralhad Joshi as the new Union education minister.

Pradhan's resignation, however, helped calm the protests after the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which had been leading the agitation, appealed to protesters to return home, saying their primary demand had been met following a meeting with Union ministers Jagat Prakash Nadda and Jitendra Singh.

World.title: US FDA nod for 1st pill to replace jabs to fight high cholesterol
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Patients with difficult-to-control high cholesterol could soon have an oral alternative to cholesterol-lowering injections after US Food and Drug Administration approved the world's first oral PCSK9 inhibitor, a class of medicines that dramatically lowers "bad" cholesterol.

The tablet, Lipfendra, has been approved for adults with high cholesterol, including those with an inherited condition called heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia.

However, the drug is not expected to be available in India immediately. "Even if a medicine is approved abroad, it cannot be marketed in India automatically... it must obtain approval from CDSCO... which may include clinical trials as required under Indian regulations," said Dr Subhash Mandal, national general secretary, Indian Pharmaceutical Association.

The approval is significant because many high-risk patients continue to have elevated low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol despite treatment with standard oral medicines.

Clinical trials involving 3,207 adults found the once-daily oral drug reduced LDL cholesterol by 56-59% over 24 weeks in patients already on maximally tolerated statins, delivering reductions comparable to injectable PCSK9 inhibitors and offering another option for those whose cholesterol remains uncontrolled despite existing therapy.





However, cardiologists said that the drug is unlikely to become a first-line treatment.

"The new oral therapy lowers LDL... by about 50-60%, making it a promising option for patients who prefer to avoid injections," said Dr Ambuj Roy, Professor of Cardiology at AIIMS Delhi.

World.title: At no point did government stop students from protesting: Nirmala Sitharaman
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Government did not stop students from protesting at any point in time, while at the same time, it was gearing up to conduct the NEET re-examination in time and punish the culprits who had engaged in paper leaks, finance minister

said.

"Permission was given when they came, as soon as Dipke landed. We didn't try at any point in time to stop the protest at all. When things didn't go right at the first time when the exams were held and leak became public, and it had to be acted upon, soon the govt arrested those who had bought and sold the papers. It was the responsibility of the govt to arrest them and put into the judicial process... but equally important was that the re-examination happens in time, so that one whole year does not get affected," Sitharaman said on why the govt took long to respond to the students' protest.

She stressed it was after the successful re-examination that education minister Dharmendra Pradhan took the "wise" decision to resign. "If he hadn't done that (the re-examination process), it would have been irresponsible of everybody in the system," she said.

Besides, she said, India faced the risk of inflation from both external and internal factors. "...this year, there is El Nino. The catchment areas are not receiving adequate rains. So, water for irrigation and drinking is going to pose a challenge. So, inflation cannot be just imported. It is also our own," she said.

World.title: Parliament Monsoon Session Day 6 LIVE: Discussion on anti-paper leak Bill set for 5 p.m. in Lok Sabha
World.content:
Union Minister Jitendra Singh introduced the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, in the Lok Sabha on Monday (July 27, 2026). The Bill has strong penal provisions to deal with any case of paper leaks.

The Bill significantly toughens the penalties established under the 2024 Act, introduces mandatory two-month investigation deadlines, along with designated Special Fast Track Courts, and steep financial penalties reaching up to ₹10 crore for organised crime networks.

Also read | Parliament monsoon session day 5 highlights

Opposition parties protested on Monday (July 27, 2026) outside Parliament on the use of brute force on protestors during Parliament March on July 20, adding that they will continue to raise their demand for accountability from the Union Home Minister over the incident.

World.title: Supreme Court seeks Centre's reply on Kapil Sibal's plea on interpretation of anti-defection law
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Monday (July 27, 2026) agreed to hear a plea filed by independent Rajya Sabha MP and senior advocate Kapil Sibal seeking reconsideration of the interpretation of the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution that allows MLAs and MPs to avoid disqualification under the anti-defection law by claiming a merger with another political party.

A Bench of Justices P.S. Narasimha and Alok Aradhe, which issued a notice to the Centre, observed that there are several issues involved that are required to be taken by Parliament.

Mr. Sibal said that this issue has "huge repercussions on our polity" as a minority party can become a majority. In contrast, a majority can become a minority due to the provision.

The Bench said that the Tenth Schedule, meant for the lawmakers, was passed by the Parliament, and it is for them to devise a mechanism.

Mr. Sibal said there is a similar matter related to the defection of MLAs from Goa pending before the court. The Bench then tagged the plea along with the Goa matter.

Mr. Sibal has filed the plea in his personal capacity and sought interpretation of the law. On July 22, he had sought an urgent listing of his plea, saying it relates to the issue of whether the composition of Parliament can change in the manner in which it is happening in this country, and to the interpretation of the Tenth Schedule, paragraph four, in that context.

The plea comes against the backdrop of MPs from AAP, Trinamool Congress and the Shiv Sena (UBT) joining the ruling BJP and other political parties by invoking the merger provisions under the Tenth Schedule.

World.title: Congress MPs protest in Parliament complex over alleged 'police brutality' against student protesters, seek Home Minister Amit Shah's apology
World.content:
Congress MPs, led by party general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, protested in the Parliament House complex on Monday (July 27, 2026), over alleged ‘police brutality’ against student protesters during the agitation on the NEET paper leak issue and demanded Home Minister Amit Shah's apology.

Carrying placards and a large banner, the Congress MPs protested in front of the steps of the Makar Dwar of Parliament. They raised slogans, demanding answers from the Home Minister over alleged police excesses against protesting students.

The Congress-led opposition is set to keep the pressure on the government in Parliament over the issue, demanding action against those responsible for the assault on students and an apology from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Mr. Shah.

Leader of the Opposition (LoP) in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has written to Mr. Shah, seeking accountability for what he called ‘barbaric assault’ on peacefully protesting students and asking the Minister whether he approved the use of ‘lethal force’, including pellet guns.

In his letter, Mr. Gandhi said peaceful protest is crucial to any democracy and that it is the government's responsibility to protect protesters and resolve their grievances through dialogue.

"Such brutal violence destroys every norm, and has outraged the country. Youth and students, the future of our country, are demanding answers and accountability. Their voice will be heard," the former Congress Chief has said.

World.title: Two traffic police personnel caught on camera taking bribes in Bengaluru
World.content:
Two separate incidents of Bengaluru Traffic Police personnel allegedly accepting bribes were caught on camera on Saturday, raising fresh concerns about corruption during traffic enforcement.

A traffic head constable, identified as Somashekhar of the Pulakeshinagar Traffic Police Station, has been suspended after allegedly accepting a ₹5,000 bribe from a truck driver.

According to the suspension order issued by Bengaluru East Traffic Deputy Commissioner of Police Sahil Bagla, Somashekhar allegedly demanded money from truck driver Syed Afroz, who was transporting an iron-laden lorry during a vehicle inspection.

The head constable was accused of threatening the driver that a formal case would lead to court proceedings and a fine unless he paid the bribe. The truck driver reportedly recorded the transaction on his mobile phone and submitted the video to senior police officials. Following a preliminary inquiry, the head constable was suspended on charges of misconduct and accepting illegal gratification.

In another incident, a traffic assistant sub-inspector attached to the Peenya Traffic Police Station was allegedly seen accepting ₹200 from a motorist at 8th Mile. According to the allegation, the police had stopped the rider during a vehicle check and reportedly told him he would let him go if he paid ₹200. Residents recorded the exchange on their mobile phones. In the video, the motorist is heard saying, “I paid ₹200 and they let me go.” The video has since surfaced on social media, prompting public criticism.

While body worn cameras are mandatory for traffic police personnel in the city, in both these incidents, it is learnt that the accused policemen allegedly failed to comply with the directive.

World.title: Former Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah announces retirement from electoral politics, citing age and ‘polluted’ politics
World.content:
Former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah has announced his retirement from electoral politics, while asserting that he will continue to remain active in public life and work for the Congress and the people.

Addressing a gathering during the 86th birth anniversary celebrations of former Speaker, the late ‘K.R. Pet’ Krishna, at K.R. Pet town in Mandya district on Saturday, the veteran Congress leader said he would not contest the 2028 Assembly elections.

The announcement came after supporters urged him to remain in electoral politics for another decade. Mr. Siddaramaiah, who represents the Varuna Assembly constituency, categorically stated that he would not seek re-election in 2028.

His remarks prompted many in the audience to appeal to him to reconsider the decision. The announcement also disappointed many of his supporters and loyalists in the Congress, several of whom want the 79-year-old leader to continue in active electoral politics.

Mr. Siddaramaiah, Karnataka’s longest-serving Chief Minister after surpassing the record of D. Devaraj Urs, reiterated that he would remain active in politics despite stepping away from electoral contests.

After demitting office as Chief Minister this May to make way for D.K. Shivakumar, Mr. Siddaramaiah had said he would continue serving the people and undertake any responsibility assigned by the Congress high command.

He had also declined the party’s reported offer of a Rajya Sabha seat, saying he was not interested in national politics.

‘Polluted’ and honest politics’

After his announcement in KR Pet, in a Facebook post, Mr. Siddaramaiah said the changing nature of politics had influenced his decision. “Politics has become polluted. Therefore, I have decided not to contest the 2028 Assembly elections. However, I will remain active in politics, stay with the people and continue to support them,” he said.

Recalling his political journey, Mr. Siddaramaiah said he entered public life in 1978 as a member of the Taluk Board and would complete 50 years in politics in 2028. “I have witnessed both victory and defeat, but I have never compromised on my ideology or betrayed my conscience. That gives me immense satisfaction,” he said.

Expressing concern over the present political nature, he said honest politics had become increasingly difficult. “There was a time when people voluntarily contributed money to help me contest elections. Today, the situation has changed, wherein money has to be given to people if one contests elections. There is no scope for honest politics. Considering this reality, along with my age and health, I have decided not to contest elections,” he said.

Mr. Siddaramaiah said he would be around 80 or 81 years of age when the next Assembly term begins and acknowledged that advancing age and health considerations would limit his ability to work with the same energy.

Thanking the people of Karnataka for their unwavering support over the past five decades, he said, “The people of Karnataka have treated me as one among them and showered me with love and affection. I remain indebted to them and will continue to work for their welfare.”

World.title: Marriage brings discipline, reality of live-in relationships can be seen across world: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat
World.content:
Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat on Sunday (July 26, 2026) said marriage is a discipline which instils dharma, while the reality of live-in relationships can be seen all over the world.

Speaking at an event on 'contemporary motherhood' organised by Vishwa Mangalya Sabha in Hyderabad, he also said Gen Z is imitative, emotional and does not think with a calm mind, and what comes across to them as genuine appeals.

"Marriage is a discipline which instils dharma. Its alternative is live-in relationship. Modernity. What are its consequences? We don't want responsibilities but happiness. Stay together when it is wanted and part ways when not wanted. No responsibilities. What will grow with it? What is growing, look around the world," he said.

He, however, said modernity is also needed and changing with times is also a rule in the country's traditions.

In an apparent reference to live-in relationships, he said it is degradation and blind imitation of Western culture, while modernity is welcome.

The RSS chief also said LGBTQ is a part of our society and that they should not be looked down upon.

Mr. Bhagwat favoured following mobile phone discipline by parents and stressed the importance of conversation among family members to answer the questions of new generation children and to address various family-related issues.

World.title: Three missing girls traced in Chhattisgarh after week-long search by Hyderabad Police
World.content:
Three minor girls, who went missing from their home in Domalguda in Hyderabad on July 19, were traced safely in Chhattisgarh after a week-long search involving the scrutiny of 262 CCTV cameras and technical surveillance, the city police said.

The girls, aged 17, 16 and 15, had left their residence in Fareed Basti during the early hours of July 19. Their family, which had migrated from Chhattisgarh to Hyderabad in May this year for livelihood, lodged a missing complaint after frantic searches failed to locate them.

The police registered a case under Section 137(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and formed four special teams comprising personnel from the Domalguda police station and the Secunderabad Task Force.

Investigators reconstructed the girls’ journey through CCTV footage. The police said the trio left their house at 1.47 a.m., travelled by autorickshaw to Kachiguda Railway Station, then proceeded to Secunderabad Railway Station. After spending several hours moving between the railway station and James Street, they boarded the Dhanapur Express from Secunderabad at around 9 a.m. and reached Nagpur the following evening.

From Nagpur, the girls travelled by bus to Gadchiroli and later to Patanjur village, where they stayed for two days at the house of a person identified as Biswajith.

Acting on technical evidence and other investigative leads, a Hyderabad police team, assisted by personnel from Kanker police station in Chhattisgarh, traced and safely rescued the three girls.

During questioning, the girls told the police that they had left home voluntarily after being scolded by their parents. The search was carried out under the supervision of senior officers, with personnel from the Domalguda police station and the Secunderabad Task Force;s participation.

World.title: Plea against Internet shutdown around Jantar Mantar withdrawn from Delhi High Court
World.content:
Legal services organisation Software Freedom Law Centre, India, on Monday (July 27, 2026), withdrew from the Delhi High Court its PIL against the suspension of mobile Internet services in parts of central Delhi, with services restored following the withdrawal of the Cockroach Janata Party's (CJP’s) stir.

"The counsel for the petitioner says he has instructions to withdraw the petition. The petition is dismissed as withdrawn," said a Bench of Chief Justice D.K. Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia.

In its petition, Software Freedom Law Centre, India (SFLC.In), sought quashing of orders issued by the Union Ministry of Home Affairs on July 17, 20, 22 and 23 to shut down mobile Internet services in parts of central Delhi.

The CJP had been protesting in the heart of Delhi at Jantar Mantar since June 20 to seek accountability from the government over the NEET paper leak and the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union Education Minister.

The over-a-month-long agitation was called off after Mr. Pradhan stepped down on Saturday (July 25, 2026), and other demands of the CJP were accepted by the government. Soon after, Internet services were restored in central Delhi.

SLFC.In said in its petition that the temporary suspension of telecommunication services, including mobile Internet services, was ‘one of the most extraordinary coercive powers conferred upon the Executive’ as it interfered with the exercise of freedoms guaranteed under Articles 19(1)(a) (free speech), 19(1)(b) (peaceful assembly), 19(1)(g) (right to practice any trade or profession) and 21 (right to life and liberty) of the Constitution.

Terming the suspension orders ‘illegal, arbitrary and unconstitutional’, the petitioner said they neither disclosed any public emergency nor provided reasons to demonstrate why a blanket suspension of mobile Internet services was necessary or proportionate to any alleged threat.

The plea underscored that the authorities invoked Section 20(2)(b) of the Telecom Act read with the Suspension Rules, 2024, to record that the suspension was necessary ‘in the interest of public safety and averting public emergency’ but failed to consider ‘less restrictive alternatives’ before imposing a blanket suspension of mobile Internet services.

It further alleged that the suspension orders did not disclose an ‘apparent independent application of mind’ and ‘reflect a mechanical exercise of statutory power inconsistent with the requirements of administrative law.’

"The present challenge arises from the Impugned Orders issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs directing suspension of all mobile Internet technologies within a radius of approximately 1.5 kilometres from Jantar Mantar, New Delhi," the plea said.

"The repeated issuance of six separate suspension orders over a span of seven days further underscores the necessity of examining whether each exercise of statutory power was independently undertaken in accordance with Section 20(2)(b)," it said.

World.title: AICTE Scholarship 2026-27: Medical students to get up to Rs 3 lakh, Diploma holders Rs 1.25 lakh
World.content:
The All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) has activated the portal for the submission of online applications for the Special Scholarship Scheme for the Students of Union Territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh (SSSJKL). Students who have passed their intermediate, i.e. Class 12 and Engineering Diploma Holders can now apply to avail this scholarship at the online portal designed by AICTE especially for the Special Scholarship Scheme (PM USPY) – aicte-jk-scholarship-gov.in.

The registration process for Class 12 and engineering diploma students is scheduled to close today. The council started accepting online applications for this scholarship under the Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan (PM-USP) Yojana for the academic year 2026-27 from July 16 for Class 12 and July 17 for diploma students. Registered candidates are also instructed to visit the nearest Facilitation-cum-Document Verification Centres (FDVCs) before July 30.

World.title: Mumbai model Rhiya Ahir, who stopped police van with bare hands, alleges online ‘slut-shaming’, bullying; files complaint
World.content:
Rhiya Ahir, the 27-year-old Mumbai model who stood in front of a police van escorting detained Shivaji Park protesters, has approached the Mumbai Police, alleging sustained harassment, bullying, ‘slut-shaming’ and defamation on social media after images and videos went viral.

One of the defining faces of the Shivaji Park protest, Rhiya Ahir also alleged in her complaint that she has been ‘slut-shamed’ and fears it could affect her real life, her family’s safety and reputation.



In her complaint, Rhiya Ahir has accused several social media content creators of falsely claiming that she produces and sells adult content through her social media accounts.

World.title: Deep depression over Odisha-West Bengal coasts, IMD warns of ‘extreme’ rain today
World.content:
Odisha’s wettest locality on Sunday was Jagatsinghpur, where the 24-hour rainfall recorded was 330 mm. (File photo for representative use)

A deep depression has formed off the north Odisha-West Bengal coast, and it will bring ‘extremely’ heavy rainfall (over 200 mm in 24 hours) over many parts of Odisha on Monday, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has warned.

The Met office has forecast that heavy rain is also expected to affect West Bengal on Monday and Tuesday, with overall wet conditions likely to continue till July 30 over the Gangetic West Bengal, Jharkhand, Bihar, and Chhattisgarh along with the eastern and western regions of both Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.

Odisha’s wettest locality on Sunday remained Jagatsinghpur, where the 24-hour rainfall recorded was 330 mm. Similar rainfall is expected on Monday, too, the Met office has warned.

World.title: Shaheer Sheikh was overwhelmed playing Arjun in Mahabharata: ‘Locked myself in bathroom’
World.content:
Actor Shaheer Sheikh, who was recently seen in the web series Ab Hoga Hisaab, has been a celebrated name on Indian television. While he has dabbled in films and the OTT space, the actor still feels he exists in survival mode. During a conversation with Digital Commentary, Shaheer opened up about the challenges he continues to face despite his popularity. The actor also recalled the time he played Arjun in Mahabharata and the impact the role had on his life.

During a recent podcast, Shaheer was asked if he has gotten out of survival mode and now leads a luxurious life. The actor said, “I am still in survival mode only; it is not like I have arrived; hard work is still going on. Being in survival mode, in today’s time when there is so much competition, is important. You have to be on your toes; there is excitement in that because you don’t know what will happen next. You have to be prepared for anything.”

Also Read: People generally call me moody: Shaheer Sheikh

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Shaheer Sheikh (@shaheernsheikh)

Later, discussing how actors at times see success with a character or show, and that transforms their lifestyle; however, once they drop out of that show, how do they sustain their lifestyle? Shaheer added, “You think we are not surviving that way now? Tough situations keep coming, but I try not to get into such situations. I don’t get used to a certain lifestyle; I keep giving myself a reality check. I can survive on bare minimum or even nothing. I have trained myself. Luxuries are far-fetched; if I don’t have the basic requirements, I will work for it every day. Everyone has a different journey. Very recently, I was out of work for 1 to 2 years, and I was forced to… sometimes you are forced to do work that you don’t want to.”

Shaheer on playing Arjun in Mahabharata

Looking back at one of his iconic roles on television, Arjun spoke about his character in Mahabharata. He said, “I was very scared playing the role of Arjun in Mahabharata. It was the first time that we had prepped for a year and a half for a show. Producers were researching and writing before that. It took 4 years for the show to start; it was a huge responsibility, and I couldn’t go wrong. Despite being ready, I was extremely nervous.”

He also recalled, “On the launch day, the producer had kept a party; seeing people’s response, I got so overwhelmed that I locked myself in the bathroom. I couldn’t control myself and got very emotional. The producer spoke to me for 15-20 minutes and calmed me down. That’s the kind of effect the show had on me. I was very nervous at that time. Sometimes after giving your 100 percent, you are not sure how people will react to this, so it was a huge responsibility. That character gave me a lot and left a major impact on my belief system.”

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Shaheer Sheikh (@shaheernsheikh)

Talking about his struggles, back in 2021, Shaheer had told Zoom how he faced financial struggles before signing Mahabharata. He said, “Of course, there was a big gap between Navya and Mahabharat when I had switched to photography. I started doing photography; I used to do folios for my friends because there were few projects which were getting delayed. There was almost a one-year span where I was only doing auditions and roaming around.”

Back in 2018, Shaheer had told SCREEN how he never aimed to become a star. “Being famous is not my aim. I don’t want to become a superstar. Television helps me reach out to so many people and entertain them every single day. I think as an actor, that’s a bigger responsibility. I really feel lucky to be a part of this industry,” he had said.

On the work front, ahead of Ab Hoga Hisaab, Shaheer was seen in Do Patti alongside Kriti Sanon and Kajol. He has been a part of popular shows like Kya Mast Hai Life, Navya, and Kuch Rang Pyaar Ke Aise Bhi.

World.title: ‘Our kids will spread the word’: Delhi transporters turn to Gen Z for E20 fuel protest
World.content:
To build momentum for their August 4 protest march to Parliament against ethanol-blended petrol, Delhi’s transporters are turning to an unlikely ally: Gen Z. They plan to enlist their children to create reels, amplify their message on social media, and rally support among young transporters and taxi drivers for the agitation.



Sanjay Samrat, president of the Delhi Taxi Tourist Transporters and Tour Operators Association, said the idea emerged after the student-led protests at Jantar Mantar against the NEET paper leak.

“After the students’ protest (at Jantar Mantar), we saw the support they mobilised through the internet. Many of us transporters are old and not tech-savvy… I don’t know how to use Instagram and post videos online. So, we decided to ask our children to spread the word among young transporters and drivers active on social media,” Samrat said.

World.title: At least 5 years in jail, Rs 50 lakh fine: New anti-paper leak law highlights
World.content:
The Bill to amend the anti-paper leaks law, which the government introduced in Lok Sabha on Monday in the aftermath of nationwide student protests, provides for a 10-year jail term and a Rs 50 lakh fine for people convicted of involvement in such leaks. Jitendra Singh, Minister of State for the Prime Minister’s Office, introduced the Bill in Lok Sabha as Opposition MPs demanded the government’s response to questions on alleged excesses during the crackdown on protesters during the July 20 march to Parliament. The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which led the protests against paper leaks, has scored a big win with Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan stepping down on Saturday.

What the revised law says

The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, amends the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024. The new legislation sets a two-month deadline to complete the investigation into paper leak cases. It has increased the punishment for individuals involved in unfair means, including paper leaks, from three to five years in the 2024 Act to five to 10 years. The fine, earlier set at Rs 10 lakh, has been hiked to Rs 50 lakh. If the crime is found to be organised, the Bill proposes a minimum sentence of seven years and a fine of up to Rs 10 crore. In the draft legislation, 15 illegal acts, including leaking question papers, tampering with OMR sheets, creating fake websites and issuing fake admit cards, have been listed as offences.

According to the Bill, states and Union Territories will be empowered to set up fast-track courts that can complete the trial within three months of filing of the chargesheet. The Centre, it says, will be empowered to set up a special task force to probe some paper leak cases.

Opposition leaders protested inside and outside the House on Monday. PTI Opposition leaders protested inside and outside the House on Monday. PTI

Bill tabled amid chaos

The Bill was tabled amid chaos in the House as Opposition members raised slogans against the alleged excesses during the crackdown against protesters in the Delhi protest. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla asked the members to participate in the discussion. “It is the first step towards improving the public examination process. Instead of sloganeering, you should discuss the Bill in the House. The government will try and incorporate the improvements suggested by you,” he said. When the Opposition continued to protest, the Speaker adjourned the House till 2 pm. When the House met again, the protests continued, and proceedings were adjourned till 5 pm.

The first week of the Monsoon Session, which began on July 20, was washed out amid nationwide protests demanding Pradhan’s resignation. The Opposition joined voices with the protesters at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar and elsewhere to demand the minister’s exit. Eventually, Pradhan stepped down on Saturday. The Opposition has now shifted its focus to Union Home Minister Amit Shah, who controls Delhi Police, on the alleged excesses, such as use of pellet guns, in the crackdown against protesters.

The government, pushed onto the backfoot, has also announced the formation of a task force led by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani to suggest reforms to make the public exam system leakproof.

World.title: Asked not to take video of CPR treatment, patient’s son assaults doctor at Sassoon hospital
World.content:
A doctor at the Sassoon General Hospital was assaulted allegedly by the son of a patient, who was later booked by the police.

According to police, the incident happened when the doctor asked the accused not to record the video of cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) treatment. Police said the patient died of a heart attack.

An FIR in this case was registered at the Bundgarden police station on Saturday.

Police said the accused, a 30-year-old man from Ghorpadi, brought his father who suffered cardiac arrest to the government-run Sassoon General Hospital for treatment on Saturday.

Police said the patient was taken to the emergency ward. In an attempt to save the patient, when the trainee doctor at the hospital was giving him CPR, the accused started recording a video of the procedure on his cell phone.
